confirmed.title: groupmember has no index on profile_id/role_id, yet every access-control and learner path filters on it
confirmed.location: packages/db/src/schema.ts:1287-1323 (only unique(group_id,profile_id) variants); queries/allocation/allocation.ts:129-204 (isCourseTutorForLearner, isTutorAllocatedToCourse, listAllocatedLearnerIdsForCourse); queries/caseload/dashboard.ts:19-84; queries/coursework/grid.ts:33-51; queries/comms/announcement.ts:57-70; queries/course/course.ts:956-1075; queries/dash/dash.ts:40,72-90; queries/exercise/lms.ts:55-65
confirmed.current: groupmember's only indexes are PK and three UNIQUE constraints that all lead with group_id. Hot queries start from the other side: WHERE profile_id = ? AND role_id = 3, or tutor_allocation.learner_id -> groupmember.profile_id JOINs (tutor course-open guard, tutor caseload courses/enrolments, submissions grid, learner announcements feed, getEnrolledCourses, getLMSExercises, tutor-course lists). With no profile_id index the planner seq-scans groupmember (one row per learner per course) or hash-joins the whole table on each call.
confirmed.breaks_at: Roughly 20-50k groupmember rows (a few thousand learners x several courses): each tutor course-open, progression and caseload render scans the whole table. These run per page view and per heartbeat-adjacent request, so p95 climbs and the 10-connection pool queues. The tutors-see-only-allocated-learners guards (isTutorAllocatedToCourse, listAllocatedLearnerIdsForCourse) are the slowest hit.
confirmed.fix: Add CREATE INDEX groupmember_profile_role_idx ON groupmember (profile_id, role_id) INCLUDE (group_id, created_at); also CREATE INDEX groupmember_group_role_idx ON groupmember (group_id, role_id) INCLUDE (profile_id) for per-course student lists/counts (admin-overview getOrgCoursesWithEnrolment, course/people, dash_org_stats view). Declare both in schema.ts and build with CONCURRENTLY (see migration-safety finding). Semantics are unchanged: indexes only.
confirmed.flow_risk: No behaviour change, so admin, tutor, learner and manager flows are unaffected. The only risk is the lock taken during a non-concurrent build, which blocks enrolment writes briefly. Do not drop unique_group_profile, because the enrolment race protection depends on it.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: schema.ts:1287-1323 has no index leading with profile_id/role_id (only the 3 uniques leading group_id). isCourseTutorForLearner (allocation.ts:22-31) filters tut.profile_id+role_id and stu.profile_id with no group_id predicate, so it must scan groupmember. The tutor_allocation to groupmember joins (lines 72,91) also join only on profile_id+role_id. profile_id FK (no ON DELETE) means a profile delete also scans groupmember. But two claims are overstated. (a) isTutorAllocatedToCourse and listAllocatedLearnerIdsForCourse have course.id = const, so the planner can start from course -> group_id -> groupmember via unique(group_id, ...), bounded by that course's members, so they are not the 'slowest hit'. (b) getEnrolledCourses (course.ts:956+) joins groupmember ON group_id = group.id AND profile_id = ?, which is already served by unique_group_profile, so it is not helped by the new index. A seq scan of 20-50k narrow rows costs a few ms, not seconds. 'critical' is too high; 'high' is right because the guards run per request.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Keep the index (profile_id, role_id) INCLUDE (group_id). INCLUDE created_at is unnecessary. (group_id, role_id) INCLUDE (profile_id) is useful for per-course role counts. Drop getEnrolledCourses and isTutorAllocatedToCourse from the 'benefits' list. Never drop unique_group_profile. Build it per the migration-safety process.

confirmed.title: Migrations auto-run inside the API container entrypoint in one transaction; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot be used and a failure crash-loops the API
confirmed.location: docs/REPLICATION.md:3562 and docker/entrypoint-api.sh (db:setup -> drizzle-kit migrate); packages/db/drizzle.config.ts; packages/db/src/migrations/*.sql (all plain CREATE INDEX, e.g. 0011:42-46, 0026:19-23)
confirmed.current: Every API container start runs drizzle-kit migrate over the 5432 session pooler. drizzle applies pending migrations in a single transaction, so CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY errors there. All existing index migrations are plain CREATE INDEX, which takes a SHARE lock that blocks writes to the table for the build. A failed migration (for example a unique index over duplicate rows) exits the container and the API crash-loops, which takes the whole site down. The deploy already builds images on the droplet for 20-45 minutes, so rollback is slow.
confirmed.breaks_at: Not a problem at today's table sizes. Once session, coursework_submission, message, notification and groupmember hold hundreds of thousands of rows, a plain index build blocks writes for seconds to minutes (learner heartbeats and submissions fail). A unique-index migration on a table with duplicates takes the API down.
confirmed.fix: Ship every new index in two steps. (1) Run the DDL by hand beforehand (psql or Supabase SQL, session pooler or direct): CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS <name> ..., one statement per call and outside any transaction, with SET lock_timeout='5s'. (2) Commit the matching drizzle migration written as CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (a no-op in prod) so the journal and schema.ts stay in sync. For UNIQUE indexes, run a duplicate-detection SELECT first and dedupe, then CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. Add a pre-deploy checklist step and set statement_timeout/lock_timeout for the migrator connection. Optionally add MIGRATE_ON_BOOT=false so schema changes are applied by a one-shot job, not by the serving container.
confirmed.flow_risk: Process change only. Run (1) before deploying code that depends on the index. A half-built INVALID index left by a cancelled CONCURRENTLY build must be dropped before retrying (check pg_index.indisvalid). IF NOT EXISTS makes the committed migration idempotent on fresh databases.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: entrypoint-api.sh runs db:setup on every start; db-setup.ts runs drizzle-kit migrate (drizzle's migrator wraps pending migrations in one transaction, so CONCURRENTLY cannot work). All existing index migrations are plain CREATE INDEX (0011:42-46). On failure db-setup does process.exit(1), and the compose service has restart: unless-stopped, so the API crash-loops. A pg_advisory_lock already serialises concurrent startups (db-setup.ts:96-110), which the finding does not mention. Impact is a process risk, not a scale bug. Plain index builds on tables under ~100k rows take well under a second, so 'high' is overstated.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The hand-run CONCURRENTLY + committed CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS pattern is sound. The index name must match schema.ts exactly so drizzle-kit generate shows no diff. Hand-run SQL is not tracked in the drizzle journal, so keep a checklist. SKIP_DB_SETUP=true (already supported) plus a one-shot migrate step is a simpler way to get MIGRATE_ON_BOOT=false than new code. A unique-index migration must have its duplicate check run first.

confirmed.title: session/account/verification have no indexes beyond PK+token, are never purged, and session carries a write per tab per minute
confirmed.location: packages/db/src/schema.ts:113-167; queries/analytics/analytics.ts:45-122 (getLastLogin/getLastSeenForUserIds filter session.user_id); queries/dash/admin-overview.ts:309-340 (getOnlineOrgMembers filters session.updated_at); queries/organization/users.ts:97-108; apps/api/src/routes/account/account.ts:111-123 (/heartbeat); apps/dashboard/src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte:32-40 (60s ping); apps/jobs/src/workers/maintenance.ts (no session/verification purge)
confirmed.current: session has only PK and UNIQUE(token); account and verification have only PK. getLastSeenForUserIds (called by caseload, progression, admin overview and management) does SELECT user_id, MAX(updated_at) FROM session WHERE user_id IN (...) GROUP BY user_id, which is a seq scan. getOnlineOrgMembers filters on session.updated_at with no index. The account lookups better-auth makes on sign-in, password change and user delete scan the account table, and verification lookups by identifier scan verification. The /heartbeat endpoint UPDATEs session.updated_at once a minute per open tab (the source of the ~33k session writes). Expired sessions and verification tokens are never deleted except by chance.
confirmed.breaks_at: Each login adds a session row that is only removed if that token is used again after expiry. With thousands of learners, session reaches 10^5-10^6 rows within months, so every tutor pipeline and admin load seq-scans it. Heartbeats from ~2k concurrent learners (~33 writes/s) each rewrite a session row (with fillfactor 100 many updates fall off the HOT path) and bloat the table.
confirmed.fix: 1) CREATE INDEX session_user_id_idx ON session (user_id); account_user_id_idx ON account (user_id); verification_identifier_idx ON verification (identifier). 2) Add a maintenance purge job (batched, 5k rows per DELETE ... WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid ... LIMIT)) for session WHERE expires_at < now() - interval '1 day' and verification WHERE expires_at < now(). 3) Make touchSession conditional: UPDATE session SET updated_at=now() WHERE id=? AND updated_at < now() - interval '45 seconds', which cuts multi-tab write amplification. 4) ALTER TABLE session SET (fillfactor=70, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.02). 5) Better: move presence to Redis (ZADD online:{org} ts userId) or a narrow user_presence(user_id PK, last_seen_at) table, so getOnlineOrgMembers and getLastSeen stop depending on session.updated_at. Do NOT add an index on session.updated_at, because it would make every heartbeat a non-HOT update.
confirmed.flow_risk: Purge must keep non-expired sessions, so no logged-in user is signed out. Impersonation sessions (session.impersonated_by) follow the same expiry. The Online-now panel and last-seen columns must keep working during any presence migration, so dual-write first. The conditional touch makes presence up to 45s stale, which is invisible against the 5-minute online window.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: schema.ts:113-167 has session with only PK + unique(token); account and verification have only PK. getLastSeenForUserIds filters inArray(session.userId) with GROUP BY (analytics.ts:95-103), getLastLogin filters session.user_id, deleteSessionsByUserId (users.ts) filters session.user_id, and getOnlineOrgMembers filters session.updated_at. touchSession (users.ts:106) is an unconditional UPDATE from /heartbeat. maintenance.ts only purges system events and dead letters (lines 7, 33, 82), with no session or verification cleanup. The user_id FK cascades also scan these tables on user delete. The claimed write rate depends on how many concurrent users there are. The session(user_id) index is safe for HOT updates because user_id never changes.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add session(user_id), account(user_id), verification(identifier). Do NOT index session.updated_at. Purge only WHERE expires_at < now() - 1 day, batched, so no live session is lost; impersonation sessions follow the same expiry. A conditional touch (updated_at < now() - 45s) is safe against the 5-minute online window. Redis presence is optional and can come later. Treat the fillfactor change as optional tuning.

confirmed.title: Every coursework download does an unindexed jsonb containment seq-scan (two scans for feedback files), per key
confirmed.location: packages/db/src/queries/coursework/coursework.ts:205-231 (getSubmissionByFileKey / getSubmissionByFeedbackFileKey); apps/api/src/middlewares/guards/ownership.ts:371-392 (assertCourseworkDownloadAccess, sequential per key); schema.ts:3998-4037 and 4048-4079
confirmed.current: files @> '[{"key":...}]'::jsonb on coursework_submission and feedback_files @> ... on coursework_result have no GIN index, so each lookup scans the table. The guard calls them per key in a sequential loop, and for tutor feedback files the first lookup misses and a second scan joins the two tables. Download-all and preview of N files means N or 2N full scans.
confirmed.breaks_at: About 100k+ submission rows (5k learners x 20+ items x versions), where each signed-URL request costs tens to hundreds of ms of CPU on the shared 2-vCPU droplet DB client path. A tutor batch download of 30 files stalls a pooled connection for seconds.
confirmed.fix: Preferred: derive narrowing predicates from the key. Keys are coursework/{courseId}/{learnerId}/{lessonId}/{assessmentSlug}/{version}/file (packages/core/src/utils/upload.ts, services/coursework/coursework.ts courseworkKeyPrefix). Parse learnerId/lessonId from the key and add AND learner_id=? AND lesson_id=? (using existing idx_coursework_submission_learner_lesson) while keeping the @> check, so a forged key still resolves to nothing. Belt-and-braces: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY coursework_submission_files_gin ON coursework_submission USING gin (files jsonb_path_ops) and the same on coursework_result(feedback_files). Also run the keys through one batched query (WHERE files @> ANY(...)) instead of a loop.
confirmed.flow_risk: This is the only door to coursework bytes, so authorization must not weaken. The key is only a locator and canReadCoursework still decides, and keys that do not parse must fall back to the GIN path or deny. Learner self-view, allocated tutor and admin downloads are unchanged. GIN adds write cost on insert (only 1 row per submission and result, so negligible).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: getSubmissionByFileKey and getSubmissionByFeedbackFileKey (coursework.ts:205-231) use jsonb @> with no GIN index; schema.ts:4035-4036 only has (learner,lesson) and (course) indexes. assertCourseworkDownloadAccess (ownership.ts:371-392) loops sequentially and a feedback key costs two scans. Today there are 7 rows. A scan of 100k rows with jsonb containment is ~100-500 ms, so a download-all of N files costs N times that. The key-parsing fix is feasible because submit enforces key.startsWith(courseworkKeyPrefix(courseId, actor.userId, lessonId, ...)) (services/coursework/coursework.ts:145), and the feedback prefix has the same course/learner/lesson layout (upload.ts:102). 'high' is a bit generous, but the guard sits on the path of every download.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Parsing learnerId/lessonId out of the key as an extra AND predicate is OK only if the @> check stays, and malformed keys must deny. Parse by segment, not regex over the whole string. For feedback keys, narrow coursework_result via its submission's learner_id/lesson_id by joining, not by a column on the result. A GIN jsonb_path_ops index on files is the simplest uniform fix; the feedback_files GIN is also needed because those keys have no learner column on coursework_result. Batch the keys with Promise.all or one query to cut the sequential latency.

confirmed.title: Caseload, progression and admin reports load every submission row (with files/feedback) for the whole roster into memory and re-sort; no supporting composite index
confirmed.location: packages/db/src/queries/coursework/coursework.ts:252-300 (getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners); apps/api/src/services/caseload/caseload.ts:70-130; apps/api/src/services/progression/progression.ts:236-250,320-330; queries/reports/reports.ts:90-131 and queries/dash/admin-overview.ts:579-640 (DISTINCT ON learner,lesson,assessment ORDER BY version DESC); schema.ts:4035-4036
confirmed.current: The tutor caseload and the admin org-wide caseload call getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners(rosterIds). It has no LIMIT or paging, selects the jsonb files and feedback text, joins course/lesson/result, and orders by submitted_at. The service then reduces to latest-per-unit in JS. For admin the roster is the entire org (inArray with thousands of ids). The DISTINCT ON queries need rows ordered by (learner, lesson, assessment_key, version DESC), but the existing unique index is ASC on version, so Postgres still sorts. getCourseProgressReport + buildCoursePassSet run the same course-wide DISTINCT ON twice per target course in buildProgressionForRoster.
confirmed.breaks_at: 5k learners x 25 items x ~1.5 versions is about 190k rows (50-100 MB of jsonb/text) materialised per admin caseload or progression request, plus a 190k-row sort per course per report. Several admins/tutors at once will OOM or time out the 4 GB droplet. inArray with more than ~65k ids hits the Postgres bind-parameter limit.
confirmed.fix: Push latest-per-unit into SQL: SELECT DISTINCT ON (learner_id, lesson_id) ... for the caseload, selecting only the columns the screen needs (drop files/feedback; fetch per-learner detail lazily). Add CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY coursework_submission_latest_idx ON coursework_submission (course_id, learner_id, lesson_id, assessment_key, version DESC) INCLUDE (id, submission_type, submitted_at) WHERE submission_type='final', and (course_id, submitted_at) for the tutor pipeline's recent/awaiting queues. For awaiting-marking use NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM coursework_result r WHERE r.submission_id=s.id). Long term, keep a coursework_assessment_state(learner_id, lesson_id, assessment_key, latest_final_version, latest_verdict, updated_at) row maintained in the marking/submit transaction, so reports read it directly. For admin, key the query by org (join course->group) rather than an id list. De-dupe the double getLatestMarkedResultsForCourse call per course.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor scoping must stay allocation-only (docs/ACCESS.md s8, commit ad92abcf5): keep the learnerIds filter derived from tutor_allocation and never replace it with a course filter for tutors. 'Latest version wins, a later Refer overrides an earlier Pass' semantics must be preserved exactly, including legacy rows with NULL assessment_key (NULLS NOT DISTINCT) and drafts never gating. A denormalised state table must be written in the same tx as recordCourseworkResult and backfilled.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners (coursework.ts:252-300) has no LIMIT and selects files jsonb, comment and feedback for the whole roster. getTutorCaseload (caseload.ts:70-130) then reduces to latest-per-unit in JS. For ADMIN the roster is listAllocatedLearnersForOrg, i.e. the whole org. Memory and latency grow linearly with learners x submissions. The 65k bind-parameter claim is unrealistic (rosters are in the low thousands). The ASC/DESC version sort claim is plausible but secondary. The JS reducer keys by learner::lesson (ignores assessmentKey) and also counts drafts, so its semantics must be preserved exactly.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The proposed partial index WHERE submission_type='final' would NOT serve the caseload query, which does not filter on type. The unique (learner, lesson, assessment_key, version) already covers the per-learner lookups, so the new composite (course_id, learner_id, ...) index is probably redundant; prove it with EXPLAIN before adding. A SQL DISTINCT ON (learner_id, lesson_id) ORDER BY version DESC still needs a separate GROUP BY count for submissionCount, and must keep drafts in the count and the NULL assessment_key behaviour. Keep the learnerIds allocation filter for tutors (ACCESS.md s8). Org-wide admin may use a group.organization_id join instead of an id list. Drop the 'state table' idea for now; it is a large denormalisation with consistency risk.

confirmed.title: computeLearnerCourseProgress issues 2-3 queries per unit; the learner home and the tutor-feedback status call it for every course and run per page load
confirmed.current: For each unit hasLearnerPassedUnit runs SELECT documents FROM lesson, then either getLatestMarkedResultsByAssessment or getLatestMarkedResult. A learner with 3 courses x 30 units is about 270 queries for one /lms dashboard load, fired with Promise.all across courses. getTutorFeedbackStatus recomputes the same totals, and getProgressionDetail does it again per course. The pool is max 10 connections per process (drizzle.ts:24).
confirmed.breaks_at: A few dozen concurrent learner-home loads (login surge, deadline day) occupy all 10 pooled connections with hundreds of tiny round trips each, starving every other request; Supabase pooler latency (~10-30 ms/round trip) makes one dashboard take seconds.
confirmed.fix: Batch per learner: one query for the course's lesson documents (getAssessmentItemsByLesson already batches, use it for all units) and one for the learner's latest FINAL verdicts across the course (SELECT DISTINCT ON (lesson_id, assessment_key) ... WHERE learner_id=? AND course_id=?), then call the pure computeProgress with an in-memory predicate (the report path already does this with assembleReportRows). Index to support it: coursework_submission (learner_id, course_id, lesson_id, assessment_key, version DESC) WHERE submission_type='final'. Cache the tutor-feedback status or compute passedUnits from the same shared result.
confirmed.flow_risk: The progress numbers must stay identical across the learner self-view, tutor view and reports (docs/PROGRESS-MODEL.md); reuse computeProgress and isPassingResult, do not fork the rule. Preserve the legacy per-unit fallback for units with no tagged assessments and the isNonGatingUnit exclusions. Unit-lock gating (isUnitUnlocked) uses the same passed helper, so test sequential-unlock courses.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: computeLearnerCourseProgress (progress.ts:80-94) loops units sequentially and awaits hasLearnerPassedUnit per unit (coursework.ts:~460-470): one lesson-documents query plus one result query each, so about 2 queries per unit per course. getLearnerDashboard (lms/dashboard.ts:118-135) and computePassedUnits (tutor-feedback.ts:17-22, used by GET /lms/tutor-feedback) both call it for every enrolment. The pool-exhaustion claim is overstated: within a course the queries run serially, so one request holds up to (#courses) connections at once, not hundreds. The real cost is per-request latency (about 2 x units x 10-30 ms) and the repeated recomputation (dashboard + tutor-feedback + progression).
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Batch with getAssessmentItemsByLesson for all units and one DISTINCT ON (lesson_id, assessment_key) query per (learner, course) restricted to type='final' and kind='verdict', then reuse isPassingResult. Preserve the legacy per-unit fallback (units with no tagged assessments use getLatestMarkedResult, which has different semantics: no assessment_key filter) and isNonGatingUnit. The hasLearnerPassedUnit helper is also used for unit locking, so keep its signature and add a batched variant instead of replacing it.

confirmed.title: Message inbox/summary reads the entire message history per request; listMessages returns the OLDEST 200, not the newest; no per-org thread index
confirmed.current: Both inbox queries are SELECT DISTINCT ON (message.thread_id) ... ORDER BY thread_id, created_at DESC over every message of every thread the participant is in, and the unread count scans all of them too. idx_message_thread_created is (thread_id, created_at ASC) so the DESC pick still sorts. listMessages is documented as 'the newest limit are returned' but orders ASC with LIMIT 200, so after 200 messages a thread shows only the first 200 (a real correctness bug that appears at scale). message_thread has no organization_id index, so getOrgMessagingStats scans threads/messages by org. idx_message_thread and idx_message_thread_tutor are redundant prefixes.
confirmed.breaks_at: Heavy tutors (hundreds of learners x hundreds of messages) pay a scan of 10^4-10^5 message rows per inbox open and per learner-home load. A long thread silently stops showing new messages past 200.
confirmed.fix: Rewrite with a LATERAL: FROM message_thread t JOIN LATERAL (SELECT body, sender_id, created_at FROM message WHERE thread_id=t.id ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1) m ON true; compute unread with EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM message WHERE thread_id=t.id AND sender_id<>? AND created_at > coalesce(lastReadAt,'-infinity') LIMIT 1) or a per-thread counter. Index: replace message(thread_id) + (thread_id, created_at) with CREATE INDEX message_thread_created_desc ON message (thread_id, created_at DESC) INCLUDE (sender_id); add message_thread(organization_id). Fix listMessages to ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT n then reverse (and add a before-cursor for paging).
confirmed.flow_risk: Messaging is allocation-gated at the service layer (isAllocatedTutor, archived threads read-only); these queries do no access control, so changing them must not change which threads a participant sees (archived threads and learner-sent messages still count). The read cursor semantics (null cursor = unread) must be preserved. Chat order in the UI stays oldest-first after reversing the page.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly confirmed. listMessages (message.ts:99-111) is documented 'the newest limit are returned' but does ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 200, so it returns the OLDEST 200. This is a real correctness bug, and more likely than the finding implies because message_thread is UNIQUE(tutor_id, learner_id), so one thread accumulates the whole relationship. The inbox query (message.ts:222-250) is a DISTINCT ON over all messages of all the participant's threads; real, but a learner has 1-3 threads and only heavy tutors pay. 'message_thread has no organization_id index' is true but useless at one org (no selectivity). messagesLast7d filters message.created_at with no created_at-leading index.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Fix listMessages first (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT n, then reverse; this is a safe small change, but it changes what the UI shows past 200 messages, so check the thread UI first). The LATERAL rewrite is fine and does not change which threads are visible. Do not add message_thread(organization_id) for a single-org deployment; consider message(created_at) for the 7-day stat. The redundant idx_message_thread drop is fine.

confirmed.title: Notification list sorts without an index, rows are inserted one at a time per recipient inside the request, and the table is never pruned
confirmed.current: listNotificationsForUser does WHERE user_id=? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT n, but the indexes are (user_id) and (user_id, read_at), so rows are fetched and sorted. countUnreadNotifications (bell badge, probably polled) counts via (user_id, read_at). hasRecentUnreadForEntity filters (user_id, entity_type, entity_id, read_at, created_at) with no entity index. emitNotification loops recipients sequentially doing insert + preference SELECT + coalesce SELECT + email enqueue, and publishAnnouncement awaits it in the request: an all_learners broadcast to 5,000 learners is ~15,000 sequential round trips on one connection. Nothing ever deletes notifications.
confirmed.breaks_at: Broadcast to a few thousand learners takes minutes and holds a pooled connection and the HTTP request (timeouts, duplicate publishes). Per user the bell/list degrade as notifications accumulate for years; the table grows linearly with learners x events.
confirmed.fix: Indexes: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY notification_user_created_idx ON notification (user_id, created_at DESC); CREATE INDEX notification_user_unread_idx ON notification (user_id) WHERE read_at IS NULL (replace idx_notification_user_unread and idx_notification_user; add (user_id, entity_type, entity_id) WHERE read_at IS NULL if coalescing stays). Code: for fan-out, bulk INSERT ... VALUES in chunks of 500 returning ids, prefetch notification_preference for all recipients in one inArray query, and run big audiences (>~50) as a BullMQ job in apps/jobs with the HTTP call returning immediately. Retention: nightly job deleting read notifications older than ~90 days in batches.
confirmed.flow_risk: In-app rows must still be ALWAYS written even when email is off (docs/COMMS-MODEL.md). Per-recipient email preference defaults and thread coalescing must keep identical results when batched. Announcement targeting rules (all_learners / course / learner / tutor) and archived/deleted filtering are untouched.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: notification indexes are (user_id) and (user_id, read_at) only (schema.ts:4203-4204), while listNotificationsForUser sorts by created_at DESC, so a per-user sort. emitNotification (notify.ts:41-90) loops recipients sequentially, and publishAnnouncement awaits it inside the HTTP request (announcements.ts:~190). Nothing prunes notifications. The query count is overstated: announcement recipients are built as { userId, emailFields } with no email (announcements.ts:~195), so the `!recipient.email` continue skips the preference SELECT and the email leg entirely. The fan-out is therefore about 1 INSERT per recipient (5,000 sequential inserts, tens of seconds at pooler latency), not 15,000 round trips. Still a real request-blocking risk.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Index (user_id, created_at DESC) is the main win and is safe. For fan-out: chunked bulk INSERT, then queue the big audiences to the jobs worker, as proposed. Keep always-write in-app rows. Note the announcement email leg is currently dead because recipients have no email; decide whether that is intentional before 'fixing' it, since enabling it would suddenly send mail. Retention delete of read notifications older than ~90 days is safe.

confirmed.title: Learner course list (getEnrolledCourses) and similar queries drive from all org courses and use correlated subqueries per row
confirmed.current: getEnrolledCourses starts FROM course JOIN group (org filter) and LEFT JOINs groupmember/program/lesson to find the learner's rows, then filters WHERE groupmember.id IS NOT NULL OR programMember.id IS NOT NULL. It is O(active courses in org) per learner request rather than O(enrolled courses), and each returned row evaluates 3-4 correlated subqueries (lesson_completion count, exercise counts, isExerciseCompletedSql over submission). getCourseStats joins groupmember x lesson x lesson_completion with COUNT(DISTINCT), producing students x lessons rows per course. getOrgCourses LEFT JOINs lesson with GROUP BY plus subqueries.
confirmed.breaks_at: Hundreds of courses x thousands of learners: every /lms home and course list load scans all courses plus the group/program joins. getCourseStats on a course with 2,000 students x 40 lessons is 80k joined rows per course, per admin dashboard load.
confirmed.fix: Drive from the learner: SELECT ... FROM groupmember gm JOIN course c ON c.group_id=gm.group_id WHERE gm.profile_id=? (uses the new groupmember_profile_role_idx) UNION ALL the program-member path, then compute counts with GROUP BY subqueries once per course set (lesson counts: WHERE course_id = ANY(?) GROUP BY course_id; completions: batch over those course ids). Replace COUNT(DISTINCT) cross-joins in getCourseStats with separate pre-aggregated subqueries (students per course, lessons per course, completions per course). Cache the admin dash numbers for 60s or read dash_org_stats as a materialized view refreshed by a job.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learners can reach a course by direct enrolment OR program membership; the rewrite must keep both paths and the dedupe of courses reachable by both. Compliance-cycle columns (latest cycle) and LIVE_CLASS upcoming sessions must be preserved. Output shape of TStudentCourse must not change.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly confirmed. getEnrolledCourses (course.ts:956-1075) does FROM course JOIN group with LEFT JOINs to groupmember/program, then WHERE gm.id IS NOT NULL OR pm.id IS NOT NULL, so it iterates all ACTIVE org courses per learner request (LEFT JOINs prevent driving from the learner). However the groupmember join is ON group_id = group.id AND profile_id = ?, already served by unique_group_profile, so the groupmember profile index does not help here. The correlated subqueries sit in the select list with GROUP BY, so they run per returned (enrolled) row, not per org course. Course count grows slowly for a training provider (tens to hundreds), so the scan is cheap. getCourseStats' COUNT(DISTINCT) cross product is real but only matters at 2,000 students x 40 lessons per course on an admin page.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Defer. If rewritten, the UNION of the direct and program paths must dedupe courses reachable by both, keep cohort/program status = 'ACTIVE' and org filters, and keep certificateEarnedAt and compliance-cycle columns. Prefer fixing getCourseStats with pre-aggregated subqueries; cache the admin number rather than adding a materialised view.

confirmed.title: Admin overview/report aggregates are uncached and join through group.organization_id with missing org indexes on allocation/thread tables and an anti-join on tutor_allocation
confirmed.current: tutor_allocation is filtered by organization_id in listAllocationsByOrg, listAllocatedLearnersForOrg and the NOT EXISTS orphan check, but has only (tutor_id, learner_id) unique + tutor and learner indexes, no organization_id index and no index leading with learner_id where the anti-join needs (learner_id, organization_id). message_thread has no organization_id index (getOrgMessagingStats). Every aggregate (referral breakdowns, completions, submissions-per-month, time-to-complete, open-refer counts) reaches org scope through course->group.organization_id, and the date filters use extract(year from ...) = ?, which cannot use an index. These ~15 queries run on every admin dashboard/report load with no caching.
confirmed.breaks_at: Roughly 100k+ results/submissions: each report page runs several multi-join full scans (referral queries touch every coursework_result row of the org). Concurrent admin/manager viewers multiply the load on the shared droplet.
confirmed.fix: Add: tutor_allocation (organization_id, tutor_id) and (learner_id, organization_id); message_thread (organization_id) INCLUDE (archived_at); coursework_result (kind, recorded_at) WHERE kind='verdict'. Rewrite year filters as range predicates (completed_at >= make_date(?,1,1) AND < make_date(?+1,1,1)). Cache the whole admin overview payload in Redis for 30-60s keyed by org (explicit invalidation on marking/enrolment is optional). For the heaviest, add a nightly/5-min materialised summary table (org_daily metrics) like analytics_org_daily.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin/manager read-only paths; keep the org scoping through group.organization_id so one org can never see another's rows. Cached numbers can lag by up to the TTL, so label as 'updated every minute' or invalidate on write. Managers have read-only access to the same aggregates.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly confirmed. extract(year from ...) = ? is non-sargable (admin-overview.ts:125,243,268), the endpoints are uncached (no cache/redis in services/dash/admin-overview.ts or routes/dash/stats.ts), and tutor_allocation/message_thread have no organization_id index. But this deployment is single-org, so an organization_id index has no selectivity and the planner would ignore it. The listed multi-join aggregates only become costly at 100k+ result rows. The org scope goes through course->group.organization_id, which is fine.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Skip the organization_id indexes unless a second org is planned. Do the sargable range rewrite (>= make_date(y,1,1) AND < make_date(y+1,1,1)) and a 30-60s per-org Redis cache on the overview payload; both are low-risk and read-only. Keep org scoping through group.organization_id. The coursework_result (kind, recorded_at) partial index needs EXPLAIN evidence before adding.

confirmed.title: Org member lists/counts need (organization_id, role_id) and name/email search uses ILIKE '%x%' with no trigram index
confirmed.current: organizationmember has (org), (profile), (profile, org) and partial uniques, but nothing on (organization_id, role_id). Role-filtered listing (listOrgLearners, listOrgTutorMembers, getMemberRoleStatusCounts, countActiveStudents which runs on each enrolment for the student cap) reads every member of the org. Admin people search uses ilike on profile.fullname, profile.email and organizationmember.email with leading wildcards, which no btree can serve; plus OFFSET paging and a separate COUNT.
confirmed.breaks_at: 10-50k members: the student-cap COUNT and every roster build scan all members; admin people search seq-scans profile (and OR-of-three ILIKE forces a full scan) for each keystroke.
confirmed.fix: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY organizationmember_org_role_idx ON organizationmember (organization_id, role_id) INCLUDE (profile_id). Enable pg_trgm (Supabase: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm WITH SCHEMA extensions) and add GIN gin_trgm_ops indexes on profile(fullname), profile(email), organizationmember(email). Prefer keyset paging for large lists. Consider dropping idx_organizationmember_profile_id (prefix of the (profile_id, organization_id) index).
confirmed.flow_risk: Search semantics (case-insensitive substring) are preserved by trigram indexes. Index-only scans need the visibility map, so keep autovacuum healthy. Dropping the redundant profile_id index is safe because resolveActor and getUserOrgRolesMap use (profile_id, organization_id) prefixes.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly confirmed. organizationmember has no (organization_id, role_id) index (schema.ts:1878-1884), and the search uses ilike '%x%'. But organizationmember has one row per user (tens of thousands at most), so role-filtered scans and countActiveStudents are a few ms, and in a single-org deployment the students are nearly the whole table, so an (org, role) index barely helps the student count. The proposed trigram fix will not work as written: getOrganizationUsers (users.ts:29-95) ORs ilike across profile.fullname, profile.email and organizationmember.email AFTER a LEFT JOIN, and an OR across two tables cannot use per-table GIN indexes.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Low priority. If pursued: (org, role) INCLUDE (profile_id) is fine for tutor/admin lists; for search, restructure to search profile first (BitmapOr of trigram indexes on profile.fullname/email) and join, or add a single generated search column. Add keyset paging only if the member lists actually grow past tens of thousands. pg_trgm GIN indexes add write cost on profile, so defer.

confirmed.title: Public registration dedupe is check-then-insert with no unique constraint, so double-submits and bots create duplicate pending applications
confirmed.current: The unauthenticated registration form checks hasOpenRegistrationForEmail and then inserts; only a non-unique index (organization_id, status, created_at) exists. Two concurrent submissions (double-click, retry, scripted) both pass the check and both insert. Approval is then double-onboarded or leaves duplicate queue rows. Emails are lowercased by the caller only.
confirmed.breaks_at: Any time two requests race, which on a public form under launch traffic or bot load is routine; the staff queue fills with duplicates.
confirmed.fix: Before creating the index, dedupe: DELETE or reject duplicate pending rows per (organization_id, lower(email)). Then CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY registration_org_email_pending_unique ON registration (organization_id, lower(email)) WHERE status = 'pending'. Change insertRegistration to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING and map no-row to the existing 'already registered' response.
confirmed.flow_risk: Approved/rejected registrations must still allow a fresh application (the partial predicate only covers pending). The approval flow's claimPendingRegistration compare-and-swap is unaffected. A rejected applicant re-applying later still works. The unique build fails if duplicate pending rows exist, so dedupe first (see migration-safety).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: insertRegistration + hasOpenRegistrationForEmail (registration.ts:26-75) are check-then-insert, with only a non-unique (org, status, created_at) index (schema.ts:4458). Two simultaneous submissions both insert. It is a correctness race (duplicate staff-queue rows), not a scale problem, and rate limiting on the public route (check) reduces it. Emails are stored lowercased and trimmed (schema comment line 4434), so lower(email) is not needed in the index.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Use a partial UNIQUE (organization_id, email) WHERE status = 'pending'; dedupe existing pending duplicates first. Change insertRegistration to ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING and map an empty return to the existing 'already registered' response, keeping the same response shape so the public form behaves identically.

confirmed.title: Bulk enrolment and tutor-course assignment are read-then-insert with no ON CONFLICT, so one concurrent duplicate fails the whole batch
confirmed.current: enrollUsersInCourseGroups reads existing (group_id, profile_id) pairs, filters in JS, then runs a plain multi-row INSERT. unique_group_profile and unique_group_email exist, so a concurrent enrolment of the same learner (admin bulk import racing a registration approval, or two admins) raises 23505 and rolls back the entire multi-row insert, so none of the batch's learners are enrolled. setTutorCourseAssignments has the same select-then-insert per course.
confirmed.breaks_at: Bulk onboarding of hundreds of learners (the scaling scenario) with any overlapping action turns a successful import into an all-or-nothing failure that the operator has to retry blindly.
confirmed.fix: Use db.insert(groupmember).values(rows).onConflictDoNothing({ target: [groupmember.groupId, groupmember.profileId] }).returning() in addGroupMembers and report the number actually inserted; chunk to 500-1000 rows per statement. For tutor assignment use onConflictDoUpdate setting role_id=TUTOR only when the existing role is not already TUTOR, and never downgrade an ADMIN.
confirmed.flow_risk: Silent do-nothing must not hide a role mismatch: if a learner already exists in the group with a different role (for example a tutor being enrolled as a student), surface it. unique_group_email conflicts (email-only rows with NULL profile_id) are a different target and still raise. The student-plan cap check should run after the insert count is known.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly confirmed. enrollUsersInCourseGroups (group.ts:64-89) reads existing pairs and then does one multi-row INSERT (addGroupMembers, group.ts:25-33) with no ON CONFLICT; a concurrent duplicate raises 23505 and fails the whole batch. A real but narrow race. setTutorCourseAssignments (people.ts:294-309) already runs in a transaction and does select-then-update/insert, which is only racy against a concurrent identical request for the same tutor and course. More important for bulk onboarding of thousands: the single INSERT has about 5 bind parameters per row, so around 13k rows hits the 65,535-parameter limit, and getExistingGroupMembers builds an inArray cross product of group ids x profile ids with no chunking.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: onConflictDoNothing targeting (group_id, profile_id) is right but does not cover unique_group_email / unique_entries conflicts, which still raise. Chunk both the existing-member lookup and the insert to ~500-1000 rows. Do not onConflictDoUpdate a role on enrolment (it could downgrade an ADMIN or flip a TUTOR); keep existing 'skip existing' behaviour and report skipped counts.

confirmed.title: Redundant duplicate indexes and over-indexed append-only logs add write cost; log/analytics tables have no retention and an unbounded purge
confirmed.location: schema.ts:427-428 (idx_profile_id, idx_profile_email), 1882-1884, 2638-2640,2667 (sso/token org_id dup of .unique()), 3982-3984, 4264-4266, 4292-4293, 4077-4078, 3819-3820, 4113-4146, 4203-4204, 2380-2382, 2461-2463, 2507-2508, 2830-2831, 3105-3106, 3140-3141, 1168-1171; 3860-3909 (audit_event, system_event_log), 202-228 (analytics_page_event); queries/system-events/system-events.ts:63-71; apps/jobs/src/workers/maintenance.ts:24-83
confirmed.current: Exact or prefix duplicates of existing unique/PK indexes: idx_profile_id (PK), idx_profile_email (profile_email_key), idx_organizationmember_profile_id (prefix of profile_org), idx_organization_sso_config_org_id and idx_organization_token_auth_org_id (duplicate the .unique() columns), idx_tutor_allocation_tutor and idx_message_thread_tutor (prefix of the pair uniques), idx_message_thread (prefix of thread_created), idx_coursework_result_submission and idx_media_transcript_asset (duplicate uniques), idx_unit_time_spent_learner / idx_unit_time_monthly_learner / idx_unit_time_monthly_learner_month and idx_analytics_login_events_user_id (prefix of uniques), idx_notification_user (prefix of user_unread), and the *_program_id / *_cohort_id / *_widget_id / tag_id / goal_id single-column indexes that duplicate the leading column of a unique. Low-cardinality candidates for the advisor's 74 unused: idx_*_event_type, system_event_log severity/event_type/user_email (the ILIKE '%x%' search cannot use a btree), idx_ape_event_type/session/user, idx_audit_event_action/actor/org, idx_organization_api_key_type, idx_widget_status, idx_program_goal_status, idx_assets_organization_byte_size. unit_time_* are written every 30s per active learner. The only retention job covers system_event_log (90d) and dead letters; the purge is DELETE ... RETURNING id of every old row in one statement. audit_event, analytics_page_event, job_step, media_job and analytics_login_events grow unbounded.
confirmed.breaks_at: Not user-visible until write-heavy tables reach millions of rows, when each extra index multiplies insert/update cost and vacuum time and a single-statement purge of millions of rows holds locks and memory on the small droplet.
confirmed.fix: Confirm with SELECT relname, indexrelname, idx_scan FROM pg_stat_user_indexes WHERE idx_scan = 0 on the Supabase DB (the stats there are authoritative; I could not read prod), then DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY the duplicates above in a hand-run script and remove them from schema.ts. Make deleteSystemEventsOlderThan batched (DELETE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... LIMIT 5000) in a loop, no RETURNING of ids) and add the same loop for read notifications, expired sessions/verification, analytics_page_event (rolled up into analytics_*_daily first) and job_step/media_job. Set fillfactor 80 on unit_time_spent, unit_time_monthly and lesson_video_progress so heartbeat upserts stay HOT.
confirmed.flow_risk: Only drop an index after idx_scan confirms zero use over a representative period; unique constraints (which enforce correctness) must never be dropped. audit_event is a compliance trail, so agree a retention period with the owner before pruning. Analytics rollups must be written before raw deletes.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed for the examples checked: idx_profile_id duplicates the PK and idx_profile_email duplicates profile_email_key (schema.ts:425-428); idx_organization_sso_config_org_id and idx_organization_token_auth_org_id sit beside unique columns; the system-event purge (system-events.ts:63-71) is a single DELETE ... RETURNING id of every old row. analytics_page_event carries 5 secondary indexes on an append-only table. Impact is only write cost and vacuum time, and the purge runs daily so it deletes about one day of rows, not millions. Retention for audit_event and analytics tables is a policy decision.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Drop duplicate indexes only after pg_stat_user_indexes shows idx_scan = 0 on prod (the advisor's 74 unused are the authoritative list). Do not drop anything backing a unique constraint. Change the purge to a batched DELETE without RETURNING. Do not prune audit_event without the owner agreeing a retention period.

confirmed.title: Hot lookups by course_section.course_id, lesson.section_id and the quiz stack (submission/question/question_answer/exercise) have no supporting index
confirmed.location: schema.ts:288-299 (course_section), 975-1069 (lesson.section_id), 577-620 (submission), 1217-1258 (exercise.lesson_id), 1918-2007 (question, question_answer), 1568-1598 (lesson_completion.profile_id); queries/course/course.ts:1306-1308; queries/course/public-course.ts:158-164; queries/caseload/dashboard.ts:87-95; queries/course/progression.ts:346-366 (isExerciseCompletedSql)
confirmed.current: course_section is read by course_id on every course/outline/public-course load (plus lesson->section joins for lesson ids) with no index on course_id; lesson.section_id has none (join and cascade-delete path). The stock quiz tables are queried through correlated EXISTS (isExerciseCompletedSql: submission.exercise_id + submitted_by -> groupmember; question.exercise_id) inside every getCourseProgress and getEnrolledCourses row, with no index on submission(exercise_id, submitted_by), question(exercise_id), question_answer(submission_id/group_member_id) or exercise(lesson_id). lesson_completion has only unique(lesson_id, profile_id), so per-profile lookups across courses cannot seek.
confirmed.breaks_at: Tables are tiny today (the quiz tables are probably empty in prod), so impact is low now. With hundreds of courses the course_section scan grows linearly per course page view, and once quizzes are used the EXISTS subqueries become per-course-row seq scans of submission.
confirmed.fix: Add (only the queried ones, not all 103 advisor FKs): course_section (course_id, "order"); lesson (section_id); submission (exercise_id, submitted_by); question (exercise_id); question_answer (submission_id); exercise (lesson_id); lesson_completion (profile_id) WHERE is_complete. All via CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. Skip created_by/revoked_by/recorded_by-style audit FKs that no query filters on; instead, ensure their ON DELETE SET NULL deletes (profile removal) are rare and run off-peak.
confirmed.flow_risk: Index-only changes. If quizzes are confirmed unused for Pearl, de-prioritise the submission/question/question_answer indexes (but then consider removing the dead exercise subqueries from getEnrolledCourses/getCourseProgress as a code simplification).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: course_section has no index (schema.ts:288-299; course_id FK cascades), lesson.section_id has none, lesson_completion has only unique(lesson_id, profile_id). The reviewer also checked lesson.course_id: it IS covered by the prefix of idx_lesson_course_slug (course_id, slug), so no new lesson index is needed. All of these tables are small (per-course sections, per-learner completions); the quiz tables (submission/question/question_answer/exercise) are probably empty in prod, so the practical impact is low.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add only course_section(course_id) and lesson(section_id) (cheap, used on every course load and in cascade deletes) and lesson_completion(profile_id) if profile deletes or per-profile queries show up. Skip the quiz-stack indexes unless quizzes are used; confirm with row counts first.

confirmed.title: Admin overview recomputes the full marking pipeline org-wide AND once per tutor (all submissions loaded into JS, 100+ concurrent pipelines on a 10-connection pool)
confirmed.current: getAdminOverview calls listOrgLearners, then computePipelineForRoster(orgRoster), which does getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners(allLearnerIds): ONE query returning EVERY coursework_submission row for the org (3 left joins, ships files jsonb, comment and feedback text) via inArray(learner_id, [all ids]). All grouping/stats are done in JS. It then does tutors.map(async t => listLearnersForTutor + computePipelineForRoster(roster)) under Promise.all: each tutor re-runs the same pipeline (about 10 queries: allocation, submissions, lesson docs, getLastSeen x2, profile status, courses, lessonIds, lesson docs again) and re-fetches its slice of the same submissions. It also runs getCourseProgressReport per published course (4-5 queries each, unbounded). The 60s in-memory cache has no single-flight, so concurrent misses (several admins/managers, or the 60s expiry under a refresh poll) each start the whole fan-out.
confirmed.breaks_at: 5,000 learners x about 40 submissions = about 200k rows (50-150 MB of JSON incl. files/feedback) materialised in the Node heap for the org pass, and about the same again summed across 100 tutor passes. About 1,000+ queries are queued at once on a postgres.js pool of 10 (DATABASE_POOL_MAX), so every other request (login, lesson load, heartbeats) waits behind them (head-of-line blocking). The 4 GB droplet shared with dashboard/jobs/redis risks OOM or a 30 s+ response. With Supabase's auth_db_connections warning this also pins pooler slots.
confirmed.fix: 1) Replace the JS aggregation with SQL: one grouped query for org-wide pipeline stats (DISTINCT ON (learner, lesson, assessment_key, submission_type) latest-per-item CTE, then count(*) filter (...) for awaiting/resubmission/overdue/dueSoon/passed/referred, avg turnaround as avg(recorded_at - submitted_at)). 2) Compute per-tutor performance in ONE query: join tutor_allocation to that CTE and GROUP BY tutor_id, instead of one pipeline per tutor. 3) Fetch per-course completion with one grouped query (count of learners whose non-exempt units are all passed) instead of getCourseProgressReport per course. 4) Add single-flight (an in-flight promise map per org) plus stale-while-revalidate, and move the cache to Redis (already available) so it survives restarts and is shared. 5) Never return files/comment/feedback to stats code (select only id, learner_id, lesson_id, assessment_key, type, version, submitted_at, result, kind, recorded_at). 6) Short term: bound concurrency (3-4 tutors at a time) if the SQL rewrite is deferred.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin and Manager dashboards only (route is requireManagerOrAdmin). Tutor and learner flows are untouched. The access rule is unaffected because the per-tutor numbers must still come ONLY from tutor_allocation (docs/ACCESS.md section 8); keep the join on tutor_allocation.tutor_id so nothing widens. Edge cases that must keep identical semantics: pickLatest by version separately for final vs draft; assessmentPassed means any passing verdict across all versions (not just the latest); priorRefer = any earlier FINAL verdict that is non-passing; overdue SLA from MARKING_SLA_HOURS env; dueSoon only for the latest (final ?? draft) with an unpassed item; legacy rows with null assessment_key (NULLS NOT DISTINCT); learners with zero submissions; DEACTIVATED learners counted as suspended and excluded from the active/inactive/never buckets. Write a parity test comparing the SQL output with the current JS output on a seeded dataset before switching.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed in admin-overview.ts: computePipelineForRoster(learnerRoster) runs getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners(allIds), which loads every submission with files/comment/feedback and 3 left joins, aggregated in JS. Then tutors.map(listLearnersForTutor + computePipelineForRoster) runs unbounded under Promise.all, plus getCourseProgressReport per published course. The cache in stats.ts:275-283 has no single-flight, and drizzle.ts:24 sets max=10. However, the route is manager/admin only with a 60s cache, so it is not critical. Per-tutor slices partition the allocated learners, so the total is about 2x the org pass, not 100x the org. 5k learners x ~10-40 submissions is tens of MB and seconds of pool contention, not a likely OOM. Fix point 5 is right (stats never use files/comment/feedback). Course/unit title joins are also unneeded for stats.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Ship the low-risk steps first: (a) single-flight in-flight promise per org plus stale-while-revalidate, (b) a lean status-only column query for the stats path, (c) bound tutor concurrency to 3-4, (d) derive per-tutor stats from the org-wide submission rows grouped by an in-memory tutor->learner map built from ONE tutor_allocation query, instead of re-querying per tutor. Do the full SQL rewrite only with a parity test. Semantics the SQL must keep: stats.assignments counts ALL assessment items of the roster's courses (every lesson, not just lessons with submissions); avgTurnaround is taken over every verdict row (resultKind='verdict', any version) with d>=0; totalGraded/pass/refer count every verdict row across versions; a learner allocated to 2 tutors counts for each; DEACTIVATED learners are suspended and excluded from the active/inactive/never buckets. Per-tutor numbers must still come only via tutor_allocation.

confirmed.title: Tutor pipeline, caseload and course-content views load every submission for the roster and aggregate in JS (lean columns, duplicate lookups, O(n*m) scans)
confirmed.current: getTutorCaseload and computePipelineForRoster call getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners(roster ids): all versions of all submissions across all courses, including files jsonb, comment and feedback text, that the stats never use. getAssessmentItemsByLesson then loads the full lesson.documents jsonb for every lesson seen, and a second time for every lesson of every roster course (getLessonIdsForCourses then getAssessmentItemsByLesson) just to count assignments. caseload.ts:112 does roster.find(...) inside the awaiting loop (O(learners x awaiting)). getTutorCourseContent (course-view.ts:104) fetches the roster's submissions for ALL courses though only one course is shown, and for an ADMIN the roster is every enrolled learner (visibleLearnerIdsForCourse to listEnrolledLearnersWithName).
confirmed.breaks_at: A tutor with 150 learners and about 40 submissions each loads about 6k wide rows (several MB) per dashboard or caseload open, and the tutor dashboard is the page tutors keep open. As the number of tutors grows, N tutors x this query is concurrent load on the 10-connection pool. The admin variants (getTutorCaseload for ADMIN, course-view with an admin roster of 5,000) load 200k rows per request with no pagination. The roster.find loop is 5,000 x 1,000 = 5M comparisons for an admin.
confirmed.fix: 1) Add a lean variant (getSubmissionStatusRowsForLearners) selecting only the columns the pipeline needs, with no files/comment/feedback; keep the heavy variant only for detail views. 2) Add courseId as an optional filter to the query and pass it from getTutorCourseContent; for single-assessment views use getSubmissionsForAssessment. 3) Compute 'assignments' from one query over the lessons of the roster courses (jsonb_array_length of the assessment-kind elements) and reuse the already-loaded itemsByLesson instead of reloading. 4) Replace roster.find with a Map. 5) Paginate the caseload learner list (limit/offset or keyset) and the grid (getAssessmentSubmissions returns every learner plus a versions[] array per learner); keep summary counts in SQL.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor dashboard, caseload list and learner detail, course content view and submissions grid. Allocation scoping must stay: the learner id set still comes only from listLearnersForTutor or listAllocatedLearnerIdsForCourse, so filtering and pagination must never be done in a way that bypasses it (never accept learnerIds from the client). The grid UI currently expects the full rows array and a summary over the whole roster, so pagination needs the summary computed separately or the UI changed. Do not drop the legacy null-assessment-key rows. Watch the learner-detail endpoint, which does need files and feedback.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. computePipelineForRoster, getTutorCaseload and getTutorCourseContent all load wide rows (files, comment, feedback, titles). getTutorCourseContent (course-view.ts:104) fetches submissions for ALL courses though one course is shown. caseload.ts:112 has roster.find in a loop. But a tutor's roster is allocation-bounded (about 150 learners, so about 1-6k rows), so this is not high for tutors. The large cases are the ADMIN variants (listAllocatedLearnersForOrg, the enrolled roster in course-view), which are rarer.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The lean variant, the courseId filter (lesson->course is 1:1, so it is safe) and the Map replacement are all safe. Do NOT reuse the already-loaded itemsByLesson for stats.assignments: it only covers lessons that have submissions, while assignments counts every lesson of the roster's courses, so the number would silently drop. Use a separate lean query over the course lessons' documents. Paginating the caseload or grid needs the summary computed over the whole allocated roster, with learner ids still derived server-side from listLearnersForTutor / visibleLearnerIdsForCourse.

confirmed.title: Org-wide progression / learners report: unpaginated, uncached, and each course's verdict set is queried twice per run
confirmed.current: getOrgProgression loads every org learner, then for each target course runs buildCourseCatalog, buildCoursePassSet and getCourseProgressReport in parallel. getCourseProgressReport itself calls getLatestMarkedResultsForCourse and buildCoursePassSet calls the very same query again, so the DISTINCT ON over all final verdicts of the course runs twice. Each report also loads enrolled learners, completions, units and lesson docs. The result (one row per learner, 5,000 rows) is returned to the client with no pagination, and /reports/learners recomputes everything on every hit (it has no cache, unlike /admin-overview). The admin overview then repeats the same getCourseProgressReport per published course.
confirmed.breaks_at: A course with 5,000 learners x 30 units has up to 150k verdict rows per course, read twice; with 5 courses that is about 1.5M rows transferred and aggregated in JS per page view, repeated for every admin refresh. Response payload is about 1 MB+ for rows alone. Concurrent Promise.all across courses multiplies pool pressure.
confirmed.fix: 1) Build one 'course progress' function that returns passed/total/currentPosition plus workbook/casestudy counts from a single pass, and derive the pass set from the same result rows instead of re-querying. 2) Move the per-learner counts into one SQL query per course (count of passed assessment items per learner joined to the course's assessment catalog) or a materialised view refreshed on result.recorded. 3) Paginate and sort server-side (limit/offset plus course filter plus search) for the Learner-Progressions table; compute the report aggregates (distribution buckets, atRisk) in SQL. 4) Cache with Redis plus single-flight like the overview.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin/Manager Learner-Progressions page and Learners report; the tutor progression list uses the same buildProgressionForRoster, so keep the roster parameter. Must preserve: DEACTIVATED learners excluded; course filter drops learners not enrolled; target course = most recent enrolment when no filter; legacy per-unit fallback for units with no tagged assessments (passed.has(lessonId::'')); exempt/optional units excluded from the denominator. The front-end table must be adapted to paged data. Tutors keep seeing only allocated learners because listLearnersForTutor still defines the roster.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. getCourseProgressReport calls getLatestMarkedResultsForCourse (reports.ts:~288) and buildCoursePassSet (progression.ts:123-130) calls the same query again, so the DISTINCT ON runs twice per target course. /reports/learners is uncached and returns an unpaginated list. The scale math is overstated: the verdict set is one row per (learner, lesson, assessment) for the TARGET courses only (each learner's primary course unless filtered), not learners x all courses x 30 units. getOrgProgression is ADMIN-only, so it is not an admin-and-manager page.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Deduplicating is safe and easy: have getCourseProgressReport also return its results array, or accept pre-fetched results, then build the pass set from it in progression.ts. Same query, same semantics. Treat pagination and SQL aggregation as a separate, larger step, since getLearnersReport needs the full row set for its buckets and atRisk list. Add Redis/in-memory TTL plus single-flight like the overview.

confirmed.title: Per-unit sequential round trips (2 queries per unit) in progress, completion and unlock logic; the same progress is recomputed 3x per learner home load and inside the marking transaction
confirmed.current: hasLearnerPassedUnit does getAssessmentKeysForLesson (1 query on lesson.documents) and then getLatestMarkedResult(s) (1 more query). computeLearnerCourseProgress, isCourseComplete and getCourseUnlockMap call it in an awaited for-loop, once per non-exempt unit. Each course costs 1 (units) + 2N + 1 (completion) serial round trips. The learner home triggers it three times: /courses/enrolled (overlayResultDerivedProgress per course), /lms/dashboard (per enrolled course, plus getLearnerAssignments which runs getCourseUnlockMap per course), and the tutor-feedback status poll (computePassedUnits). recordResult runs recordCompletionIfComplete inside a DB transaction, so the 2N serial queries hold a pooled connection while a tutor saves a verdict.
confirmed.breaks_at: For a 30-unit course, about 62 serial queries per course per call at about 3-8 ms each is 0.2-0.5 s of connection time. A learner with 3 courses opening home triggers about 3 x 3 x 62 = about 560 queries. With 2,000 learners active in an hour that is about 1M queries/hour of pure overhead, saturating the 10-connection pool. Marking a Pass holds a transaction connection for the whole walk.
confirmed.fix: Add one batched primitive, getPassedLessonIdsForLearnerCourse(learnerId, courseId, client): a single query (lesson docs for the course via getAssessmentKeysByLesson, plus the DISTINCT ON latest FINAL verdict per (lesson, assessment_key) filtered by learner_id and course_id) and evaluate the pass predicate in memory with the same keys.every / legacy-null rule that assembleReportRows already uses. Use it in computeLearnerCourseProgress, isCourseComplete, getCourseUnlockMap and isUnitUnlocked. Then make the /lms home endpoints share one computed result (a small per-request or Redis memo keyed by learner:course with a TTL of 15-30 s, invalidated in recordResult) so enrolled-courses, dashboard and tutor-feedback do not each recompute.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner home, My Learning cards, course outline lock hints, completion trigger and certificate/completion audit. This is the single source of truth for pass/complete: parity with hasLearnerPassedUnit is critical (a unit passes iff EVERY tagged assessment has a passing latest FINAL verdict; units with no tagged assessments use the legacy highest-version-with-a-result rule that ignores assessment binding and the final/draft split; Refer after Pass overrides). Run it inside the same tx client in recordResult so read-your-writes still sees the just-recorded Pass. Caching must be invalidated on result entry or the learner sees stale progress. There is a unit test surface (progress/completion/unlock tests), so extend those for equivalence.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. hasLearnerPassedUnit (coursework.ts:~459) does getAssessmentKeysForLesson then a results query, so 2 queries per unit. computeLearnerCourseProgress (progress.ts:80-94, not 296-310 as cited), isCourseComplete (completion.ts:29-41) and getCourseUnlockMap loop over units sequentially. recordResult runs recordCompletionIfComplete inside runInTransaction (marking.ts), so the 2N serial queries hold a pooled connection. The same progress is recomputed by /courses/enrolled (overlayResultDerivedProgress), /lms/dashboard (plus getLearnerAssignments) and the tutor-feedback status path. The unit count per course is not verified, but the per-unit round-trip pattern itself is real.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: PARITY TRAP in the proposed fix. It says to use 'the same keys.every / legacy-null rule that assembleReportRows uses', but that is NOT equivalent to hasLearnerPassedUnit. For a unit with no tagged assessments, hasLearnerPassedUnit uses getLatestMarkedResult: the highest-VERSION submission with ANY result row, no final/verdict filter, any assessment_key. assembleReportRows only looks at FINAL + verdict + null-key rows. The batched primitive must reproduce getLatestMarkedResult exactly for untagged units. Draft feedback rows can currently decide a legacy unit. Filter by the course's lessonIds (as the existing per-lesson queries do), not only submission.course_id. Accept a DbOrTxClient so recordResult stays read-your-writes inside the tx. Skip the Redis memo: batching alone cuts about 62 queries to about 4, and a cache adds invalidation risk on a pass/complete path. Extend the existing progress/completion/unlock tests with old-vs-new equivalence cases (untagged unit with a draft result, Refer after Pass, null key).

confirmed.title: 30-second unit-time beat runs the full course-content-lock query plus two upserts for every active learner
confirmed.current: Each PUT /:lessonId/time (one per ~30 s per learner with a lesson open) passes authMiddleware and courseMemberMiddleware, then assertEnrolledStudentContentAccess, which runs getCourseById + getCourseProgress (4-5 queries) + getCourseContentItems (a UNION ALL over sections/lessons/exercises with per-row EXISTS subqueries and regexp_replace over lesson_language.content HTML for hasNoteContent) just to decide whether the lesson is locked. Then addUnitTimeSpent does two sequential upserts (unit_time_spent and unit_time_monthly).
confirmed.breaks_at: 1,000 concurrent learners = 33 beats/s; each beat is about 8-10 queries including the heavy content-items UNION with HTML regex scans, so about 300 qps of mostly wasteful reads plus 66 upserts/s into two small hot tables. Row-lock contention on a learner's own unit_time rows is minimal, but the regex/UNION scan is CPU on the Supabase instance, and p95 for real requests degrades.
confirmed.fix: The beat is only reachable from a lesson page the learner already loaded under the content-read and unlock guards, so replace assertEnrolledStudentContentAccess here with a lightweight check: is the actor an enrolled STUDENT of this course (one indexed query, or reuse courseMemberMiddleware's result) and optionally isUnitUnlocked. Fold the two upserts into one round trip (single statement with two CTEs, or a multi-statement via one query). Optionally buffer beats in Redis (HINCRBY learner:lesson, flush every 60-120 s from the jobs worker) to cut writes by 4-10x.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner study-time tracking, which feeds the tutor progression 'time per unit' and the admin study-hours chart. Dropping the lock check means a learner could accrue time on a locked unit if they craft the request (cosmetic only, per-beat cap of 120 s and rate limit still apply), so keep a cheap isUnitUnlocked if exactness matters. Redis buffering adds an eventual-consistency window and a flush failure mode, and the jobs worker must own the flush; keep it behind a flag. Staff and manager beats are already skipped.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. PUT /:lessonId/time (lesson.ts:372-405) runs authMiddleware, courseMemberMiddleware (2+ queries), then assertEnrolledStudentContentAccess. That runs getCourseById, getCourseProgress and getCourseContentItems (the UNION ALL with per-lesson EXISTS plus regexp_replace over lesson_language.content, content.ts:31-153) in Promise.all, then annotateCourseContentWithProgression adds about 4 more queries for students. Staff and managers also pay the 3 heavy queries, because the LEARNER check happens after the assert. This is the highest-frequency endpoint (every 30s per open lesson).
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The proposed replacement is unsafe as written. (1) The current check also guarantees the lessonId belongs to this courseId (404 otherwise). unit_time_spent is keyed (learner, lesson) and the courseId comes from the URL, so a lessonId from another course would write time under the wrong course and corrupt the tutor 'time per unit' and the per-course study totals. A replacement must verify lesson.course_id = :courseId. (2) The stock progression lock (progressionMode 'sequential') is dropped too. Safe minimal fix: skip the assert entirely when actor.role !== 'LEARNER' (an immediate win, since staff pay 3 heavy queries for nothing), and for learners use one query that checks an enrolled STUDENT groupmember plus lesson.course_id = :courseId. Optionally add isUnitUnlocked. Keep the second (unit_time_monthly) upsert separate: it is deliberately best-effort in a try/catch, and merging it into one statement would couple its failure to the authoritative total. Redis buffering is not needed yet.

confirmed.title: Announcement/notification fan-out is a serial per-recipient loop executed inside the HTTP request
confirmed.current: publishAnnouncement awaits emitNotification, which for each recipient sequentially does insertNotification (1 insert), getNotificationPreference (1 select), optionally hasRecentUnreadForEntity (1 select) and enqueueTransactionalEmail (a Redis/BullMQ call). Nothing is batched and the loop runs before the response returns. recordResult also emits one emitNotification per newly unlocked unit in a loop.
confirmed.breaks_at: An all_learners broadcast to 5,000 learners is about 10k-15k serial DB round trips (about 3-10 ms each = 30-150 s) plus 5,000 enqueues inside the request, which will exceed proxy/Caddy/client timeouts (the admin sees an error although the announcement row exists, and a retry duplicates it). It holds one pool connection for minutes while the rest of the pool serves everything else.
confirmed.fix: 1) Bulk-insert notification rows in chunks (about 500 per statement) with INSERT ... SELECT. 2) Fetch email preferences for all recipients in one query (WHERE user_id IN (...) AND category = ...), and resolve the default in memory. 3) Replace per-recipient hasRecentUnreadForEntity with one grouped query. 4) Return 202 from publish and do the fan-out in the jobs worker (BullMQ job with announcement id, chunked, idempotent via the existing idempotency key and a unique (user_id, type, entity_id) guard), so the request is O(1).
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin broadcast compose, learner and tutor notification bell, email opt-in. Preserve: in-app row ALWAYS written; email only if a template is given, an address exists, the preference is on (defaulting to config) and the coalescing window has not suppressed it; one recipient's failure must not stop the rest (today try/catch per recipient). Keep announcement scoping: all_learners uses getOrgLearnerIds, course uses getEnrolledLearnerIds, tutor-targeted uses allocation, so visibility rules are unchanged. Async delivery means the publish response can no longer report delivery counts, so the UI needs a 'queued' state.
confirmed.verifier_note: The serial per-recipient loop inside the HTTP request is real (notify.ts:45-95 awaited from announcements.ts:194). But the stated per-recipient cost is wrong. publishAnnouncement builds recipients as { userId, emailFields } with NO email (announcements.ts:196), so emitNotification hits 'if (!recipient.email) continue' and skips the preference lookup, the coalesce check and the enqueue. Each recipient costs exactly one INSERT, not 2-3 queries plus an enqueue. 5k recipients is about 5k serial inserts (roughly 15-50s), which is slow and a timeout risk but not 10-15k round trips. recordResult's session.unlocked loop is typically 1 unit per pass, so that part is not a concern.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: A chunked multi-row INSERT (about 500 per statement, 4 columns) is enough and keeps the request synchronous and ordered: 5k rows becomes about 10 statements. No queue is required. Do NOT add a global unique (user_id, type, entity_id) on notification: other types (session.unlocked, message coalescing) rely on repeats. If idempotency is wanted, scope it to type='announcement.published'. Batch the email-preference and coalescing queries only when the email leg is actually wired for announcements. Keep per-recipient failure isolation (insert in chunks, fall back to per-row on a chunk error).

confirmed.title: getCourseStats multiplies students x lessons x completions in a single join (cartesian blow-up) on the org dashboard
confirmed.current: The subquery joins course to group to groupmember (all students) LEFT JOIN lesson (all lessons) LEFT JOIN lesson_completion on (lesson_id, profile_id), then COUNT(DISTINCT ...) FILTER over the product, grouped by course. Row count per course = students x lessons. getOrganisationAnalytics runs it on every call with no cache (only the login-activity chart is cached).
confirmed.breaks_at: A course with 5,000 learners and 100 lessons produces 500k intermediate rows per course before DISTINCT aggregation (sort/hash spill), several courses = millions. Query time climbs from ms to tens of seconds and blocks a pool slot.
confirmed.fix: Aggregate each dimension separately in subqueries/CTEs (students per course, lessons per course, completed lessons per course via GROUP BY lesson.course_id, certificates per course) and join the small results; or read from the existing dash_org_stats materialisation. Wrap the service result in the same Redis TTL cache used for login activity (60-300 s).
confirmed.flow_risk: Org admin dashboard 'top courses' card (completion %, certification %). Results must stay identical: totalStudents is COUNT(DISTINCT groupmember.id) with role 3, completion % = completed lessons / (students x lessons), limit 5 ordered by completed lessons. Only ACTIVE courses are included. Low blast radius (read only, admin page).
confirmed.verifier_note: The join in dash.ts:22-60 (groupmember x lesson x lessonCompletion, COUNT DISTINCT) is a real students x lessons row blow-up per course, and getOrganisationAnalytics has no cache. But realistic sizes (1k students x 30 lessons = 30k rows/course, with the LIMIT 5 applied after the subquery, which aggregates ALL active courses) cost tens to hundreds of ms, not tens of seconds. It is a stock ClassroomIO admin card on /stats (manager/admin, requireSameOrg). Low blast radius.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Semantics trap: the outer query ORDERs BY completedLessons ASC (the inner DESC is discarded), so the card currently shows the 5 LEAST-completed courses, not the top ones. A rewrite 'must stay identical' would preserve that, so decide explicitly whether to keep or fix it. Aggregate each dimension separately (students per course, lesson count per course, completed lessons via lesson_completion joined to lesson group by course, certs), then join. Keep role 3 only, ACTIVE courses only, and the COUNT(DISTINCT groupmember.id) semantics.

confirmed.title: Material download and lesson-read guards repeat full-course scans and run isUnitUnlocked (3-5 queries) per requested key
confirmed.current: assertCourseMaterialDownloadAccess calls getCourseMaterialKeys(courseId) and getMaterialKeyLessonMap(courseId), two separate full reads of every lesson's documents and videos jsonb in the course, then loops over the requested keys and awaits isUnitUnlocked for each one. isUnitUnlocked re-reads getCourseSequentialUnlock, getOrderedUnitsForCourse and hasLearnerPassedUnit (2 queries) every time, with no caching between iterations of the same request. requireCourseContentRead also runs canReadCourseContent (enrolment query + getCourseById) and isUnitUnlocked on every lesson GET.
confirmed.breaks_at: A lesson with 8 materials opened by a learner costs about 2 full jsonb scans + 8 x (1+1+2) = about 34 queries per presign call, plus the same again if the page presigns per file. 1,000 concurrent learners downloading materials is tens of thousands of queries/min against tables whose rows carry large jsonb.
confirmed.fix: Fetch lessons once, build the key to lessonId map and the key set from the same row set (one query), de-duplicate lessonIds, and evaluate isUnitUnlocked once per distinct lesson with the course's ordered units and sequentialUnlock flag loaded once. With the batched pass-set from the progress fix, one extra query decides all locks.
