Cache course-level static data (ordered units, sequentialUnlock, material key map) in a short-TTL Redis/in-memory cache invalidated on lesson/course update.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner lesson page, material and video presigning, sequential-unlock enforcement (the control, not just presentation). Do not weaken: coursework/ keys must still be rejected here, non-staff keys must be current materials of this course, locked-unit materials must stay 403, staff bypass unchanged. If a cache is added, an author editing or removing a material must invalidate it immediately, otherwise a removed file stays downloadable. This runs on the hot learner path, so test unlocked, locked and optional/exempt units.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed in ownership.ts:298-312: getCourseMaterialKeys and getMaterialKeyLessonMap are two full reads of every lesson's documents/videos jsonb, then isUnitUnlocked is awaited per requested key. Each call is getCourseSequentialUnlock (1) and, when sequential unlock is on, getOrderedUnitsForCourse (1) plus hasLearnerPassedUnit (2). The '34 queries' figure only holds with sequential unlock ON and distinct lessons. With unlock OFF it is about 1 query per key. Multiple keys from the same lesson repeat the full walk. It is on the learner hot path.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: One lesson scan building both the key set and the key->lessonId map, and evaluating isUnitUnlocked once per DISTINCT lessonId, are safe. Do NOT cache the current material key set (even with a short TTL). It is the security control that makes a removed or cross-course material unretrievable, and cache invalidation across author edits is the risk. Caching only the ordered units and the sequentialUnlock flag is acceptable if invalidated on course/lesson update. Keep the coursework/ rejection, staff bypass and default-deny currency check as they are.

confirmed.title: Bulk enrolment/import paths issue unbounded parallel single-row inserts, a possibly over-limit multi-row insert, and per-learner N+1 compliance checks; none is transactional
confirmed.current: Cohort enrolment does Promise.all(toInsert.map(addCohortMember)): one INSERT per learner-cohort pair, all fired at once. Course people add does Promise.all(members.map(addCourseMember)) where each call also runs getCourseGroupId first (2 queries per member). enrollAudienceStudentProfilesInCourses builds pairs = profiles x groups and sends one addGroupMembers INSERT of all pairs (postgres limit is 65,534 bind parameters, about 16k rows at 4 columns) with no chunking. ensureComplianceEnrollmentRecordsForProfiles loops courses x learners with getLatestComplianceRecordsByProfiles per learner (N+1). None of it runs in a transaction, so a mid-way failure leaves partial enrolment, and the follow-up emails assume success.
confirmed.breaks_at: Importing 5,000 learners into 4 courses = 20k pairs x 4 columns = 80k parameters, so the single insert fails outright (bind-parameter overflow) and nothing is enrolled; a cohort import fires 5,000 concurrent inserts on a pool of 10 and starves the site for the duration. Compliance enrolment adds 2 queries x 5,000 x courses.
confirmed.fix: Chunk inserts (about 1,000 rows, so under 16k params) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING instead of select-then-insert, in one transaction per course/cohort (runInTransaction). Resolve groupId once, outside the loop. Convert the compliance loop to a batch: fetch latest records for all profileIds in one call (getLatestComplianceRecordsByProfiles already accepts an array), then insert missing rows in bulk. Where the request is large (more than a few hundred rows) hand the work to a BullMQ job.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin audience import, cohort membership, course people tab, compliance enrolment. Keep: unique (group_id, profile_id) and email constraints (use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and compute counts from RETURNING); welcome-email idempotency keys (audience-course-welcome:{group}:{profile}); only org STUDENT members are enrolled; alreadyEnrolled and assigned counts the UI shows. Moving to a transaction changes partial-failure behavior (all or nothing), which is desirable but should be called out. Do not alter tutor allocation, which this path does not create.
confirmed.verifier_note: The code patterns are real (audience.ts:283 Promise.all of single inserts, a single addGroupMembers insert, no transaction, compliance N+1). But the stated breakage is not reachable: ZAssignAudienceCourses caps profileIds at .max(500), and ZImportAudienceMembers caps recipientCsv at 25,000 chars (about 700-1,000 recipients). 5,000 learners x 4 courses = 20k pairs cannot be submitted in one request. The 65,534-parameter overflow (4 params/row, about 16k rows) needs roughly 1,000 learners x 17+ courses (allCourses=true). The compliance N+1 only runs for COMPLIANCE-type courses and is bounded by the same caps. The cohort Promise.all queues behind the pool of 10 for a short time, bounded by the 500-1000 cap.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Low-cost hardening only. Chunk addGroupMembers at about 1,000 rows with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (unique(group_id, profile_id) exists) inside one runInTransaction per call. Convert cohort inserts to a single chunked insert. Batch the compliance lookup via the existing array-accepting getLatestComplianceRecordsByProfiles. No BullMQ move is needed at current caps. Preserve the welcome-email idempotency keys and the assigned/alreadyEnrolled counts the UI shows.

confirmed.title: Allocation admin screens cap pickers at 100 users and return all allocations unpaginated
confirmed.current: getAssignablePeople fetches the first page of 100 ACTIVE tutors and 100 ACTIVE learners (getOrganizationUsers limit 100, ordered by member id desc) with no search or next page. listOrgAllocations returns every tutor_allocation row in the org with two profile joins and no limit. getOrganizationUsers also issues a separate COUNT with ILIKE '%search%' on three unindexed columns.
confirmed.breaks_at: With more than 100 learners or tutors, the allocation picker silently omits everyone beyond the newest 100, so an admin cannot allocate older or other learners (a functional failure at scale, not just slowness), and the unallocated-learners alert in the overview cannot be actioned for them. The allocations table at 5,000+ rows returns a multi-hundred-KB payload per load. ILIKE %term% scans the whole member and profile set (about 5-20k rows, fine now, degrading with growth).
confirmed.fix: Replace the two 100-row dumps with server-side typeahead (search param, limit 20, keyset by id) for learners and tutors, reusing the existing searchOrgAudience pattern; paginate listOrgAllocations (limit/offset plus tutorId and learnerId filter and search). Add a pg_trgm GIN index on profile.fullname and profile.email if ILIKE search stays.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin/Manager allocation management UI, which needs a front-end change (combobox with async search, paged table). Server validation in createTutorAllocation (role checks via getOrgMemberRoleId, 409 on duplicate pair, audit) already guards correctness and must not change. This does not touch tutor visibility: tutors still see only tutor_allocation rows.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed and the most functionally important finding: getAssignablePeople (allocation.ts:38-41) calls getOrganizationUsers with limit 100 (and the function itself clamps at Math.min(limit,100)), ordered by member id DESC, with no search or paging. Beyond 100 active learners or 100 tutors the picker silently omits the older ones, so an admin cannot allocate them. Because tutors see ONLY allocated learners (ACCESS.md section 8), those learners become permanently unreachable by any tutor and just sit in the unallocated list. This is correctness-at-scale, not only performance. listOrgAllocations is also unpaginated.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Use server-side typeahead (the existing getOrganizationUsers already supports search/page) with a requireManagerOrAdmin route, limit 20 and an org-scoped role filter, and keep the existing createTutorAllocation role validation (getOrgMemberRoleId, 409 duplicate, audit) untouched. Paginate listOrgAllocations with tutorId/learnerId/search filters. A bulk allocation endpoint (many learners to one tutor) would help the 'unallocated learners' alert flow. pg_trgm is optional at this size.

confirmed.title: getLastSeenForUserIds scans login events and sessions for up to 5,000 ids on every pipeline/progression call, and swallows errors into false 'never logged in' stats
confirmed.current: For each call it runs two GROUP BY ... MAX queries (analytics_login_events and session) with inArray(user_id, ids). analytics_login_events gets one row per user per day, so it only grows. The result is recomputed per tutor in the admin overview (100 x) and per page view. On any error it catches, logs, and returns a map of nulls.
confirmed.breaks_at: After a year, 5,000 learners x 365 days = about 1.8M login rows aggregated per call; the admin overview triggers up to 1 + 100 such calls. On a transient DB error every learner reports 'never logged in' and 'inactive' counts and the at-risk list are silently wrong.
confirmed.fix: Denormalise last_seen_at onto profile (one timestamptz), updated by the login hook and the heartbeat at most once per few minutes (a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE last_seen_at < now() - interval '5 minutes'), then read it with the profile rows already being fetched. Until then, add an index on analytics_login_events(user_id, logged_in_at desc) and compute per-tutor stats from the single org-wide pass. Do not swallow the error: let it propagate or mark stats degraded.
confirmed.flow_risk: Activity buckets (active/inactive/never/suspended) on tutor and admin dashboards, the learners report 'at risk' list, and 'active in 7d/30d'. Backfill last_seen_at from MAX(login, session) at migration time so history is preserved; the 30-day threshold and 'created' state (no login ever) must read the same. Changing error behavior may surface 500s where it used to show zeros; handle it in the UI.
confirmed.verifier_note: The error-swallowing is real and the most serious part: analytics.ts:117-120 catches any error and returns all-null, so on a transient DB error every learner reads 'never logged in'/inactive and at-risk lists are silently wrong. The scan cost is real but overstated. Per-tutor calls partition the roster (about 2x org total, not 100x). The suggested index on analytics_login_events(user_id, ...) already effectively exists: idx_analytics_login_events_user_id plus a unique (user_id, logged_in_date) used by trackLoginHook's ON CONFLICT. Row growth of 5k x 365 = 1.8M is right. The session half has NO user_id index (schema.ts:113-130; see missed).
confirmed.fix_adjustment: First change: stop swallowing errors (rethrow or return a 'degraded' flag), which is a tiny change. Skip the new login-events index. Add session(user_id) instead. The denormalised profile.last_seen_at is the right end state but needs a backfill from MAX(login, session) and writes in both the login hook and heartbeat (conditional UPDATE), so keep the 30-day and 'created' (never logged in) semantics identical.

confirmed.title: 60-second presence heartbeat writes session.updated_at for every open tab; Online-now query reads sessions with a join
confirmed.current: POST /heartbeat (client ping every 60 s) runs authMiddleware (per-request actor/org lookups) and then UPDATE session SET updated_at = now() WHERE id = ... The prod stats show about 33k session updated_at writes already with 1 org and about 40 learners. getOnlineOrgMembers joins session, profile, organizationmember with a GROUP BY and MAX per poll (the admin dashboard polls every 45 s).
confirmed.breaks_at: 2,000 concurrent tabs = 33 UPDATEs/s (about 2M row updates/day) on a table that is also the auth session store, each a dead tuple and WAL record, with autovacuum pressure on the table every request reads. Each heartbeat also pays the full per-request auth/actor lookup chain.
confirmed.fix: Keep presence in Redis: SET presence:{org}:{user} with a 5-minute TTL (or ZADD with timestamp) from the heartbeat, and let getOnlineNow read the ZSET (ZRANGEBYSCORE) plus a single profile lookup for the names; stop touching the session row except at login/refresh. If it must stay in Postgres, make the UPDATE conditional (WHERE updated_at < now() - interval '2 minutes') and widen the heartbeat to 2-3 minutes with an online window of 5-7.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin 'Online now' panel and any code that treats session.updated_at as last activity (getLastSeenForUserIds reads MAX(session.updated_at), so it must keep working or move to the last_seen_at column). Redis outage must degrade gracefully (empty panel) without failing the heartbeat. Does not affect auth sessions, because better-auth owns its own refresh of updated_at.
confirmed.verifier_note: touchSession (account.ts:117-124, users.ts) does one primary-key UPDATE per tab per 60s, and getOnlineOrgMembers joins session/profile/organizationmember with GROUP BY. Real, but 33 single-row updates/s is trivial for Postgres (session.updated_at is not indexed, so these are HOT-eligible). The larger cost per heartbeat is the unconditional per-request identity lookups in the global middleware (see missed), not the UPDATE itself.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do the one-line conditional UPDATE (WHERE updated_at < now() - interval '45 seconds') and keep the 5-min online window. A Redis ZSET is unnecessary now and would break getLastSeenForUserIds, which reads MAX(session.updated_at) for activity buckets, unless last_seen_at is moved at the same time. Do not touch better-auth's own session refresh.

confirmed.title: Several list reads are unbounded and sort whole histories (tutor inbox, announcements, org tutor/learner lists, grid versions)
confirmed.current: listConversationsForParticipant runs SELECT DISTINCT ON (thread_id) across ALL messages in all of the participant's threads (sort by thread_id, created_at desc), with no limit. getLearnerMessageSummary does the same plus a count join on every learner home load. listAnnouncementsForOrg, listAnnouncementsForLearner and ForTutor return all non-deleted announcements with no LIMIT. listOrgLearners (selectDistinct plus ORDER BY fullname) and listOrgTutors return every row. getSubmissionsForAssessment returns every version row with files/feedback jsonb for the whole roster.
confirmed.breaks_at: A tutor with 200 learners x 100 messages = 20k rows sorted just to show a list of 200 threads each time the inbox opens. A year of weekly broadcasts is only about 50 rows now but grows without bound, and 5,000-row learner/tutor lists are materialised as selectDistinct on every admin call.
confirmed.fix: Add a last_message_at / last_message_body (or last_message_id) denormalised onto message_thread, maintained in insertMessage, so the inbox is a plain indexed ORDER BY last_message_at LIMIT 50 (keyset). Compute unread counts with a per-thread cursor aggregate limited to threads with last_message_at > last_read_at. Add LIMIT/keyset to announcement lists (admin: paged; learner/tutor: latest 50) and index announcement(organization_id, published_at desc). Drop DISTINCT where a unique index already guarantees uniqueness (listOrgLearners on organizationmember joined by profile id).
confirmed.flow_risk: Messaging inbox (tutor, learner), learner home message widget, announcements pages. Messaging rules must stay: participant-only access, archived threads read-only but still listed, threads with no messages omitted, unread = other party's message after read cursor (null cursor = unread). A denormalised last_message column must be backfilled and kept consistent in the same transaction as insertMessage. Announcement visibility (all_learners / enrolled published course / targeted learner / allocated tutor) is query-enforced, so keep that predicate intact when adding LIMIT.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: listConversationsForParticipant and getLearnerMessageSummary (message.ts:~128-232) DISTINCT ON over ALL messages in the participant's threads, with no limit. message_thread is unique per (tutor, learner) pair, so a learner has few threads but an unbounded history, and the learner-home summary runs on every home load. Announcement lists have no LIMIT. These are real but only bite after long histories.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: A LATERAL 'latest message per thread' (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1) with an index on message(thread_id, created_at desc) gets the same result with no denormalised column to keep consistent. Add LIMIT/keyset to announcement lists while keeping the audience predicate intact. Keep: archived threads read-only but listed, threads with no messages omitted, null read cursor = unread. Do not drop DISTINCT in listOrgLearners unless uniqueness per profile is guaranteed (one org member row per profile).

confirmed.title: Enrolment lookups by profile_id have no usable index on groupmember (unique indexes all lead with group_id)
confirmed.current: groupmember has only unique(group_id, profile_id), unique(group_id, email) and unique(group_id, profile_id, email). Hot queries filter by profile_id alone or inArray(profile_id, ids) with role_id = 3: getEnrolledCourses (every learner home), getEnrolmentsForLearners and getCoursesForLearners (every tutor/admin dashboard and progression), listAnnouncementsForLearner, isCourseGroupMember (course-member middleware on every course request), isCourseTutorForLearner/isTutorAllocatedToCourse. These cannot use a (group_id, profile_id) btree for a profile_id-leading predicate, so they sequentially scan groupmember. This matches the advisor's 103 unindexed foreign keys. Also coursework_submission has no (course_id, lesson_id, assessment_key) composite for the grid and course report reads, which rely on idx_coursework_submission_course.
confirmed.breaks_at: groupmember grows with learners x courses (+ tutors), so 5,000 x 4 = 20-50k rows. One seq scan is about 2-10 ms, but it runs on most authenticated learner requests (course-member middleware) and in loops, so it becomes the top CPU consumer on the DB before row counts look large. Combined with the advisor's unused-index and FK warnings it also inflates write cost.
confirmed.fix: Migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_groupmember_profile_role ON groupmember (profile_id, role_id) INCLUDE (group_id); add coursework_submission (course_id, lesson_id, assessment_key, learner_id) INCLUDE (version, submission_type). Verify with EXPLAIN against pg_stat_statements top queries first, and drop the unused indexes the advisor lists in the same change window.
confirmed.flow_risk: Pure additive indexes: no behavior change. Risks are operational: run CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction (Drizzle migration runner must not wrap it), run via the session pooler :5432 not :6543, and apply off-peak because index builds on a small droplet-fronted DB add I/O. Dropping 'unused' indexes should be a separate, verified step: some back FK cascades (deleting a profile cascades into groupmember, coursework_submission, tutor_allocation) and are only 'unused' because traffic is tiny today.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: groupmember only has unique(group_id, profile_id), unique(group_id, email) and unique(group_id, profile_id, email) (schema.ts:1320-1322), so profile_id-only predicates (getEnrolledCourses, getEnrolmentsForLearners, getCoursesForLearners, announcement/allocation lookups) cannot use an index. But the finding's example of the course-member middleware is WRONG: isUserCourseMemberOrOrgAdmin joins course.group_id so it filters on (group_id, profile_id), which the unique index serves. So the hottest middleware path is not a seq scan. coursework_submission also lacks a (course_id, lesson_id, assessment_key) composite. The strongest benefit is the learner home and tutor/admin dashboards, not every request.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Additive and safe. Because the tables are small (tens of thousands of rows), a plain CREATE INDEX is fine for this one-org DB, so CONCURRENTLY is not required (and Drizzle's transactional migration runner cannot run it). Add (profile_id, role_id) INCLUDE (group_id) on groupmember and (course_id, lesson_id, assessment_key) on coursework_submission. Verify with EXPLAIN. Treat dropping the 74 'unused' indexes as a separate step, since several back FK cascades and look unused only because traffic is tiny.

confirmed.title: Root layout reruns on EVERY navigation and fires /organization/first + an OG-image 'warm' call: this is the source of the ~335k organization / organization_plan / 'order by created_at limit 1' queries and the storage.objects lookups
confirmed.current: Root +layout.server.ts calls getOrgSiteInfo() on every run. Self-hosted (PUBLIC_IS_SELFHOSTED=true) => getFirstOrg() => GET /organization/first => getFirstOrganizationWithPlans(): query 1 'select id from organization order by created_at limit 1', query 2 organization LEFT JOIN organization_plan. That is exactly the 335k 'order by created_at limit 1' + organization + organization_plan trio. Then, because isOrgSite is true, line 28-43 fires an un-awaited fetch to the API OG endpoint (resolveOrgSiteOgWarmUrl -> /org-site/og/:siteName). That handler runs getOrganizationBySiteName (organization select), getActiveOrganizationPlan (organization_plan select, plus a 2nd organization select for parentOrganizationId when the org has no active plan row), then S3 HeadObject and a full GetObject of the 2x PNG (storage.objects lookups on the Supabase side, ~166k). The load re-executes on every client navigation because getBaseMetaTags uses url.pathname for canonical/og:url (metaTags.server.ts:141-144), which SvelteKit tracks as a dependency; the `url` object is also passed to getOrgSiteInfo. Additionally resolveOrgSiteOgImageUrl does a HEAD to the media CDN (2s timeout) inside the load whenever PUBLIC_MEDIA_CDN_URL is set. Public/anonymous pages (login, org-site) pay all of this too. If persistOrgSiteOgImage returns null (og-cache.ts:60-63 returns before uploading when mediaPublicBaseUrl is unset) or HEAD misses, every warm call falls through to getCloudflarePngBuffer = a paid Cloudflare Browser Rendering screenshot per page view, with no single-flight.
confirmed.breaks_at: Roughly 5-8 DB queries + 3-4 internal HTTP calls + 2 S3 calls per navigation, per user, before any page data. 2,000 concurrent learners clicking once every 20s = ~100 navigations/s = ~500-800 DB qps and ~300 S3 ops/s on the 2 vCPU droplet and a 10-connection pool; it also dominates Supabase storage API load. Bots hitting public pages trigger the same path unauthenticated and the dashboard->API key calls skip the rate limiter (rate-limiter.ts:109-113).
confirmed.fix: (1) Dashboard: module-level TTL cache (60s, single-flight) around getOrgSiteInfo()'s API calls keyed by (selfhosted | siteName | customDomain), so org lookups are 1 call/min/process instead of per navigation. (2) Remove url.pathname/url.origin usage from the server load's tracked deps: compute canonical/og:url on the client from page.url (or in +layout.ts), or return org data from a separate load that does not touch `url` so SvelteKit does not rerun it. (3) Delete the per-request OG warm fetch; instead warm once per process per siteName (Set + 1h TTL) or when the org branding is saved in the API. The OG route is already lazy so first scraper hit still works. (4) API: in-process cache (30s TTL, single-flight) for getFirstOrgForSelfHosted and for getOrganizationBySiteName/getActiveOrganizationPlan used by the OG route; invalidate in updateOrganization / org plan write functions (createOrganizationPlan, updateOrganizationPlan, webhook handlers). (5) OG service: cache {etag,buffer} per siteName in memory/Redis for 5-10 min, add single-flight around getCloudflarePngBuffer, and make persistOrgSiteOgImage log loudly instead of silently returning null. (6) Skip the CDN HEAD in resolveOrgSiteOgImageUrl via a cached result.
confirmed.flow_risk: All roles hit this (login page, every authenticated page). Risk is staleness only: branding/theme/plan changes by an admin show up after <=60s instead of instantly; invalidate the dashboard cache on the org-settings save response path or accept 60s. Custom-domain / subdomain (cloud) branch must keep keys per host so tenants never share an entry (self-hosted today is one org). Do not cache null/error results for more than a few seconds or a transient API blip locks the login page into org=null. Social-share previews must still work: keep the lazy OG route. Moving canonical to the client changes SSR HTML for crawlers: keep canonical server-side using event.url.pathname in a handle/transformPageChunk or hooks-level head injection if SEO matters (it is a closed LMS, likely not).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed in code. Root +layout.server.ts awaits getOrgSiteInfo() on every run. Self-hosted calls GET /organization/first, which runs getFirstOrganizationWithPlans (select id order by created_at limit 1, then organization LEFT JOIN organization_plan). The fire-and-forget OG warm fetch then runs generateOrgSiteOgImage: getOrganizationBySiteName (organization select), getActiveOrganizationPlan (organization_plan select), S3 HeadObject, and a full GetObject of the PNG on an etag match. That trio matches the 335k counts exactly. The load reruns per client navigation because getBaseMetaTags reads url.pathname (metaTags.server.ts:141-144) and url.origin, which SvelteKit tracks. persistOrgSiteOgImage returns null when mediaPublicBaseUrl is unset (og-cache.ts:60-63), so every warm call would render via Cloudflare (a paid screenshot per page view). The OG route has no single-flight. A guard at hooks level also means the API call carries PRIVATE_SERVER_KEY, so it skips the rate limiter. Per-query cost is small (PK/limit), so the severity comes from volume plus the S3/CF side effects, not from query cost.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Delete the per-request warm fetch (the lazy OG route still serves scrapers; the CDN HEAD miss falls back to the API URL). Add a dashboard TTL cache (30-60s, single-flight) for getOrgSiteInfo, keyed per host/siteName. Never cache null or error beyond ~2s. Server-side API cache invalidation cannot reach the dashboard process, so TTL is the only freshness mechanism there. Prefer `untrack` for url.pathname in the server load, or drop canonical/og:url from the server load and build them in +layout.svelte/+layout.ts from page.url. Do not move canonical out of SSR if crawlers matter. Also cache the HEAD result in resolveOrgSiteOgImageUrl. In generateOrgSiteOgImage use an in-memory {etag,buffer} cache plus single-flight so a scraper burst cannot trigger N Cloudflare renders. Do the dashboard-side cache first. The API-side invalidation list is less important once the warm call is gone.

confirmed.title: Every authenticated API request does 3 DB round trips for identity (customSession x2 + resolveActor) and /api/auth/* requests do it twice
confirmed.location: apps/api/src/app.ts:110-153,167-222; packages/db/src/auth.ts:304-325 (customSession); packages/db/src/actor.ts:18-43; packages/db/src/queries/organization/organization.ts:509-529; apps/api/src/middlewares/org-member.ts:4-6, org-admin.ts:7-9, org-team-member.ts:7-9 (stale comments)
confirmed.current: The global middleware calls auth.api.getSession() which, because of the customSession plugin, ALWAYS runs the plugin's fn after the cookie-cache/DB session lookup (custom-session/index.mjs:46-62: the fn runs even on a cookie-cache hit). The fn does getUserOrgRolesMap (select organizationmember by profile_id) + select profile.status. Then app.ts:144 calls resolveActor which re-reads organizationmember JOIN profile for the same user. Comments in auth.ts and org-*.ts claim 'no per-request DB query' and that orgRoles 'refreshes when the cookie cache expires'; that is false, orgRoles/status are re-read every request. So the real cost is 3 queries per request on top of any route queries (matches ~90-110k resolveActor organizationmember+profile lookups in pg_stat_statements, with a parallel set from customSession). Also the global middleware runs for /api/auth/* (e.g. /api/auth/get-session called by the dashboard SSR on every navigation and by the browser on focus) and then the auth handler (app.ts:222) calls getSession again, doubling the cost (about 6 queries per get-session).
confirmed.breaks_at: 3 queries x every API call incl. 60s heartbeat, 60s notification poll, 45s admin summary poll and the SSR get-session. At 3,000 active users ~150-250 req/s => 450-750 identity queries/s, each a ~5-20ms round trip to Supabase through a 10-connection pool (postgres-js max 10): queueing starts around 500-1000 qps and every request slows together.
confirmed.fix: Introduce one cached authz snapshot per user: getAuthzSnapshot(userId) -> { memberships: Record<orgId, roleId>, status }, backed by an in-process LRU (max ~5k entries, TTL 10s, single-flight) with optional Redis as shared L2 (key authz:{userId}, TTL 30s) if the API is ever run as >1 replica. Both customSession (orgRoles/status) and resolveActor (pick membership by cio-org-id, else earliest membership ordered by created_at) derive from it, taking identity cost from 3 queries to ~0 in steady state. Invalidate (delete key) inside the db-layer writers so every caller is covered: changeOrgUserStatus/updateProfile when status present (services/organization/users.ts:217-224), createOrganizationMember(s) (organization.ts:133,196,210), deleteOrganizationMember / AudienceMember (:375,:392), invite.ts:494 role/membership updates, sso-provisioning.ts:71/129/150, account.ts:108. NEVER cache an empty/missing-membership or missing-profile result (so freshly created, auto-joined or invited users are not denied for the TTL). Cross-process writers (apps/jobs) cannot clear the API memory, so the 10s TTL is the ceiling; for hard guarantees publish invalidations on a Redis channel. Separately add a skip in the global middleware for path.startsWith('/api/auth/') (set ANONYMOUS_ACTOR, let the auth handler do its own getSession); signup-guard does not read user/actor. Fix the misleading comments.
confirmed.flow_risk: Highest-risk change in the review because it is the authorization boundary. Preserved properties: deactivation must bite promptly: changeOrgUserStatus already deletes sessions and updateProfile triggers invalidation, so API-originated deactivation is immediate; jobs-originated is <=10s. Role change (tutor<->admin<->student) invalidated at the writer; tutor allocation (ACCESS.md section 8, ad92abcf5) is NOT touched because allocation checks are separate per-route queries (isTutorAllocatedToLearner), keep them uncached or cache only with explicit invalidation. Admin/tutor/learner/manager all pass through here. Edge cases: user in multiple orgs (resolveActor with no cio-org-id header currently picks an arbitrary row because there is no ORDER BY at actor.ts:21-34, make it deterministic); self-hosted auto-join (profile.ts:62-72) inserts membership right after a first /account call: invalidate there; impersonation / view-as-student token flows mint a new session for another user: snapshot is keyed by user id so fine; dashboard getActor consumes customSession status/orgRoles so SSR also becomes <=10s stale unless invalidated. Add a unit test that a deactivate followed immediately by a request returns 401/denied.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. The customSession plugin overrides the getSession endpoint (better-auth custom-session/index.mjs), so auth.api.getSession always runs fn after the base lookup, even on a cookie-cache hit. fn issues getUserOrgRolesMap plus a profile.status select (auth.ts:285-293). app.ts:144 then calls resolveActor (organizationmember JOIN profile). That is 3 identity queries on top of any session lookup. For /api/auth/* the global middleware runs getSession and then auth.handler runs the custom get-session endpoint again, so the work is doubled. The comments claiming 'no per-request DB query' are wrong. resolveActor has no ORDER BY with limit(1) when no cio-org-id header is sent, so it is nondeterministic for multi-org users.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Cheaper first step with no staleness change: build the Actor from the session's orgRoles and status, which customSession already read fresh on the same request. That drops resolveActor with zero new cache and no invalidation surface. Then collapse customSession's two selects into one join (organizationmember JOIN profile). Only after that consider a TTL snapshot. The snapshot is the authorization boundary and has cross-process invalidation gaps (jobs, scripts, direct SQL), so it needs the invalidation list plus a deactivate-then-request test. Skipping /api/auth/* in the global middleware changes the rate-limit key for signed-in users on those paths from user:ID to ip:..., which shares a bucket for NAT'd offices. Keep /api/auth/get-session exempt as now. Add ORDER BY created_at to resolveActor. Allocation (isTutorAllocatedToLearner) stays uncached.

confirmed.title: Live-presence heartbeat is the ~33k session.updated_at writes: one DB UPDATE per open tab per 60s, even in hidden tabs, each also paying full auth cost
confirmed.current: Every signed-in tab POSTs /account/heartbeat every 60s (no document.hidden / visibilitychange check, no backoff, one timer per tab). The handler does touchSession => UPDATE session SET updated_at=now() WHERE id=? (this raw write bypasses better-auth, so it is independent of updateAge=1 day; better-auth itself only writes ~1/day/session). The request also pays global auth (3 identity queries, see authz-double-resolution) + 4 Redis commands for the rate limiter, so a 'cheap single-row update' is really ~4 Postgres statements + 1 Redis MULTI per user per minute. The online panel/summary reads max(session.updated_at) for the last 5 minutes.
confirmed.breaks_at: N concurrent open tabs => N/60 writes/s plus 3N/60 reads/s. 5,000 learners with a tab open = ~83 writes/s + ~250 reads/s purely for presence, producing constant MVCC dead tuples on the widest auth table (session) and autovacuum churn on Supabase; background tabs left open overnight keep it going for ever.
confirmed.fix: (a) Client: skip the ping when document.hidden, ping on visibilitychange->visible, raise interval to 120-180s (5-min online window stays accurate with a 10-min window or 2-min cadence), dedupe across tabs with a BroadcastChannel/localStorage leader or a lastPing timestamp. (b) Server: do not write Postgres at all for presence; ZADD presence:{orgId} <now> <userId> in Redis (ZREMRANGEBYSCORE older than 10 min on read) and have getOnlineOrgMembers read from it, with DB fallback. Minimum change: keep the DB write but gate it with an in-process Map<sessionId,lastTouch> and skip if < 120s ago. (c) Move the heartbeat route before the global getSession/resolveActor work or give it a cheap path (cookie-cache only). (d) Apply the same throttle to the unit-time heartbeat in lesson.ts:370 if it writes per tick (not reviewed in detail).
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin 'Online now' panel and the header '{n} online' pill (admin-overview.ts, management.ts:259-285) change definition slightly; keep the 5-min window semantics by matching cadence to window. Learners/tutors: heartbeat failures are already swallowed, so no user-visible break. Impersonation sessions (impersonatedBy) should keep not counting twice: keep keying by userId. If moved to Redis, Redis outage must degrade to 'no presence', never to request failure.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. +layout.svelte pings every 60s with no document.hidden check. touchSession is a raw UPDATE session SET updated_at by PK. Each ping also pays the full auth path (3 identity queries) plus the rate limiter's Redis MULTI. A PK update of a non-indexed column can be a HOT update, so bloat is lower than claimed. It is still the main write path and it scales linearly with open tabs. Hidden/background tabs ping forever.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do the client-side fix: skip when document.hidden, ping on visibilitychange, and use a 120-180s cadence with jitter. Server-side, move presence to Redis ZADD or an in-process lastTouch gate (>=120s) per session id. Do NOT add an index on session.updated_at (see session-table-indexes): it would defeat HOT updates for this exact write. 'Move heartbeat before the global session work' is not feasible because it needs the session id; use a cheap auth path via the cookie cache instead. Lengthen the online window to match any slower cadence.

confirmed.title: Dashboard hook makes an uncached, un-timed HTTP get-session call to the API on every non-proxy request (incl. each __data.json navigation); API slowness or restarts bounce all users to /login
confirmed.current: handle() awaits getSessionData() for every page/data request. It forwards the browser's cookies to authServerClient.getSession (HTTP to PRIVATE_SERVER_URL /api/auth/get-session) with no AbortSignal/timeout, no per-cookie memoisation, and no coalescing of the 2-4 parallel data requests SvelteKit issues on one navigation. The Set-Cookie that would refresh the cookie cache is discarded server-side, so SSR always relies on the 1h cookie cache then DB. Each call costs the API ~6 queries today (double auth, see above). It also console.logs 'has locals' and baseURL on every request. On any failure (timeout, API restart during the 20-45 min on-droplet image builds, 5xx) getThroughAuthClient returns null/throws => locals.user empty => (app)/+layout.server.ts requireActor redirects to /login for everyone, although their cookies are fine.
confirmed.breaks_at: Every navigation by every user; at ~100 nav/s this is 100 internal HTTP calls/s plus 600 queries/s. During a deploy or a slow Supabase moment the hung fetches hold SvelteKit request slots (no timeout) and the single dashboard container stalls; users see login redirects.
confirmed.fix: Add a short-lived server memo: Map<sha256(session cookie string), {locals, expiresAt}> with TTL 3-5s and in-flight promise coalescing, evicted explicitly when the proxy forwards POST /api/auth/sign-out or sign-in (hooks.server.ts:100 already sees those paths). Add AbortSignal.timeout(3000-4000) to the get-session fetch. On timeout/5xx (not on a clean 'null session' 200) do not redirect to /login; render an error page or retry once so a backend blip is not a logout. Remove the per-request console.logs. Optionally add cookieCache refreshing by relaying Set-Cookie from the SSR get-session response to the browser.
confirmed.flow_risk: All roles. 5s cache means a role change/deactivation seen by SSR guards (requireAdmin etc.) can lag <=5s on the dashboard side; the API remains authoritative and fresh, so no authorization hole. Logout must evict the cache entry (same-origin proxy path), otherwise a just-logged-out cookie can render one page for <=5s. Differentiate 'session invalid' from 'API unreachable' carefully; the reportToApi session_invalid_bounce metric (hooks.server.ts:146,177) should not fire for transport errors.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. hooks.server.ts awaits getSessionData for every non-proxy request once a cio cookie exists. getThroughAuthClient calls authServerClient.getSession with no signal/timeout and nothing memoised. It also logs 'has locals' and baseURL per call. The catch returns null, locals.user stays empty, hooks resolve because a cookie is present, and (app)/+layout.server.ts requireActor then denies. So a slow or restarting API (including during the 20-45 min on-droplet builds) bounces logged-in users to login. Overstated: SvelteKit sends one __data.json per navigation, not 2-4 parallel requests, so request coalescing buys little; the memo and the timeout are what matter.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add AbortSignal.timeout(~4s). Distinguish transport/5xx/timeout (render an error or retry once, and do not fire session_invalid_bounce) from a clean 200 null session. Add a small LRU memo (3-5s TTL) keyed by a hash of the cookie string, evicted on sign-out/sign-in through the proxy. Never memoise failures or nulls for more than about 1s. Remove the per-request console.logs.

confirmed.title: Cookie cache (1h) keeps revoked sessions alive; password reset does not actually 'end old sessions'; customSession comment documents behaviour that does not exist
confirmed.current: session.cookieCache.enabled with maxAge 1h: while the signed session_data cookie is valid, getSession returns the cached session without checking the DB session row. users.ts:267 deleteSessionsByUserId after a password reset, and :222 on deactivation, only delete DB rows. Deactivation is still safe because status is re-read from the DB on every call (customSession/resolveActor), but a password reset (or any manual session revoke) leaves the old cookie usable for up to 1h. If the snapshot caching above is added, this is the only thing left depending on the DB for revocation.
confirmed.breaks_at: Security/consistency issue rather than scale: grows with the number of password resets/offboardings. Also, because the cache is bypassed after 1h or when SSR drops the refreshed cookie, a full DB findSession (session + user join) is paid at least hourly per user per device.
confirmed.fix: Either (a) accept 1h and fix the comment, or (b) use cookieCache.version as a function that returns the user's password-reset/security stamp from the authz snapshot so resets invalidate cached cookies immediately, or (c) set cookieCache.maxAge to 5 min (cost: one extra session lookup per 5 min per user, negligible next to the other wins). Keep updateAge at 1 day.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learners/tutors: shorter maxAge => more frequent session+user join (primary-key/token lookups, cheap). Do not set disableCookieCache globally. The admin 'reset password' flow (users.ts:267) is the only flow that gains behaviour.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: session.cookieCache maxAge is 1h, and getSession returns the signed cached session without a DB row check. resetUserPassword (users.ts:267) and deactivation only delete DB rows. Deactivation is still safe because status is re-read each request, but an admin password reset leaves the old cookie usable for up to 1h. This is a security and consistency gap rather than a scale problem. The customSession comment about refresh on cache expiry is false.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Prefer cookieCache.maxAge of 5 min. It is cheap because customSession already hits the DB on every call. Do not rely on a cookieCache.version function without verifying the installed better-auth (1.4.18 in node_modules) supports it. Fix the misleading comments. For the reset flow, an explicit stamp check is the only immediate option.

confirmed.title: Three independent 45-60s pollers per open tab, all paying full auth; admin summary runs three aggregate queries including a full scan of session
confirmed.current: Per tab: heartbeat every 60s, notification list+unread count every 60s (limit up to 50 rows, plus on popover open), and for admins the org summary every 45s. None check document.hidden, none share timers across tabs, none back off on errors or 429. The summary (getOrgSummary) runs getMemberRoleStatusCounts + getCourseCounts + getOnlineOrgMembers per admin tab per 45s; getOnlineOrgMembers joins session x profile x organizationmember with a range filter on session.updated_at, which has no index, plus group by/sort.
confirmed.breaks_at: ~3 requests/min/learner => with 3,000 learners ~150 req/s of pure background traffic, each at 3 identity queries + its own query = ~600+ qps idle load; the global per-user rate limit (100/min) is not the concern but the DB pool is. Admin summary cost grows linearly with member count and with session-table size (see session-table-indexes).
confirmed.fix: Client: one shared scheduler (single BroadcastChannel-elected leader tab), pause on document.hidden, resume on visibility with an immediate refresh, add jitter (+/-20%) so thousands of clients do not align, exponential backoff on 429/5xx, raise cadence to 120-180s for bell and summary. Server: add a cheap unread-count endpoint (SELECT count(*) with partial index on (user_id) WHERE read=false) and let the list load only on open; cache getOrgSummary result per org for 30-60s in memory (admin counts do not need 45s freshness) with single-flight so N admins share one computation.
confirmed.flow_risk: Notification freshness for learners/tutors drops from 60s to ~2 min unless push is added; acceptable but communicate. Summary pill for admins slightly staler. Make sure caches key on orgId so a future multi-org setup does not leak counts.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly real. The pollers exist and none check document.hidden or back off. Corrections: the org summary poll lives in app-header, which is only mounted in the admin-guarded org/[slug] layout, so it is admin-only and a few tabs, not per learner. Learners run heartbeat (60s) plus the bell (60s) plus in-lesson time beats (30s), roughly 2-4 requests/min, not the 3 claimed for everyone. The bell's GET /notifications runs 3 queries (list, unread count, lesson link targets) every poll. getOnlineOrgMembers filters session.updated_at with no index, so the cost grows with the session table (ties to session-table-indexes).
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The suggested partial index on 'read=false' is wrong: the column is read_at, and idx_notification_user_unread (user_id, read_at) already exists. Add a count-only endpoint (count where read_at is null) for the poll and load the list only on open. Add visibility pause, jitter, backoff and a 120-180s cadence. Cache getOrgSummary per orgId for 30-60s with single-flight.

confirmed.title: session table has no user_id or updated_at index and expired sessions are never purged
confirmed.current: session has PK + unique(token) only. Queries by user_id (deleteSessionsByUserId, last-seen analytics, online panel join, FK cascade from user delete) and by updated_at range (online panel) seq-scan. better-auth never deletes expired rows by itself, the only purge job in apps/jobs is system_event_log retention, and every login/impersonation/login-link/token-exchange inserts a new session row (7-day lifetime), so the table grows without bound. This also matches the advisor's 'unindexed foreign keys'.
confirmed.breaks_at: Rows = logins x devices over time; at thousands of learners logging in daily the table reaches millions of rows within months, making the 45s admin summary, deactivation (delete by user_id) and analytics full scans slow and holding pooled connections.
confirmed.fix: Migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY session_user_id_idx ON session(user_id); and a partial/btree index on session(updated_at) (or restrict presence to Redis per heartbeat finding and skip this one). Add a daily maintenance job in apps/jobs: DELETE FROM session WHERE expires_at < now() - interval '1 day' in batches of 5k. Migration runs via the 5432 session pooler per project rules.
confirmed.flow_risk: Index creation is non-blocking with CONCURRENTLY; purge only touches already-expired sessions so no login is affected (better-auth treats expired rows as invalid anyway). The 'last seen' analytics use max(updated_at) so keep recent rows; purging by expires_at<now()-1day retains them.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. The session table (schema.ts:113-130) has only the PK and a unique token index. No migration indexes session.user_id, and the only scheduled purge is system_event_log. better-auth removes only the expired row it happens to look up. user_id queries (deleteSessionsByUserId, FK cascade, the online join) seq-scan, and rows grow with every login or impersonation.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Index user_id only. Do NOT index updated_at: heartbeat updates that column every 60s per tab, so an index would defeat HOT updates and amplify write cost (this conflicts with the heartbeat finding). CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction and drizzle's migrator wraps migrations, so run it as a separate script or via the SQL editor, or use plain CREATE INDEX while the table is small. Add a batched daily purge of expires_at < now() - 1 day in the jobs maintenance worker.

confirmed.title: Rate limiter: per-request Redis MULTI with a ZSET entry per request, new limiter instance per request, and every request waits up to 2s when Redis stalls
confirmed.current: Sliding-window via ZREMRANGEBYSCORE + ZCARD + ZADD + EXPIRE in a MULTI for every authenticated request (4 commands, one ZSET member per request, up to 100 members/user/min, all appended to the AOF). A new RedisRateLimiter object is built per request. When Redis is down or the node-redis offline queue is stalling, each request awaits RATE_LIMIT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 before failing open (logged once but the delay is paid every time), adding 2s to all API latency and holding sockets. Exempt: /api/auth/get-session and any request with the PRIVATE_SERVER_KEY bearer, so SSR-originated calls and the unauthenticated get-session endpoint are unmetered. Unauthenticated callers share an IP bucket.
confirmed.breaks_at: ~200-500 req/s => 800-2,000 Redis commands/s plus AOF writes on the same 4 GB box; Redis failure => +2s on every request (looks like a full outage under load).
confirmed.fix: Switch to a fixed/approximate window with INCR + EXPIRE NX (one round trip, or a single Lua script) keyed user:{id}:{minute}; hoist the limiter instance; add a simple circuit breaker (after 3 consecutive failures skip Redis for 10-30s); consider an in-process token bucket as first line and Redis only for coarse global limits. Set redis maxmemory + allkeys-lru so rate_limit keys cannot grow unbounded; AOF can be disabled for this Redis instance if BullMQ durability is acceptable (or run a second Redis). Reconsider exempting get-session: add a generous per-IP limit instead.
confirmed.flow_risk: Behaviour change from sliding to fixed window allows 2x burst at window boundaries; fine for abuse protection. Do not lower limits below what a dashboard page legitimately fires in parallel (a course page can issue 10-20 calls plus 3 pollers, so 100/min is already tight for power tutors: consider 300/min for authenticated actors while keeping 429 for sign-in). BullMQ shares this Redis: do not set eviction policy that can evict queue keys (use volatile-lru or a separate instance).
confirmed.verifier_note: Mostly real but overstated. isAllowed does a 4-command MULTI with a ZSET member per request (limiter.ts), and the 2s withTimeout fail-open applies per request. Under a node-redis offline queue that stalls, each request pays up to 2s. At target traffic the Redis cost is small (sub-ms per request). A fresh RedisRateLimiter object per request is trivial. The skip for the PRIVATE_SERVER_KEY bearer and /api/auth/get-session is real.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do NOT set maxmemory with allkeys-lru: this Redis also holds BullMQ and eviction would drop queue and job keys (BullMQ requires noeviction). Rate-limit keys already carry EXPIRE, so memory is bounded (about 100 members x active users). Do not disable AOF without accepting BullMQ job loss on restart. A circuit breaker that skips Redis for 10-30s after consecutive failures is the worthwhile part. INCR+EXPIRE is optional.

confirmed.title: GET /account on every full page load runs a profile/email-verification sync (3-4 queries) plus orgs+plans join; session.update.after repeats the sync
confirmed.current: setupApp() fetches /account once per SPA lifecycle (so once per hard load/refresh). getAccountData runs getProfileById, getOrganizationByProfileId (organization x organizationmember x organization_plan), then ALWAYS syncProfileEmailVerificationFromAuthUser (select user, select profile, resolveAuthUserEmailVerified query, conditional updates), then in non-selfhosted mode a COUNT per admin/tutor org. The same sync also runs in databaseHooks session.create.after, session.update.after and user.update.after. The update hook fires at the 1-day refresh, and after the touch heartbeat is moved off DB it will not add load, but in any case the sync is idempotent and almost always a no-op.
confirmed.breaks_at: One refresh by every user at start of each lesson day: ~6-8 queries per hard load; with 3,000 users morning login burst (everybody at 9:00) = ~20k queries in a minute against a 10-connection pool, delaying login for everyone.
confirmed.fix: Run the sync only when profile.isEmailVerified is false (the function never demotes, so verified profiles never need it) and when profile.email differs from session user email (available from the session already loaded); drop the unconditional call from getAccountData. Return profile/orgs from a single join where possible; cache getOrganizationByProfileId result for 30s per user (invalidate with the authz snapshot invalidation). Keep the hooks but short-circuit on the same condition.
confirmed.flow_risk: Email verification flow (verify-email modal, invite acceptance, change-email): the sync is what promotes profile.isEmailVerified after better-auth verifies the user, so keep running it when profile.isEmailVerified=false or email mismatch; verified-forever learners skip it. Test change-email confirmation (profile.email must still follow user.email).
confirmed.verifier_note: Real but minor. getAccountData always runs syncProfileEmailVerificationFromAuthUser (user select, profile select, resolveAuthUserEmailVerified, conditional updates), plus getProfileById and getOrganizationByProfileId, once per hard load. It is about 6 queries on a once-per-load path, not a per-navigation or per-request cost, and a synchronized 9am burst of everyone is unlikely.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The proposed skip condition is wrong as written: skipping when profile.isEmailVerified is true would also skip the userNeedsVerification branch that promotes user.emailVerified. Skip only when profile.isEmailVerified AND session.user.emailVerified AND profile.email equals session.user.email. Otherwise keep running it.

confirmed.title: Automation/API-key requests do a hash lookup and an AWAITED last_used_at UPDATE on every call
confirmed.current: authenticateOrganizationApiKeyService queries organization_api_key by hash on every request, then touchOrganizationApiKeyLastUsedService awaits an UPDATE before next(). The public /public-api/v1 and automation (n8n/CRM) callers can be bursty (bulk enrolment loops).
confirmed.breaks_at: A script doing 50 req/s makes 100 statements/s on a single row (hot row lock contention: every request updates the same key row) and adds a DB write to the request latency.
confirmed.fix: Cache authenticated keys in-process by hash for 30-60s (store expiry; invalidate on key revoke/rotate in the same service) and throttle the touch to at most once per minute per key, fire-and-forget (void promise with catch).
confirmed.flow_risk: Key revocation must evict the cache entry immediately (revoke happens in the API process; keep TTL <=60s as the ceiling). Scope checks (automation-key-scopes.ts) read from the cached row, so scope edits also need to evict. last_used_at becomes accurate to ~1 minute, which is fine for an audit hint.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. The middleware does a hash lookup and then awaits updateOrganizationApiKey(lastUsedAt) on every call. This only affects integrator traffic (n8n/CRM), and the contention is on a single key's row. It adds latency and a write per call but is not a learner-scale risk.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Throttle the touch to once per minute per key and do not await it. A 30-60s in-process cache of authenticated keys must be evicted on revoke, rotate and scope edit in the same service. Separate issue: the middleware's try/catch wraps await next(), so a downstream throw is mislabelled as 401 UNAUTHORIZED.

confirmed.title: Single 10-connection pool per process, no statement/idle-transaction timeout, no queue/backpressure on pool exhaustion
confirmed.current: postgres-js max=10 (DATABASE_POOL_MAX default; the '|| 5' fallback only applies for NaN), connect_timeout 10s, idle_timeout 20s, max_lifetime 30 min, prepare:false (correct for the 6543 transaction pooler). No statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, so one slow reporting query or a stuck runInTransaction holds a pool slot. api and jobs each open their own 10. All the per-request queries listed above compete for the same 10 slots, so one slow endpoint stalls auth for every user (auth runs on every request).
confirmed.breaks_at: When concurrent in-flight queries > 10 (a few hundred active users with the current 3 identity queries per request), requests queue inside postgres-js without a limit or timeout, producing multi-second tail latency and cascading timeouts.
confirmed.fix: After reducing per-request queries (findings 1-2), set DATABASE_POOL_MAX to 20-25 for api (Supabase pooler client limit permitting) and 5 for jobs; set per-role statement_timeout (e.g. ALTER ROLE api_role SET statement_timeout='15s'; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout='30s') because startup params are not reliable through the transaction pooler; add a lightweight in-app metric/log when postgres-js queue depth is high. Keep reports/exports on a separate small pool or role.
confirmed.flow_risk: A too-short statement_timeout can break legitimate long operations (course import, reports, bulk enrolment): exempt the jobs role and the import paths, test report endpoints first. Raising the pool must stay under Supabase pooler limits across api + jobs + migrations or other services will get 'too many clients'.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: postgres-js max defaults to 10, with no statement_timeout or idle-in-transaction timeout, and api and jobs each open their own pool. With about 3 identity queries per request, pool saturation and queuing is the plausible first bottleneck. The real fix is the query reduction in the authz and layout findings.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: ALTER ROLE ... SET statement_timeout on the shared Supabase pooler role would also hit migrations (index builds), the dashboard SQL editor and jobs. Use a dedicated role per service, or exempt migrations and jobs. Supavisor's own pool_size (compute-tier dependent, often about 15) bounds real backend concurrency, so raising the client max to 20-25 may only queue at the pooler. Check the tier before raising it, and keep api+jobs+migrations under the limit.

confirmed.title: Per-request console logging on every layer with no docker log rotation
confirmed.location: apps/api/src/app.ts:94 (hono logger); apps/api/src/utils/origins.ts:20 (console.log('check origin')); apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/services/auth/session.ts:12,35 and server.ts:12; apps/dashboard/src/routes/+layout.server.ts:57-60; apps/dashboard/src/lib/features/app/layout-setup.ts:62; apps/api/src/routes/account/account.ts:30-32; docker-compose.deploy.yaml (no logging: options)
confirmed.current: Every request writes 2-6 log lines (Hono logger in+out, 'check origin' for CORS, 'has locals', baseURL, '[+layout.server] load ...', console.time('accountRouter')). Compose has no logging driver/max-size configured, so json-file logs are unbounded on the shared 4 GB droplet disk.
confirmed.breaks_at: ~100 req/s => ~500 log lines/s synchronous to stdout (blocking when the pipe is slow) and several GB/day of container logs; a full disk takes down Postgres-less droplet services (redis AOF, caddy).
confirmed.fix: Remove the debug console.logs on hot paths; keep hono logger only in non-production or sample it; add `logging: {driver: json-file, options: {max-size: 20m, max-file: 5}}` to every service in docker-compose.deploy.yaml; log structured errors only.
confirmed.flow_risk: None functionally; keep correlation-id logging for errors (HP/SA-5) and the error-handler logs.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. The Hono logger() runs on every request, origins.ts:20 logs 'check origin' per CORS check, session.ts logs 'has locals' and baseURL per call, +layout.server.ts logs per load, and account.ts uses console.time. docker-compose.deploy.yaml has no logging: options, so json-file logs are unrotated on the shared droplet. That is near-zero risk now, but a disk-fill risk under sustained load, and the fix is trivial.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add logging driver json-file with max-size/max-file to every service now. Drop the debug logs on the hot paths and sample or disable the access logger in production.

confirmed.title: Every 4xx AppError and 5xx inserts a row into system_event_log; an error storm becomes a write storm
confirmed.current: onError calls recordApiError for every AppError < 500 (warn) and every 500, each an un-batched INSERT via the shared 10-connection pool, with up to 2KB message + 4KB stack. The dashboard handleError also POSTs /log/client for every SSR error (hooks.server.ts:65-74, 3s timeout, un-throttled). A broken client retrying a 403/400 or a bot probing yields one insert per request.
confirmed.breaks_at: A retry loop of 50 req/s => 50 inserts/s competing with auth queries for pool slots; table bloat bounded only by the retention purge job.
confirmed.fix: Dedupe/throttle in recordSystemEvent: in-memory counter keyed by (eventType, path, httpStatus, userId) that writes at most 1 row per key per 30-60s with a count in metadata; batch inserts every 2-5s; skip 401/403/404/validation 4xx or sample them (keep 5xx and auth events). Keep Sentry for 5xx.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin Logger screen (system events) shows aggregated counts for repeated errors instead of every occurrence; auth.login.failure/rate_limited security events must stay un-sampled.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly overstated. recordApiError is only called from app.onError, but most routes catch and return handleError(), which does not reach onError, so only uncaught throws and middleware-thrown AppErrors are recorded. The dashboard side is the real amplifier: SvelteKit's handleError also fires for unmatched-route 404s, so a bot scan produces a console.error plus a POST /log/client. That POST carries PRIVATE_SERVER_KEY and so bypasses the rate limiter, then inserts one row per hit.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Throttle or dedupe by (eventType, path, status) in recordSystemEvent. Skip 404 and 4xx in the dashboard handleError report. Rate-limit /log/client per IP even for the server key.

confirmed.title: Per-request ownership lookups that are cacheable (course->org binding, org-by-siteName) run on every call
confirmed.current: requireCourseInOrg does getCourseOrgId(courseId) on every request to every guarded course route (immutable mapping: a course never changes org); requireCohortInOrg runs isOrgAdminByCohortId each time; courseMemberMiddleware runs isUserCourseMemberOrOrgAdmin per request and falls into ensureProgramCourseAccess (a possible write/backfill) when the first check fails. The org/[slug] layout correctly caches orgId in a 7-day non-httpOnly cookie, but it trusts that client-controllable cookie as the orgId before requireSameOrg (the API remains authoritative).
confirmed.breaks_at: Each course page fires several API calls; each pays 1 extra query for the course->org map (immutable data), pure waste: at 100 req/s that is up to 100 qps of identical PK lookups.
confirmed.fix: Add a process-level LRU for courseId->orgId (TTL 10 min; no invalidation needed except course deletion/move, which should evict), leave membership checks uncached or cache with the same invalidation hooks as the authz snapshot. Do NOT cache allocation/ownership decisions (tutor-learner allocation, ACCESS.md section 8) without explicit invalidation on allocation changes.
confirmed.flow_risk: Cross-org isolation depends on this binding: if a course is ever moved between orgs the cache must be evicted; today single-org so safe. Tutor visibility (allocated learners only) is unaffected since the cached value is only course->org.
confirmed.verifier_note: Real but trivial: requireCourseInOrg does one PK lookup per guarded request and the mapping is immutable. The org/[slug] cookie trust is harmless because the API is authoritative and requireSameOrg binds the actor.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: An LRU of courseId->orgId with a 10 min TTL is fine and must be evicted on course delete or move. Do not cache membership or allocation decisions, so the tutor-allocation rule is untouched.

confirmed.title: Course-invite accept holds one pooled connection and then asks for a second inside the same transaction (pool deadlock under a burst of invite clicks)
confirmed.current: acceptCourseInvite opens db.transaction (1 connection, 'tx'). Inside the callback it calls countInviteDistinctPreviewIps(invite.id, ...) and recordInviteAudit(...) (-> createCourseInviteAudit) which use the global `db`, not `tx`, so each needs a SECOND pool connection while the first is held idle-in-transaction. The 'ACCEPTED' audit is also committed on the second connection before the tx commits, so a later rollback (409 'already used') leaves a false ACCEPTED audit row. assertStudentCapacityOrThrow(org.id,1) (line ~1006) also uses `db` but returns early on self-hosted, so it only bites the cloud build. postgres.js has no pool-wait timeout (connect_timeout only covers the TCP/TLS handshake), so waiters queue forever.
confirmed.breaks_at: Pool max is 10 per api process. When >=10 learners accept the same course invite link concurrently (a cohort start: link emailed or posted to 100-300 learners), all 10 connections are held by transactions that are each waiting for an 11th. Every other request on that api process (login, session checks, heartbeats) also queues behind them. Nothing times out; recovery needs a container restart. Even at 5 concurrent accepts the extra connection per request doubles pool pressure.
confirmed.fix: 1) Pass `tx` through: add an optional dbClient param to countInviteDistinctPreviewIps and createCourseInviteAudit (the codebase already uses the `dbClient: DbOrTxClient = db` pattern, e.g. getGroupMemberIdByGroupAndProfile) and call recordInviteAudit(..., tx) for the ACCEPTED audit so it commits atomically with the enrolment. 2) Move the read-only IP-diversity count BEFORE db.transaction. 3) Keep the ABUSE_BLOCKED audit on the pool (outside the tx) on purpose: it must survive the rollback that follows the throw, so run it after catching/leaving the tx or via a deliberate second connection only on that rare path. 4) Pass tx into assertStudentCapacityOrThrow (or compute capacity before the tx) for cloud builds. 5) Add a lint/test guard: grep-style unit test that no function called from inside a db.transaction callback in apps/api/src/services uses bare `db` (or a code-review checklist), plus an app-level pool wait timeout (see pool-sizing finding).
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner flow: invite-link enrolment (/courses invite accept). Edge cases: (a) already-enrolled learner returns early with ACCEPTED/alreadyJoined audit, which must still be written, now on tx; (b) ABUSE_BLOCKED path must still write its audit even though the tx throws; (c) optimisticIncrementCourseInviteUsedCount conflict returns 409 and the ACCEPTED audit must now roll back with it (behaviour change that is the correct one, but the audit stats screen (listCourseInviteAuditStats) will stop counting failed accepts); (d) moving the IP count before the tx slightly widens the race window for the anomaly check, which is a heuristic only. Does not touch tutor allocation rules.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed at apps/api/src/services/course/invite.ts:921-1050: acceptStudentInvite opens db.transaction (reserves a pooled connection), then calls countInviteDistinctPreviewIps (queries/course/invite.ts uses global db), recordInviteAudit -> createCourseInviteAudit (global db), and on cloud builds assertStudentCapacityOrThrow (global db; returns early when PUBLIC_IS_SELFHOSTED=true, so prod is not hit by that one). Each needs a second pool connection while the first sits idle-in-transaction. Pool max 10 (drizzle.ts) and postgres.js has no pool-wait timeout, so ~10 simultaneous accepts is a true hold-and-wait deadlock that only a restart clears. The false ACCEPTED audit after a 409 rollback is also real because the audit commits on its own connection. Severity set to high, not critical: it needs ~10 accepts overlapping inside a ~100 ms tx window, which is plausible for a cohort-start link blast but not for every deploy. No lock conflict between the audit insert (FK KEY SHARE) and the tx's usedCount update, so the second connection does not deadlock on locks, only on pool slots.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Simplest safe fix: add an optional dbClient: DbOrTxClient = db param to countInviteDistinctPreviewIps and createCourseInviteAudit and pass tx for the read count and for both ACCEPTED audits (the already-joined audit and the final one). Do NOT pass tx for ABUSE_BLOCKED: the throw rolls the tx back and would erase the audit. Instead throw a typed AppError out of the tx, catch it outside db.transaction and write the ABUSE_BLOCKED audit on the pool after the tx has released its connection (or compute the IP-diversity check before the tx using a separate invite lookup by tokenHash). Pass tx to assertStudentCapacityOrThrow (needs getActiveOrganizationPlan/countActiveStudents to accept a client) or run it before the tx. Also fix the same pattern in cohort.ts:266 (capacity check on bare db inside a per-member tx, cloud only). Add the grep/unit-test guard. The behaviour change (failed accepts no longer leave ACCEPTED rows) is correct but listCourseInviteAuditStats numbers will drop slightly.

confirmed.title: Every authenticated API request pays 3+ sequential DB round trips for identity (customSession runs on every getSession, then resolveActor re-reads the same tables), and /api/auth/get-session pays it twice
confirmed.location: packages/db/src/auth.ts:274-300 (customSession fn), :148-151 (cookieCache), :276-278 (comment is wrong); packages/db/src/actor.ts:20-47; apps/api/src/app.ts:117-144, 167; apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/services/auth/session.ts:8-55; apps/dashboard/src/lib/features/app/layout-setup.ts:27-29; packages/db/src/queries/organization/organization.ts:941-1000
confirmed.current: better-auth's customSession endpoint (verified in node_modules better-auth 1.6.x custom-session/index.mjs) calls getSession() and then ALWAYS runs fn(), so the 'refreshes when the cookie cache expires' comment in auth.ts:276-278 is not true: getUserOrgRolesMap (organizationmember select) + a profile.status select run on every request even on a cookie-cache hit. app.ts then calls resolveActor (organizationmember JOIN profile) for the same user. That is 3 sequential queries before any route code, for every request including heartbeats, notification polls and /analytics/track. For SSR page loads the dashboard calls /api/auth/get-session, which passes through the global middleware (getSession+fn+resolveActor) AND then the better-auth handler (getSession+fn again) = ~5 queries for one session probe, and layout-setup then calls /organization/first (getFirstOrganizationWithPlans = 2 more queries) on every page load. This is the source of the ~335k organization selects and ~100k resolveActor lookups in pg_stat_statements for 1 org. When the cookie cache misses (SSR calls drop Set-Cookie so the cache is never refreshed by SSR; cache is 1h) better-auth adds session+user selects and daily session UPDATE.
confirmed.breaks_at: Roughly 4-8 queries per page view and 3-4 per background ping. 2,000 concurrent users each with one open tab (heartbeat 60s + notification poll 60s + page views) is ~70-100 req/s -> 300-600 queries/s of pure identity overhead. With a 10-connection pool and DB round trip of 5-15 ms (droplet in lon1, Supabase region unverified) the pool tops out near 700-2000 qps, so the pool saturates well before CPU does, and every user-visible request queues behind identity lookups.
confirmed.fix: 1) Collapse to ONE query per request: a single select of organizationmember JOIN profile for the user (all memberships) yields orgRoles map, status and the actor for the cio-org-id header. Compute it once in the app.ts middleware and stash it on the Hono context; make resolveActor/getUserOrgRolesMap accept a prefetched row set. 2) Stop running the expensive fn twice: skip customSession work for requests under /api/auth/get-session when the middleware already computed it (memoise per request in a WeakMap keyed on the Headers object / AsyncLocalStorage), or have the middleware call the plain (non-custom) session read and attach orgRoles/status itself. 3) Add a short-TTL (15-30 s) Redis cache keyed `authctx:{userId}` for {orgRoles,status,memberships}, with explicit invalidation (DEL) in every writer: role change, membership create/delete, deactivate/reactivate (deleteSessionsByUserId in packages/db/src/queries/organization/users.ts:99), invite accept, profile status update, admin reset. 4) Cache getFirstOrganizationWithPlans / getFirstOrganization in-process for 60 s (single org; invalidate on organization/plan update) and have the dashboard cache /organization/first per process for 60 s. 5) Correct the comment in auth.ts so nobody relies on it.
confirmed.flow_risk: Touches the authorization identity used by admin, manager, tutor and learner flows, so it must be done carefully. ACCESS.md rule that deactivation and role changes take effect on the NEXT request (actor.ts header) is only preserved if every writer invalidates the cache AND the TTL is short; a missed writer = stale tutor/learner role for up to TTL. Tutors-see-only-allocated-learners (isAllocatedTutor, ad92abcf5) is evaluated per route from the actor's userId/role and must NOT be cached or derived from the cached blob beyond role/orgId. Redis outage must fall back to the DB read (fail-open to DB, never to a cached allow). Impersonation/view-as-student sessions: key by the session's userId, not the admin's. Dashboard getActor reads orgRoles from the session JSON, so the response shape of /api/auth/get-session must stay identical.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. better-auth 1.4.18 custom-session endpoint (node_modules .../plugins/custom-session/index.mjs) calls getSession() then ALWAYS awaits fn(), so the auth.ts:276-278 comment is wrong and getUserOrgRolesMap + profile.status run on every request even with a cookie-cache hit. app.ts:106-144 then runs resolveActor (organizationmember JOIN profile) on every non-public path, so >=3 sequential queries precede any route. /api/auth/get-session is not a public CORS path, so it passes the global middleware (getSession+fn+resolveActor) and then the better-auth handler (getSession+fn again). Dashboard layout-setup.ts:28 calls getFirstOrg on every SSR load. Scale numbers are rough but the direction (identity overhead dominates the 10-connection pool) is right. Severity high is fair.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Keep steps 1, 2, 4 and 5; DROP or heavily restrict step 3 (Redis authctx cache of orgRoles/status/memberships). ACCESS.md and actor.ts require role change and deactivation to take effect on the very next request, and the writers are many (role change, membership delete, deactivation, invite accept, admin reset, raw SQL by the owner via Supabase). A 15-30 s TTL cache with DEL-on-write will eventually miss a writer and leave a stale tutor/deactivated user. Collapsing to ONE query per request (single organizationmember JOIN profile select shared by customSession and resolveActor via a per-request memo keyed on the request Headers/AsyncLocalStorage) cuts 3 queries to 1 and the double get-session cost to 1 with zero staleness. If a cache is added later, cap TTL at ~5 s and never cache isAllocatedTutor inputs. Org/plan lookups (getFirstOrganization, getFirstOrganizationWithPlans, used also by signup-guard, profile.ts, registration.ts, resolve-verification-org.ts) are safe to cache in-process for 30-60 s with invalidation on org/plan update; that is the cheapest win for the 335k organization selects. Also keep the /api/auth/get-session JSON shape identical for dashboard getActor.

confirmed.title: Presence heartbeat writes a session row every 60 s from every open tab (including hidden tabs), through the full auth pipeline
confirmed.current: Every signed-in tab POSTs /account/heartbeat every 60 s with setInterval and no document.hidden / online check. Each call runs the 3-query identity pipeline then `UPDATE session SET updated_at=now() WHERE id=` (touchSession). This is the ~33k session updated_at writes seen in prod (not better-auth's own once-a-day refresh). The same layout also polls notifications every 60 s, and learners on a lesson add the unit-time beat every ~30 s. The admin 'Online now' query (getOnlineOrgMembers) filters session.updated_at >= cutoff and joins profile/organizationmember with no index on session.updated_at or session.user_id.
confirmed.breaks_at: N open tabs = N writes/min plus 3N reads/min for this one feature: 3,000 tabs = 3,000 UPDATEs/min (WAL + dead tuples on a table that is never vacuumed aggressively) and ~12,000 queries/min before any real work. Background tabs left open overnight keep it up. Each admin dashboard open adds a 45 s poll that scans the session table.
confirmed.fix: 1) Client: skip the ping when document.hidden, use the visibilitychange event to resume, and add jitter (+-10 s) so tabs do not align; raise interval to 120 s (Online-now window is 5 min so 2 min is still accurate). 2) Server: make the heartbeat route cheap: mount it before the global session/actor middleware or give it a fast path that only validates the cookie (cookie-cache hit) and skips customSession/resolveActor. 3) Move presence out of Postgres: SET `presence:{orgId}:{userId}` EX 300 in Redis (or ZADD to a per-org sorted set with score=now) and have getOnlineOrgMembers read Redis, then hydrate names with one `WHERE id = ANY(...)` query; stop UPDATEing session rows. 4) If the DB write is kept, throttle it: only UPDATE when `updated_at < now() - interval '2 minutes'` (single conditional statement) or gate with Redis SET NX EX 90 so extra tabs of the same session do not write. 5) Add indexes (see session-growth finding).
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin 'Online now' panel is the only consumer of session.updated_at (also analytics.ts:58-103 last-seen for user lists and admin-overview 'lastActive') - switching storage must update those readers or last-seen will go stale. Learners/tutors are unaffected functionally. Hidden-tab gating means a user who leaves a tab hidden shows as offline after 5 min - intended. If presence moves to Redis and Redis is down, Online-now should degrade to empty, not 500.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: (app)/+layout.svelte:32-42 setInterval 60 s with no document.hidden check; account.ts:114 heartbeat goes through the global auth pipeline plus authMiddleware, then touchSession UPDATE session SET updated_at. getOnlineOrgMembers reads session.updated_at. Real, but the write itself is a cheap PK update (HOT-eligible because updated_at is unindexed); the dominant cost is the 3 read queries from the auth pipeline, which finding 2 already addresses. Severity lowered to medium accordingly. Browsers already throttle hidden-tab timers heavily, so visibility gating gives a modest gain.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do NOT add idx_session_updated_at (the finding's step 5 / the table-growth finding): indexing updated_at makes every heartbeat a non-HOT update with index maintenance, multiplying write cost and bloat. Index only session.user_id. Preferred fix: make the UPDATE conditional (WHERE id = $1 AND updated_at < now() - interval '60 seconds') so duplicate tabs and fast pings are no-ops, add visibilitychange gating and jitter, and keep the 60 s interval (raising to 120 s leaves little slack against the 5-minute Online-now window).
