Redis presence is optional later; if done, update analytics.ts last-seen and admin-overview lastActive readers and make Redis failure degrade to empty, not 500.

confirmed.title: Pool is sized by one hard-coded default for both api and jobs, cannot be tuned from the deploy compose, has no pool-wait timeout or metrics, and has no model for N replicas
confirmed.location: packages/db/src/drizzle.ts:22-31; docker-compose.deploy.yaml:54-57,126 (no DATABASE_POOL_MAX passed); apps/jobs/src/workers/*.ts (concurrency emails 5 + notifications 5 + media 2 + transcribe 1 + agent 1 + maintenance 1 = 15); docs/ENV.md:44; packages/db/src/scripts/db-setup.ts:68,100
confirmed.current: Exactly one postgres.js pool per process (dashboard has none: it only calls the api). api and jobs both import drizzle.ts, so each gets max = DATABASE_POOL_MAX ?? 10 (the `|| 5` fallback only triggers on NaN, so the effective default is 10, not 5). docker-compose.deploy.yaml lists api and jobs environment explicitly and never passes DATABASE_POOL_MAX, so the knob documented in ENV.md cannot be changed on the droplet without editing compose. api and jobs must use the same value (one var). Jobs run up to 15 concurrent handlers against a 10 pool. idle_timeout 20 s, connect_timeout 10, max_lifetime 30 min, prepare:false, ssl:require are all sensible for Supavisor transaction mode. Missing: any wait/acquire timeout, any pool-saturation metric, any application_name for pg_stat_activity attribution.
confirmed.breaks_at: Today ~40 learners keep the pool idle. With thousands of learners and the 3-5 queries/request above, 10 connections saturate and requests wait with no upper bound. Adding a 2nd api replica doubles backend demand but there is no coordinated budget: Supabase transaction-pooler backend pool_size (default is small, ~15, and shared with Supabase Storage/Auth/PostgREST) and Postgres max_connections (tier dependent, e.g. 60 on Micro, 90 on Small) bound total concurrency, and the dashboard-side setting is outside the repo.
confirmed.fix: Sizing rule: backend pool_size needed ~= peak_rps x queries_per_request x avg_query_seconds x 1.5 (after the auth-pipeline fix: ~1-2 queries per request). Proposal: api DATABASE_POOL_MAX=15 per replica, jobs JOBS_DATABASE_POOL_MAX=5 (read from a separate env var in drizzle.ts, or pass `max` via a factory so jobs can differ), migration/seed/script clients max:1-2. Client connections to Supavisor are cheap and multiplexed in transaction mode, so keep app-side max modest (fail fast at the app) and set Supabase pool_size ~= 0.5 x (N_api x 15 + M_jobs x 5), capped at roughly 60-80% of Postgres max_connections minus Supabase internals (Auth, Storage, PostgREST). Example: 2 api + 1 jobs = 35 client slots -> pool_size 20-25, needs a compute tier with >=60-90 max_connections. Concrete code: (1) pass DATABASE_POOL_MAX and a new JOBS_DATABASE_POOL_MAX through docker-compose.deploy.yaml and .env.deploy.example; (2) set connection:{application_name:'pearl-api'|'pearl-jobs'} (startup parameter allowed by Supavisor); (3) wrap pool acquisition in an app-level timeout - simplest is a Hono timeout middleware (e.g. 30 s) plus `sql.options.max` logging of `sql.reserved`/queue length exposed on a /ready endpoint that also does a 1 s `select 1` (keep /health dependency-free as designed); (4) lower jobs concurrency or keep it - jobs hold a connection only during individual queries so 15 handlers on 5 connections is fine, but document it; (5) verify the Supabase project region matches the lon1 droplet (docs/DEPLOY.md:116) - a cross-region DB adds 80-150 ms per query and multiplies every finding here. Advisor note auth_db_connections_absolute: that warns that the Supabase Auth (GoTrue) service uses an absolute connection count (default 10) instead of a percentage. PearlLMS authenticates with better-auth, not Supabase Auth, so those connections are pure waste against the same max_connections budget; switch the project's Auth connection strategy to percentage (or lower it to the minimum) in the Supabase dashboard - no repo change, but it must be factored into pool_size.
confirmed.flow_risk: Config-only for the env plumbing (safe). Lowering jobs max to 5 can slow bulk job bursts (analytics rollup runs 3 queries in Promise.all, notification fan-outs) but not break them. A too-low api pool without the auth-pipeline fix would make things worse, so ship the auth fix first or raise api max to 15 together. Changing pool_size/auth strategy in the Supabase dashboard briefly drops pooled backends - do it off-peak. All roles (admin, tutor, learner, manager) share this pool, so the failure mode when undersized is global slowness, not a single flow.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: drizzle.ts:22 max = parseInt(DATABASE_POOL_MAX ?? '10') || 5 (effective default 10; the 5 only on NaN), idle_timeout 20, connect_timeout 10, no queue/acquire timeout, one pool per process shared by api and jobs, and docker-compose.deploy.yaml / .env.deploy.example never pass DATABASE_POOL_MAX (grep: only drizzle.ts, ENV.md, CODEMAP.md, REPLICATION.md mention it). Jobs concurrency sums to 15 (emails 5, notifications 5, media 2, transcribe 1, agent 1, maintenance 1) against 10 connections, fine since handlers hold a connection only per query. Real but it is tuning/ops, not a defect today, hence medium. The 'raise api to 15' advice only helps if the Supabase pooler pool_size and compute-tier max_connections can back it; app-side max just moves where requests queue.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Pass DATABASE_POOL_MAX (and a separate JOBS_DATABASE_POOL_MAX) through compose and .env.deploy.example; verify Supabase pool_size and tier max_connections BEFORE raising anything. Treat the application_name startup parameter through Supavisor as unverified (test it on a staging connection before relying on pg_stat_activity attribution). A hono/timeout middleware only frees the client; it does not cancel the query or release the pool connection, so it is not a substitute for server-side statement_timeout (see no-statement-or-request-timeouts). Add a /ready endpoint with a 1 s select 1 but keep /health dependency-free as designed. Region check (droplet lon1 vs Supabase region) is the highest-value item here and costs nothing.

confirmed.title: No statement_timeout, idle_in_transaction timeout, or HTTP request timeout anywhere, so one slow query or stuck transaction can pin the whole pool
confirmed.current: postgres.js is created without statement_timeout / idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, the Hono app has no timeout middleware, and the Node server is started with defaults. Only Redis rate-limit checks are bounded (rate-limiter.ts:RATE_LIMIT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS). Admin overview, caseload, progress reports and analytics aggregates are unbounded reads over tables that will grow (analytics_page_event, submissions, group members). The daily analytics rollup runs three large aggregate queries concurrently (Promise.all) and each holds a pooled connection for its full duration.
confirmed.breaks_at: A single report on a few hundred thousand rows taking 20-60 s, run by 10 admins (or one admin refreshing), consumes the entire 10-connection pool; all other users queue indefinitely because nothing times out. A crashed handler mid-transaction leaves the backend idle-in-transaction until the pooler reaps it.
confirmed.fix: 1) Create a dedicated DB role for the app runtime (e.g. pearl_app) and `ALTER ROLE pearl_app SET statement_timeout='30s'; SET idle_in_transaction_session_timeout='15s'; SET lock_timeout='10s'` - role-level GUCs apply on backend start and work through Supavisor, unlike the `options` startup parameter which the transaction pooler does not honour. Keep migrations (DIRECT_DATABASE_URL, session pooler) on the owner role without these timeouts, or `SET statement_timeout=0` in the migration session. 2) For known heavy reports/rollups use `SET LOCAL statement_timeout='120s'` inside a transaction (or a separate pool with its own limits for jobs). 3) Add hono/timeout (25-30 s) on the api, returning 504, and set server.requestTimeout/headersTimeout on the node server. 4) Surface timeouts as 503/504 with retry hints in handleError rather than a generic 500.
confirmed.flow_risk: A too-aggressive statement_timeout will abort legitimately slow flows: course import, audience import (CSV up to 25k chars), compliance bulk assign/reset (see bulk-tx finding), agent course generation, certificate/report exports, analytics rollup. Identify and exempt those with SET LOCAL before enabling, and roll out in two steps (log-only via pg_stat_statements max_exec_time first). Marking/completion transactions (marking.ts, recordCompletionIfComplete) are short and unaffected. Tutor caseload and admin overview should be measured first since they are the likeliest to exceed 30 s on big orgs.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: drizzle.ts has no statement_timeout/idle_in_transaction option, grep of apps/api/src/app.ts and index.ts finds no timeout middleware or server.requestTimeout. Unbounded admin/report/rollup queries can pin pool connections. Real risk but it only materialises once tables are large and heavy reports are run concurrently, so medium rather than high today.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Effort is L, not M. A dedicated pearl_app role needs grants on every table/sequence, default privileges so future migrations stay accessible, RLS roles (authenticated/anon) interplay, and a new Supavisor user (pearl_app.<project-ref>); migrations must keep the owner role. Step 1 (ALTER ROLE ... SET statement_timeout) is correct in mechanism for Supavisor, but the simpler first step is measurement: use pg_stat_statements max_exec_time to find the slow statements, then use SET LOCAL statement_timeout inside targeted transactions for known heavy reads, and only then apply a role-level 30 s. Exempt rollup, course/audience import, compliance bulk, agent generation, exports. hono/timeout alone does not release connections. idle_in_transaction_session_timeout of 15 s will also kill the SSO external-call transactions and approveRegistration's tx (which spans onboardLearner), so fix those first.

confirmed.title: Pool timeouts/errors are converted into 'no org membership' and 'logged out' instead of retryable 5xx
confirmed.current: customSession catches any DB error from getUserOrgRolesMap/profile select and returns { orgRoles: {}, status: 'ACTIVE' }. The api middleware catches any getSession error and treats the caller as anonymous (401). The dashboard getSessionData swallows errors and returns null (redirect to /login). The dashboard's isMemberOfOrg treats an empty orgRoles as 'not a member' and fires the auto-join POST. Net effect of a transient connection error or a statement timeout under load: signed-in users briefly get 403 'UNAUTHORIZED' on org routes (orgMemberMiddleware reads orgRoles[orgId]), bounce to /login, or trigger auto-join/pending-invite UI.
confirmed.breaks_at: Appears only under DB pressure (pool exhaustion, pooler restart, Supabase maintenance), exactly when load is highest; it looks like random logouts and 'no access' pages and floods system_event_log with auth.session_invalid_bounce events (dashboard hooks.server.ts reports every bounce to the api, which itself needs the DB).
confirmed.fix: Let infrastructure errors propagate: in customSession rethrow instead of returning empty roles (the DB error should fail the get-session call); in app.ts distinguish 'no session' (null) from 'error' and return 503 with Retry-After for errors; in the dashboard getSessionData return a distinct error state and render a retry page instead of redirecting to /login or treating orgRoles as empty. Keep fail-closed semantics (never default to ACTIVE with elevated roles). Keep the existing status default only for the 'row not found' case.
confirmed.flow_risk: All roles. Must keep deactivated users denied (resolveActor remains authoritative). Be careful not to create redirect loops: /login already calls get-session, so a 503 there must show an error, not redirect. The auto-join flow must only run when the membership lookup SUCCEEDED and was empty. Retry logic on the client should be bounded.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: auth.ts:283-298 catches any DB error and returns { orgRoles: {}, status: 'ACTIVE' }, app.ts:117-122 treats a getSession throw as anonymous, and dashboard session.ts:22-35 swallows errors to null. Nuance: resolveActor in app.ts:140 is outside any try/catch, so under a real DB outage the API middleware itself returns 500 for authenticated requests; the 'empty orgRoles -> 403/auto-join' path appears mainly on partial failures (customSession query fails but others succeed, statement timeout on that query). The dashboard null -> /login bounce is real.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Rethrow in customSession only after confirming the result path: have app.ts distinguish getSession error (503 + Retry-After) from null session (401), and have dashboard getSessionData return a tri-state (session | none | error) so error renders a retry screen, never /login redirect (the login page itself calls get-session, risk of loop) and never sets orgRoles to {}. Auto-join must run only when the membership lookup succeeded and returned empty. Keep resolveActor authoritative and fail closed. Bounded client retry only.

confirmed.title: Bulk admin operations run unbounded per-row work and per-member transactions, monopolising the pool
confirmed.location: apps/api/src/services/cohort/cohort.ts:208-300 (Promise.allSettled over every member, each opening db.transaction, pre-tx queries also per member); apps/api/src/services/course/compliance.ts:321-360,435-500,504-560,571-660 (per-learner statements inside one transaction; runComplianceExpiryCheck opens one transaction per record serially); packages/utils/src/validation/cohort/cohort.ts:24-38 (members array has no .max())
confirmed.current: addCohortMembers fans out `Promise.allSettled(data.members.map(...))`; each member does getProfileByEmail, getCohortMemberByProfileId, then db.transaction with 3-5 statements. The validation schema has no upper bound on members. Compliance assign/reset/waive loop over every target learner issuing 1-2 statements each inside a single long transaction (a connection is held for N x round-trip). runComplianceExpiryCheck loads all ready records and runs a transaction per record sequentially.
confirmed.breaks_at: Adding a 2,000-learner cohort queues 2,000 concurrent tasks on a 10-connection pool: the pool is fully occupied for tens of seconds and interactive traffic (heartbeats, page loads, marking) stalls behind it. A compliance assignment to 5,000 learners keeps one connection in a transaction for 5,000 x ~10 ms = 50 s+, holding row locks the learners' own progress updates may need.
confirmed.fix: 1) Add .max(500) (matching the 500 cap already used for profileIds) to ZAddCohortMembers.members. 2) Replace per-member work with set-based statements: resolve all emails with one `WHERE email = ANY(...)`, existing membership with one query, then one multi-row insert ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING inside a single short transaction (the helpers insertOrganizationMembersOnConflictDoNothing / insertGroupMembersOnConflictDoNothing already accept arrays). 3) For compliance, build the rows array and use a single insert ... on conflict and one update ... where id = ANY(...). 4) Where per-item logic must stay, use the existing mapWithConcurrency helper (audience.ts, EMAIL_SEND_CONCURRENCY) with a limit of 3-4 so bulk work can never use more than ~30% of the pool. 5) Chunk (500 rows) to stay far below the 65,534 bind-parameter limit of a multi-row insert. 6) Move runComplianceExpiryCheck's loop into a batched statement.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin/manager flows: cohort member add, compliance assign/reset/waive, expiry job. Preserve per-row result reporting (createdCount/updatedCount/skippedCount, already-member 409 messages) - set-based rewrites must still return the same per-member outcome shape that the UI shows. Capacity checks (cloud only) and the 'already a member' error must stay per member. Do not widen tutor visibility: tutor cohort additions are authorised before this service is called.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: cohort.ts:208-300 maps every member through Promise.allSettled, each doing getProfileByEmail + getCohortMemberByProfileId then its own db.transaction; ZAddCohortMembers.members has .min(1) and no .max(). compliance.ts assign/reset (lines 435-500, 504, 571) loop per learner inside one transaction, holding a connection for N round trips. Real; impact only appears for very large batches, and these are rare admin actions, so medium (arguably low-medium).
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Adding .max(500) can reject bulk adds that work today if the UI or an import path sends more than 500 members; check the callers and chunk client-side first, or enforce the cap server-side by chunking the work rather than rejecting. Prefer chunked set-based statements (ANY(array) lookups and multi-row INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, existing helpers accept arrays) while preserving the per-member result/errors shape ({added, errors}) the UI renders and the per-member 'already a member' 409 text. Capacity check per member is cloud-only and must be computed up front for the batch, not per member inside the tx (it also uses bare db inside the tx, same nested-pool bug as finding 1). Tutor authorisation happens before this service; do not widen it.

confirmed.title: Every 4xx/5xx, login and analytics beacon is an unbatched fire-and-forget INSERT on the same small pool
confirmed.current: recordApiError inserts one system_event_log row for EVERY AppError < 500 (404, 403, 409, 400, 429...) and every 500, each as its own statement with no backpressure (void Promise). Login success/failure/logout also insert. POST /dash/track (analytics beacons, up to 50 events per call) and trackServerEvent insert synchronously into analytics_page_event, which has 5 secondary indexes (including a low-cardinality event_type index), after the request has already paid the 3-query auth pipeline.
confirmed.breaks_at: During an incident (pool exhaustion, scanner hitting 404s, DB blip) error volume rises, which creates more inserts competing for the same connections, which causes more errors: a positive feedback loop. At 2-3k concurrent users, page_event writes (one beacon per navigation) become a dominant write load: 5 index updates per row.
confirmed.fix: 1) Buffer events in memory (array flushed every 1-2 s or at 100 rows with one multi-row INSERT) with a bounded queue that drops (and counts) on overflow; flush on SIGTERM. For multi-replica, push to a Redis list and let the jobs worker drain it in batches. 2) Sample or skip 4xx noise: record 404/401/403 at most once per (path,status,minute) or only >=429/5xx plus a counter. 3) Make /dash/track respond 202 immediately and enqueue; skip auth pipeline work for it (only decode the cookie user id). 4) Drop idx_ape_event_type (low selectivity) if pg_stat_user_indexes shows it unused - Supabase advisor already lists 74 unused indexes.
confirmed.flow_risk: Observability only; admin 'System events' screen (dash/system-events) and analytics dashboards read these tables, so batching delays visibility by seconds. Security-relevant events (login failures, deactivated sign-in, rate-limited) should keep flush latency low and must not be dropped by sampling. Page-view funnels (landing views, enrolments) must keep exact counts, so only apply sampling to error rows, not analytics events.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly overstated. recordApiError (app.ts:65, called from onError at 328/333) only fires for errors that propagate to Hono onError; most routes catch and call handleError directly, so the 'every 4xx/5xx' claim is exaggerated. /dash/track already batches: ingestEventBatch -> insertPageEvents does one multi-row INSERT for up to 50 events (queries/analytics.ts:427), so 'unbatched beacons' is wrong for the beacon path; only trackServerEvent writes single rows. Feedback loop during an outage is theoretically real but self-limiting (recordSystemEvent catches and logs). analytics_page_event does have 5 secondary indexes (schema.ts:222-228), so idx_ape_event_type is a legitimate drop candidate if pg_stat_user_indexes shows it unused.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Low priority. Cheapest safe step: drop 404/401/403 from system_event_log or rate-limit per (path,status,minute) and drop idx_ape_event_type if unused. Do not sample security events (login failures, deactivated sign-in). Skip the in-memory/Redis buffering unless measurements show the insert load matters.

confirmed.title: better-auth session and verification tables are never purged and session lacks indexes, while analytics_page_event has no retention
confirmed.location: packages/db/src/schema.ts:113-130 (session), :155-168 (verification), :202-230 (analytics_page_event); apps/jobs/src/workers/maintenance.ts:27-89 (no session/verification/page-event purge; only system_event_log 90 d); packages/db/src/queries/organization/users.ts:99; packages/db/src/queries/dash/admin-overview.ts:321-327
confirmed.current: session has only the PK, unique(token) and a FK to user with no index on user_id or updated_at (migration 0000 line 1378 adds the FK only). better-auth deletes an expired session only when that session is presented again, so abandoned sessions (7-day expiry, one per device per login) and expired verification rows (login-link, email verification, password reset) accumulate forever. Queries filtering on session.user_id (deleteSessionsByUserId on deactivation, analytics last-seen, better-auth listSessions/revoke) and session.updated_at (Online now) sequentially scan. analytics_page_event is append-only with no purge job and is scanned by the daily rollup.
confirmed.breaks_at: Thousands of learners logging in daily across several devices produce hundreds of thousands of session rows per quarter; each heartbeat UPDATE and each Online-now poll degrades; page_event grows by a row per navigation per user and the rollup's 3 concurrent aggregates start exceeding the pool/timeout budget.
confirmed.fix: 1) Migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_session_user_id ON session(user_id); idx_session_updated_at ON session(updated_at); idx_session_expires_at ON session(expires_at); idx_verification_expires_at ON verification(expires_at) and identifier index if used by lookups. (Part of the 103 unindexed FKs advisor.) 2) Add maintenance jobs (BullMQ schedulers beside system-event-purge-scheduler) that DELETE in batches of 5,000 (loop with LIMIT via ctid/id subselect) for session WHERE expires_at < now() - 1 day, verification WHERE expires_at < now() - 1 day, and analytics_page_event older than the retention you choose after rollups are confirmed (e.g. 90-180 days). 3) Consider monthly partitioning of analytics_page_event later.
confirmed.flow_risk: Purging only expired rows cannot log anyone out. Verify the impersonation (imp_admin) and login-link sessions use normal expires_at. Do not delete page events before the daily rollup has covered that day (rollup reads yesterday only, so 30+ days of slack is safe). Batch deletes must be small and run off-peak so they do not hold locks or create long transactions. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside drizzle-kit's migration transaction - ship as a manual/non-transactional migration.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: schema.ts session table (lines 113-130) has only PK, unique(token) and FK on user_id with no index on user_id/updated_at/expires_at; no migration creates one (grep for ON "session" in migrations found none). maintenance.ts handles only dead-letter, media reaper, asset cleanup, analytics rollup and system_event purge, so expired session/verification rows and analytics_page_event are never purged. deleteSessionsByUserId and Online-now would seq-scan as the table grows. Real, but cost is gradual.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do NOT index session.updated_at (kills HOT updates for the heartbeat). Index session.user_id, session.expires_at (for the purge) and verification.expires_at. While tables are still tiny (40 users), a plain CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS inside a normal drizzle migration is fine and far simpler than a manual CONCURRENTLY migration; only use CONCURRENTLY once tables are large. Purge jobs: batch deletes of expired rows (expires_at < now() - 1 day), 5000 per batch, off-peak; for analytics_page_event choose retention only after confirming the rollup has run for those days.

confirmed.title: Every api container start runs migrations and seeds over the session pooler with extra short-lived pools
confirmed.current: The api entrypoint runs `pnpm --filter @cio/db db:setup` before starting the server unless SKIP_DB_SETUP=true. db-setup opens postgres(connectionString,{ssl}) with the default max (10), a second max:1 connection holding pg_advisory_lock, spawns drizzle-kit migrate (another session connection), then spawns the essential seed which imports drizzle.ts and opens a runtime pool of up to 10 on DATABASE_URL (6543). Steps are serialised by the advisory lock (good) but each replica start spends 10-60 s and 3+ session-pooler connections before listening.
confirmed.breaks_at: Scaling out or rolling restarts of N replicas: N containers contend for the lock while the healthcheck start_period (40 s) elapses, and session-pooler slots (shared pool with other session clients and the Supabase Storage/Auth services) are consumed. Slow migrations delay recovery after a crash loop: a restart storm of the api that all re-run seeds can exhaust the 5432 budget.
confirmed.fix: Split concerns: add a one-shot `migrate` compose service (restart: 'no') that runs db:setup once per deploy, make api depend_on it with condition: service_completed_successfully, and set SKIP_DB_SETUP=true on api replicas. Give db-setup/baseline/db-reset clients `max: 1` (the `sql` handle at db-setup.ts:68 and baseline.ts:123 only need one) and make the seed use a max:2 pool. Document that the migrate service uses DIRECT_DATABASE_URL (5432) and everything else DATABASE_URL (6543).
confirmed.flow_risk: Deploy flow only; no user flow touches it. Be sure a failed migration blocks api start (service_completed_successfully does) so a half-migrated schema is never served. Keep the advisory lock for manual concurrent runs. The first-boot role creation (authenticated/anon) and essential seed (roles, submissions, question-types) must still run before the api serves traffic.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: docker/entrypoint-api.sh runs pnpm db:setup unless SKIP_DB_SETUP=true, and db-setup.ts opens a postgres client, a max:1 advisory-lock client, drizzle-kit migrate and the seed. But the claim of 10 connections per client is overstated: postgres.js opens connections lazily and these scripts issue sequential queries, so each uses roughly 1 connection. With a single api container this is a non-issue; it only matters for multi-replica or restart storms.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Low priority. If done: a one-shot migrate service with restart: no and api depends_on condition service_completed_successfully, reusing the same api image/command so there is no extra 20-45 min build. Add max:1 to the db-setup/baseline clients as hygiene. Keep the first-boot role creation and essential seed in the migrate step so they still run before the api serves traffic.

confirmed.title: The deploy topology and some in-process state cannot be scaled past one api replica without surprises
confirmed.location: docker-compose.deploy.yaml:30,89,119 (fixed container_name), :90-95 (PRIVATE_SERVER_URL=http://api:3081); docker/Caddyfile:22; packages/db/src/auth.ts:132-142 (better-auth rateLimit default memory storage); apps/api/src/utils/origins.ts and packages/db/src/utils (in-process custom-domain registry); apps/api/src/index.ts
confirmed.current: container_name on api/dashboard/jobs prevents `docker compose up --scale api=N`. The dashboard reaches the api via the compose service DNS name; Node's undici fetch with keep-alive pins to the first resolved address, so extra replicas would receive little traffic. better-auth rateLimit has no `storage` set, so per-IP login/password-reset throttles live in each process's memory: with N replicas the real limit is N x LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT.max and a restart resets it. (App-level rate limiter and BullMQ already use Redis.) Custom-domain trusted-origin registry is process-local (cloud-only feature). better-auth sessions are read from Postgres every cache miss; no secondaryStorage.
confirmed.breaks_at: As soon as a second api replica is added on this or another droplet: uneven load, login brute-force limit weaker, and the DB pool math from the sizing finding multiplies.
confirmed.fix: 1) Remove container_name for api and jobs; put a Caddy/nginx upstream pool (reverse_proxy api1:3081 api2:3081 with lb_policy) or let the dashboard talk to a small Caddy internal upstream; set undici Agent with limited keepAliveTimeout/connections so DNS round robin rebalances. 2) Configure better-auth rateLimit storage on Redis via secondaryStorage (get/set/delete adapter over the existing redis client) - this also lets sessions be served from Redis, removing the session SELECT/UPDATE load from Postgres, but it changes where sessions live, so deleteSessionsByUserId, the Online-now query and login-link/token-exchange session inserts must be adapted; treat as phase 2. 3) Run jobs as exactly one replica (BullMQ schedulers use upsertJobScheduler so duplicates are idempotent, but double concurrency doubles the DB budget). 4) Confirm graceful shutdown (next finding) before rolling restarts.
confirmed.flow_risk: Switching rate-limit storage to Redis: if Redis is down better-auth must fall back to allowing sign-in rather than blocking all logins (wrap the adapter and fail open with a short timeout). Moving sessions to Redis would affect deactivation (sessions must still die immediately - ACCESS.md) and impersonation; do not do it without tests. LB changes touch the cookie/forwarded-host handling used for auth baseURL (x-forwarded-host/proto) so verify OAuth-free email/password sign-in still works.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: container_name on api/dashboard/jobs (compose lines 30, 89, 119) blocks --scale; better-auth rateLimit config (auth.ts:132-142) sets no storage so counters are per-process memory. Everything else is future-looking and only applies when a second replica is added. Note the single 2 vCPU droplet running a single-threaded Node api will hit CPU/pool limits before replica count matters, and the first sensible step is 2 api replicas on the same host, which does need these changes.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Treat as a pre-requisite checklist for the day replicas are added, not work for now. Do not move sessions to Redis secondaryStorage (deactivation must kill sessions immediately, impersonation, Online-now); limit to rate-limit storage in Redis with fail-open on Redis errors. Run exactly one jobs replica.

confirmed.title: api, dashboard and jobs have no SIGTERM handling and never close the DB pool
confirmed.location: apps/api/src/index.ts:25-37; apps/api/src/process-error-guards.ts; apps/jobs/src/workers/*.ts (each registers its own SIGTERM that calls process.exit(0) after closing only its worker and Redis); packages/db/src/drizzle.ts:33-43
confirmed.current: The api starts @hono/node-server `serve` and never closes it on SIGTERM; docker stop therefore waits 10 s and SIGKILLs, aborting in-flight requests and open transactions (the pooler then rolls them back). The six jobs workers each install a separate SIGTERM handler, the first one calls process.exit(0) while others are mid-job; none call sql.end() on the shared postgres.js pool.
confirmed.breaks_at: Every deploy or restart (images are rebuilt on the droplet, so restarts are frequent): users mid-submission or mid-marking get a 502 and an aborted transaction; with several replicas rolling restarts drop requests; BullMQ jobs are re-delivered after the stall interval (duplicates of non-idempotent side effects like emails use idempotency keys, fine).
confirmed.fix: Export a closeDb() from drizzle.ts (`await databaseClient.end({timeout: 5})`). In the api, keep the server handle, on SIGTERM stop accepting (server.close()), wait up to ~8 s for in-flight, then closeDb(), then exit; flip /health only if you add a readiness probe. In jobs, centralise one shutdown in bootstrap.ts that closes all workers (worker.close() waits for active jobs) then closeDb. Set `stop_grace_period: 20s` in compose.
confirmed.flow_risk: All flows benefit; risk is only that a long-running request delays shutdown - bound with the timeout. Make sure the shutdown handler is idempotent and does not mask the existing unhandled-rejection guards.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: apps/api/src/index.ts calls serve() and registers no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler and never closes the postgres.js pool; each jobs worker registers its own SIGTERM handler that closes only its own worker, quits Redis and then calls process.exit(0), so the first to finish kills the others mid-job (emails.ts:68-73 pattern, repeated in 6 workers). Every deploy recreates the container anyway, so impact is a few seconds of aborted in-flight requests per deploy.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: A Node SIGTERM handler only helps if the signal reaches node: entrypoint-api.sh ends with exec pnpm --filter @cio/api start, so pnpm (not node) is PID 1 and may not forward the signal; change the final line to exec node on the built entry (or confirm pnpm forwards). Centralise jobs shutdown in one handler that closes all workers (Promise.all) then closeDb, then exits. Set stop_grace_period 20s.

confirmed.title: SSO provider registration/deletion wrap an external IdP/Better-Auth call in db.transaction without using the transaction
confirmed.current: createSsoConnection and deleteSsoConnection call db.transaction(async () => { await authApi.registerSSOProvider(...) (OIDC discovery over HTTP) ; createOrganizationSsoConfig(...) ... }) but never use the `tx` argument, so (1) a pooled connection sits idle-in-transaction for the duration of the outbound HTTP call and (2) the writes run on other connections, so the transaction provides no atomicity (a failure after registerSSOProvider leaves a provider with no config row).
confirmed.breaks_at: Low volume today and the SSO/tokenExchange plugins are dropped on self-hosted builds (auth.ts:buildStrangerAccountPlugins), so impact is limited to the cloud variant or a future enablement; each call can hold a connection for the IdP timeout (seconds).
confirmed.fix: Do the external registerSSOProvider call first, outside any transaction, then write the config/policy rows inside db.transaction(tx => ...) passing tx to the queries; on DB failure compensate by calling deleteSSOProvider. Apply the same shape to delete (external call outside, DB deletes inside).
confirmed.flow_risk: Enterprise SSO admin flow only (not used by self-hosted PearlLMS roles). Keep the compensation path so a failed config write does not leave a registered provider that could JIT-create users.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed at sso.ts:73 and :200: db.transaction(async () => ...) never uses tx; registerSSOProvider/deleteSSOProvider (external HTTP) run while a pooled connection is idle in transaction and the DB writes run on other connections, so there is no atomicity. SSO is cloud-only (plugins dropped on self-hosted), so no impact on current prod.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Matches the finding: external call first outside any tx, then writes in db.transaction(tx => ...) passing tx, with deleteSSOProvider compensation on DB failure. Low priority.

confirmed.title: Public API / automation-key requests await a write to the api-key row on every call
confirmed.current: After authenticating the bearer key (one SELECT), the middleware awaits touchOrganizationApiKeyLastUsedService, an UPDATE on the same api-key row for every request. Integrations (e.g. polling clients) can issue many requests per second with the same key, so they serialize on one row lock and each request pays a write.
confirmed.breaks_at: A busy integration at 20-50 req/s turns into 20-50 contended UPDATEs/s on one row and holds a pooled connection for the extra round trip; the lock queue adds latency under load.
confirmed.fix: Make lastUsedAt best-effort and throttled: skip the write if the cached value is newer than 60 s (keep lastUsedAt in an in-process Map or Redis SET NX EX 60 gate) and do not await it (void ... .catch). Optionally cache authenticateOrganizationApiKeyService results by key hash for 30-60 s with invalidation on revoke/rotate.
confirmed.flow_risk: Only API-key integrations. A revoked key must stop working immediately: if you add an authentication cache, delete the entry on revoke/rotate and keep TTL short. lastUsedAt becomes accurate to ~1 minute, which only affects the admin 'last used' display.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: automation-key.ts:19-33 awaits touchOrganizationApiKeyLastUsedService (an UPDATE) on every request, inside the same try/catch whose catch returns 401, so a transient DB error on the lastUsedAt write rejects an otherwise valid key. Only integration clients are affected and call volume is unknown, so low.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Make the touch fire-and-forget with .catch, and throttle to once per ~60 s per key (in-process Map is fine). Do not add an auth-result cache unless revoke/rotate delete the entry; if added keep TTL <=30 s.

confirmed.title: Session reminders are re-sent every ~6h (and re-checked in DB every 15 min) because dedupe relies on a short-lived BullMQ jobId
confirmed.current: The 15-min scan enqueues an email per (lesson, student, offset) with jobId session-reminder:lesson:profile:offset. The only guard is BullMQ jobId uniqueness, which lasts only while the completed job is retained: removeOnComplete {age 6h, count 5000}. The 24h offset condition is 'minutesUntil <= 1440', true for the whole 24h before the session, so once the first job is pruned (6h, or earlier once more than 5000 email jobs complete) the next scan creates a new job and the learner gets another 'in about 24 hours' mail (up to ~4 per session, plus a stale 24h mail even 30 min before start). Each scan also runs a preference lookup (a personal-settings query per distinct profile, EmailPreferenceLookupCache) for every row before the dedupe is even consulted. The SQL has no index on lesson.lesson_at/call_url.
confirmed.breaks_at: Already happening with 1 org: any learner with a session within 24h gets repeated reminders. At ~1,000 learners x 3 sessions per window: ~1,000 sequential DB preference queries + ~6,000 Redis add calls every 15 min; the 5000-count cap on completed email jobs is exceeded by a single bulk send, so even the 1h reminder dedupe fails and causes duplicate-mail storms (SES reputation/complaints).
confirmed.fix: Replace jobId-as-ledger with a durable ledger table session_reminder_sent(lesson_id, profile_id, offset_minutes, sent_at) with a unique key (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING, enqueue only on a returned row). Narrow trigger windows to the offset crossing (e.g. 24h: 1440-30 < minutesUntil <= 1440; 1h: 60-30 < m <= 60) so a missed scan is still covered by a 2x-interval window plus the ledger. Pre-filter rows by the ledger in SQL (LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL) so already-reminded rows never reach preference/enqueue. Batch the preference lookup (one query for all org/profile settings per scan). Add a partial index on lesson(lesson_at) WHERE call_url IS NOT NULL. Optionally keep the jobId as a secondary guard and use removeOnComplete age >= 48h for the emails queue.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner reminders only (tutors/admins unaffected). Edge cases: lesson time edited after a reminder was sent (key on lesson_id + lesson_at epoch or clear ledger rows on reschedule, since notify-session-update already sends an updated invite); learner enrolled <24h before the session (skip 24h, still send 1h); timezone label unaffected; first deploy must backfill/seed the ledger for sessions already inside the window to avoid a one-time duplicate wave. Preference opt-outs must still be honoured.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. session-reminder-scan.ts uses only jobId session-reminder:lesson:profile:offset. QUEUE_DEFAULTS emails keeps completed jobs for age 6h and count 5000, so the jobId disappears. listUpcomingSessionsForReminderScan has a 25h horizon and the 24h gate is only `minutesUntil > offset -> skip`, so the 24h branch is true for the whole last 24h. After the first job is pruned, the next 15-min scan re-adds it and the learner is mailed again, about 4 times per session. A stale '24 hours' mail 30 min before start follows from the same condition. The 5000-count eviction also makes the 1h dedupe fragile at thousands of learners. Preference lookups are cached per (profile, org) within a scan, so DB cost is bounded; the lesson.lesson_at index claim is low value because the lesson table is small.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Ledger table with a unique key and INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING is right. Key it on (lesson_id, profile_id, offset, lesson_at epoch) so a rescheduled session re-reminds. Narrow windows to about 2x the scan interval. Cheaper interim fix: raise emails removeOnComplete age to >=48h and drop the count cap, or use a Redis SET NX key with a TTL past the session start. Use the ledger insert result to gate the enqueue, not just the jobId. The 'seed ledger' concern largely disappears once the windows are narrowed. A DB migration goes through the session pooler, so do it as a normal migration. Learner-only; the tutor allocation rule is unaffected.

confirmed.title: If Redis is down or slow, every API request that awaits an enqueue hangs indefinitely (no timeout, offline queue enabled, retries disabled)
confirmed.current: Producers share one ioredis connection built with maxRetriesPerRequest:null and enableOfflineQueue:true, so queue.add() during an outage never rejects: commands are queued in memory and the awaiting HTTP handler waits until Redis returns. Only the 'REDIS_URL not set' case degrades gracefully (isRedisConfigured). All try/catch blocks around enqueueTransactionalEmail therefore never fire during an outage. Grading, submission, enrolment, invite and course-completion handlers await the enqueue inline, so a Redis restart/AOF replay (redis:7 on the same 4GB droplet with no maxmemory) stalls these flows and piles up open requests and DB connections.
confirmed.breaks_at: Any Redis stall >~10-30s (OOM-kill on the shared droplet, AOF rewrite, container restart during the 20-45 min on-box image builds) once concurrent users are in the hundreds; unbounded memory growth from the offline queue; Caddy/browser timeouts surface as 502/504 on submit/grade/enrol.
confirmed.fix: Create a separate producer connection (createRedisConnection({ enableOfflineQueue:false, maxRetriesPerRequest:1, commandTimeout/connectTimeout ~2-3s })) for getSharedRedisConnection used by Queue/FlowProducer; keep the offline-queue/null-retries config only for Worker connections. Wrap enqueueEmailSend/enqueue* in a short Promise.race timeout and convert failure into a logged, non-throwing 'email_not_enqueued' result for best-effort flows; for must-not-lose events add a small DB outbox (pending_email table drained by the worker) as fallback. Set redis maxmemory (e.g. 512mb) with maxmemory-policy noeviction and a container memory limit so Redis fails predictably rather than via host OOM.
confirmed.flow_risk: Touches every flow that emails: enrolment, invite, grading, submission, course completion, announcements. Behaviour change: callers that currently never see an error will now see rejects, so each existing try/catch (already present at most call sites) must keep swallowing. Routes that rely on the job id (notify-exercise, notify-session, media pipeline, agent runs) must return a clear 503 'queue unavailable' instead of hanging. Do not set enableOfflineQueue:false on Worker connections or BullMQ blocking clients.
confirmed.verifier_note: Behaviour is confirmed. connection.ts DEFAULT_OPTIONS has maxRetriesPerRequest:null, enableOfflineQueue:true and a retryStrategy that never gives up. factories.ts gives Queue and FlowProducer the same getSharedRedisConnection(). During an outage queue.add() never rejects and awaiting handlers hang, so the try/catch blocks never fire. Severity is medium rather than high because Redis is a local container that compose does not recreate on app deploys, so an outage is rare. When it happens the blast radius is large: grading, submit and enrol requests hang.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Fail-fast producer connection is valid; BullMQ documents enableOfflineQueue:false for producers. Verified risk: BullMQ Queue creation and add wait for the connection to become ready, so first-use at boot is OK. Test cold start explicitly, and set connectTimeout and keep retryStrategy. Keep Worker, blocking and scheduler connections on the current config. The scheduler Queues in apps/jobs use createRedisConnection(), so they stay on the long-lived config. The Promise.race wrapper is secondary once the offline queue is off. A DB outbox is over-engineering for best-effort mails; only add it for must-not-lose events. Setting maxmemory with noeviction on a BullMQ Redis is correct. Do not use an eviction policy.

confirmed.title: SMTP/SES delivery has no connection pooling, no sending-rate limiter, and treats permanent failures like transient ones
confirmed.current: nodemailer.createTransport has no pool:true, maxConnections, maxMessages or rateLimit, so every message opens a fresh TCP+TLS+AUTH SMTP session (verify() also runs on first use and again after any init failure). The email Worker has concurrency 5 and no BullMQ limiter {max,duration}, so throughput is whatever the SMTP RTT allows, with no relation to the SES quota (sandbox 1/s, default prod ~14/s, daily cap). Throttle replies ('454 Maximum sending rate exceeded') and hard failures (550 5.1.1 unknown user, invalid address) both throw in extractProviderId and are retried identically: attempts 5 with exponential backoff 5s (5+10+20+40s, ~75s total). A provider/SES outage longer than ~75s dead-letters every queued mail; a bad address is retried 5 times (hurting reputation). Nothing handles bounces/complaints (no SES SNS webhook, suppression list or List-Unsubscribe header). A successful send is logged with the full provider response (PII) via console.log('Email status', res).
confirmed.breaks_at: A single fan-out of a few hundred mails (session update, quiz-assigned, newsfeed post to a large course) exceeds SES per-second limits and burns retry attempts; at thousands of learners, daily SES quota exhaustion and a high bounce rate can pause the SES account (blocks password resets too).
confirmed.fix: Use nodemailer pooled transport (pool:true, maxConnections 3-5, maxMessages 100, rateLimit set to ~80% of the SES per-second quota via env SMTP_RATE_PER_SEC). Add a BullMQ Worker limiter {max: N, duration: 1000} on the emails queue (env-driven). In processSendEmail classify errors: 4xx/throttling/ETIMEDOUT -> throw (retry); 5xx permanent / invalid recipient / ZodError -> throw UnrecoverableError (no retry, record suppression). Raise attempts to ~8 with backoff starting at 30-60s (exponential, cap ~15 min) for the emails queue, with custom jitter. Add an SNS bounce/complaint webhook that writes an email_suppression table checked in processSendEmail, and a List-Unsubscribe header for non-critical categories. Downgrade the success log to message id only.
confirmed.flow_risk: All outbound email for admin/tutor/learner/manager. Edge cases: SMTP_PORT 465 vs 587 pooling behaviour; Mailpit dev (SMTP_ALLOW_INSECURE) must still work; ICS attachments through the pool; suppression must never block password-reset/verification for an address that bounced once (treat only hard bounces and only for non-auth templates, or expire the suppression); changing attempts alters dead-letter timing.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: createTransport has no pool or rateLimit; the Worker has concurrency 5 and no limiter; sendWithNodemailer returns success:false and extractProviderId throws for 4xx and 5xx alike. Attempts 5 with exponential 5s gives 5+10+20+40, about 75s, so the arithmetic is right. Permanent failures are retried 5 times. ZodError from ZSendEmailPayload.parse is also retried 5 times. `console.log('Email status', res)` dumps the full nodemailer result including envelope and recipients. No bounce, complaint or suppression handling exists. Medium rather than high at today's volume: pooling is an optimisation, and the real scale risk is SES quota and reputation on bulk fan-outs.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Pool plus an env-driven rateLimit and a BullMQ limiter are fine. Classify errors by SMTP responseCode: 4xx and ETIMEDOUT/ECONNECTION retry; 5xx 550/553 and invalid-recipient throw UnrecoverableError. Do NOT suppress on a single hard bounce for auth templates (verifyEmail, forgotPassword); the auditor already notes this. Raise attempts and use a longer first backoff (30-60s). Test 465 vs 587 with pool:true and the ICS attachment through the pool. Verify with the real SES SMTP endpoint, not Mailpit. The Zoho branch (ZOHO_TOKEN) needs its own limiter if it is used.

confirmed.title: publishAnnouncement loops every recipient sequentially inside the admin's HTTP request, and the announcement email leg never fires
confirmed.current: The comment says 'fire-and-forget' but the code awaits emitNotification for the whole audience (all_learners/all_tutors/course/tutor group). emitNotification handles recipients strictly one at a time: one INSERT ... RETURNING into notification per recipient on the transaction pooler (~3-10 ms each). The announcement recipients are built as { userId, emailFields } with no email, so line 221 (!recipient.email) skips the email leg for every recipient: opted-in learners never get the announcement email (functional gap), while at the same time all of the per-recipient work is done synchronously.
confirmed.breaks_at: 5,000 learners -> 5,000 sequential round-trips = ~15-50 s in one request (Caddy/dashboard proxy timeouts, double-click re-publish creates a second announcement and a second set of rows); ties up a pool connection (max 10) while other users wait; also if later fixed to resolve emails per recipient it becomes 3+ queries/recipient plus a Redis add each.
confirmed.fix: Insert the announcement then enqueue ONE notifications-queue job (e.g. fan-out-announcement {announcementId}) with a deterministic jobId; in the worker resolve audience in pages of 500, bulk-insert notification rows (single multi-row INSERT per page), bulk-load notification_preference for the page (one IN query), join profile emails, and enqueue emails with addBulk, each with idempotencyKey announcement:{id}:{userId}. Return 201 immediately. Add email to recipients (join profile) so the opt-in email leg actually works. Add a unique (user_id,type,entity_id) guard for announcement.published rows to make the job re-runnable.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin publish (and only admin per ACCESS.md) plus learner/tutor feeds. Preserve audience rules: tutor audience must still go through listLearnersForTutor (allocated learners only), learner audience stays role 3 only; notifications will appear slightly after publish instead of instantly (bell is polled); retries must not duplicate in-app rows; enabling the email leg is a behaviour change (default is OFF, per category) so notify the owner.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed in announcements.ts:186-205 and notify.ts. publishAnnouncement awaits emitNotification, which loops recipients strictly sequentially with one INSERT ... RETURNING each, despite the 'fire-and-forget' comment. Recipients are built as {userId, emailFields} with no email, so `!recipient.email` at notify.ts skips the email leg for everyone. Announcement emails therefore never send, which is a functional bug today. At about 5k learners the request does thousands of sequential round-trips and ties up the pool; a double-click creates a second announcement. Publish is admin-only, so the frequency is low; the severity still holds because of the request length and the dead email feature.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Queue the fan-out and bulk-insert in pages, as proposed. When the email leg is enabled, bulk-resolve preferences (notification_preference IN query) and emails by joining profile, and use idempotencyKey announcement:{id}:{userId}. Keep resolveRecipients unchanged: the tutor audience must still go through listLearnersForTutor (allocated learners only) and the learner audience stays role 3. Enabling the email leg is a behaviour change, but the default category is OFF so most users are unaffected. Tell the owner. Add a client-side or idempotency guard against double publish. A unique partial index on notification(user_id, entity_id) WHERE type='announcement.published' makes the job re-runnable.

confirmed.title: Bulk import/assign enrolment fires unbounded Promise.all for membership inserts and email enqueues, each with its own preference lookups
confirmed.current: importAudienceMembers/assignAudienceToCourses build profiles x courses (or cohorts) pairs and run Promise.all over all of them (addCohortMember, enqueueTransactionalEmail). Each enqueueTransactionalEmail call with a preference creates a new EmailPreferenceLookupCache, so nothing is shared: every pair runs org-settings + personal-settings DB queries and a Redis add, all concurrently. The CSV cap is 25,000 chars (~1,000 addresses) and allCourses/allCohorts multiply it. mapWithConcurrency(…, 5) exists in the same file but is used only for the org-invite path.
confirmed.breaks_at: 1,000 learners x 10 courses = ~10,000 concurrent DB queries + 10,000 concurrent Redis adds against a postgres.js pool of max 10 on the Supabase transaction pooler (also contributes to the auth_db_connections_absolute advisor warning); request exceeds proxy timeout, other users' requests starve behind the pool queue, partial enrolment on timeout.
confirmed.fix: Replace Promise.all with mapWithConcurrency (5-10) or chunked batches of 100-200; batch DB writes (multi-row insert for members). Pass one shared EmailPreferenceLookupCache (or pre-resolve preferences with 2 IN-queries) into the enqueue helper (add an optional cache param to enqueueTransactionalEmail) and use queue.addBulk. For large imports (>~200 pairs) hand the welcome-email fan-out to a worker job and return the enrolment result immediately.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin audience import and tutor/admin assign-to-course flows; learners get welcome emails. Keep per-recipient idempotency keys unchanged (audience-course-welcome:group:profile) so re-runs do not double-send; keep the student-limit assertion (assertStudentCapacityOrThrow) before any inserts; emailsSent counter semantics must stay (count enqueued, not delivered); never widen tutor visibility (assign routes stay admin-gated).
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly accurate. The email Promise.all is confirmed (audience.ts ~213-239 and the cohort equivalent): each enqueueTransactionalEmail with `preference` constructs its own EmailPreferenceLookupCache, so every (profile, course) pair repeats the org-settings and personal-settings queries. The cohort path also does Promise.all(addCohortMember). But the COURSE membership insert is already a single multi-row addGroupMembers, so the 'membership inserts' claim is wrong for courses. postgres.js queues behind max 10, so it is slow rather than a crash. assign is capped at 500 profileIds and CSV at 25k chars, so worst case is about 500 x N courses of queued work in one request.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Use mapWithConcurrency (already in the file) or chunks of 100-200. Add an optional shared preference cache parameter to enqueueTransactionalEmail, built once per call, and prefetch the personal settings with one IN query. Batch the cohort inserts into one multi-row insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Do not change the idempotency keys. Keep assertStudentCapacityOrThrow before any insert. Offloading to a worker is only needed above about 1k pairs.

confirmed.title: Verification, forgot-password and reset-confirmation emails are sent inline in the API process, bypass the queue/retry, fail silently, and log tokens
confirmed.current: better-auth callbacks call sendEmail() directly, which awaits a brand-new SMTP session (verify + send) inside the auth request. deliverEmail swallows provider errors and returns {success:false}; neither caller checks it, so a failed password-reset/verification mail is reported to the user as sent and is never retried or dead-lettered. sendVerificationEmail does console.log('\nsendVerificationEmail', options), writing the user object and the verification URL (live token) to container logs on every signup.
confirmed.breaks_at: Signup/reset spikes (start of a cohort, many learners onboarding at once) make auth latency equal to SMTP RTT x concurrency; during an SES throttle/outage learners silently never receive verification or reset mail and cannot log in; tokens in logs are a security exposure once logs are shipped.
confirmed.fix: Enqueue these through the emails queue with a dedicated high-priority path (job priority 1 or a separate 'emails-critical' queue/worker with its own limiter), idempotencyKey per token (e.g. verify:{userId}:{tokenHash}); make sendEmail/processSendEmail throw on {success:false} so retries/dead letters work; remove the options console.log. Keep a direct-send fallback only when Redis is unavailable (with a short timeout).
confirmed.flow_risk: Signup, email change, forgot password for all roles (admin, manager, tutor, learner). Reset/verify links must keep using the same org branding/resolveVerificationOrg logic; enqueue latency adds a few seconds before delivery so UI copy ('check your email') is fine; ensure better-auth does not treat enqueue failure as a signup failure for verification (but should for forgot-password).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. email-verification.ts and email-password.ts call sendEmail() directly (a fresh SMTP session each time) and do not check the {success:false} result, so a failed reset or verification mail is silently treated as sent. `console.log('\nsendVerificationEmail', options)` writes the user object and the verification URL (live token) on every signup, and it runs BEFORE the trigger=app early return. The same pattern is in sendChangeEmailConfirmation (`console.log('\nsendChangeEmailConfirmation', options)`), which the finding missed.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do the cheap, high-value part first: remove both console.log lines now (security, effort S) and make the callers throw on {success:false} for forgot-password. Moving auth mail onto the queue is riskier than stated: password reset would then depend on Redis health, and with the current offline-queue config it could hang. Only do it after the fail-fast producer fix, with a direct-send fallback. If queued, use a priority or separate critical lane and idempotency keys keyed on the token hash, not the user id.

confirmed.title: Coursework notifications are emitted inline with no idempotency key and no per-tutor digest; one email per learner submission
confirmed.current: emitNotification enqueues emails with enqueueTransactionalEmail(..., {to, fields}) and no idempotencyKey (and no coalesce for submission.created/result.recorded; coalescing is only used for messages), so a client retry / double-submit / re-mark produces duplicate in-app rows and duplicate emails. The whole chain (getProfileById, getCourseWithOrgData, getLessonById, insert notification, preference lookup, Redis add) is awaited in the submission/marking request path and runs one recipient at a time. session.unlocked loops units sequentially.
confirmed.breaks_at: A tutor with 40-100 allocated learners each submitting several units per week receives one email per submission (hundreds/week) -> inbox flooding, SES complaints and rising unsubscribes; added 30-100 ms of notification latency to every submit/mark request that scales with allocated-tutor count.
confirmed.fix: Pass deterministic idempotency keys (type:entityId:userId:submissionId/resultId) through emitNotification to enqueueTransactionalEmail and add ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on notification for (user_id,type,entity_id,subject id). Apply coalesce:true (existing hasRecentUnreadForEntity window) or a daily digest job for submission.created. Move the whole emitNotification call to a 'notifications:emit' queue job (payload = type, recipients ids, entity) so the request returns immediately. Batch getNotificationPreference for multi-recipient emits. Keep the tutor recipient list sourced from listTutorsForLearner (allocation).
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor 'awaiting marking' alerts, learner 'result recorded' alerts, session-unlocked bell. Must not widen recipients beyond allocated tutors (ACCESS.md section 8). Coalescing must not suppress the in-app row (only the email); digest changes tutor expectations (tell the owner); retry-safe keys must not block a legitimate second result on the same unit (include result id).
confirmed.verifier_note: Mechanics are right (emitNotification passes no idempotencyKey; sequential per recipient; awaited in submit and mark). Impact is overstated. Recipients are the learner's allocated tutors (listTutorsForLearner, typically 1-2), so request latency does not scale with a tutor's caseload. Re-marking is blocked by getResultForSubmission at marking.ts:92, so duplicate result.recorded for the same submission is not reachable. Duplicate emails need a double-submit that the submit flow itself would also have to allow. The real remaining issue is tutor inbox volume (one mail per submission), which is a product decision, not a scalability bug.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: If done, key on type:submissionId:userId (include the submission or result id so a legitimate later result is not blocked) and keep the in-app row. Do not coalesce away the in-app row. Recipient list must stay sourced from listTutorsForLearner. Offer a digest as an owner option only. Do not move emitNotification to a queue just for latency; the saving is tens of ms.

confirmed.title: Scheduler-generated jobs have no removeOnComplete/removeOnFail/attempts, so Redis grows forever and failed rollups are never retried
confirmed.current: The worker-side Queue objects used for upsertJobScheduler are created without defaultJobOptions and the scheduler templates carry no opts, so the repeating jobs (media-job-reap every 5 min = 288/day, session-reminder-scan 96/day, analytics rollup, system-event purge) are stored with BullMQ defaults: kept in Redis forever on success and failure, attempts 1. QUEUE_DEFAULTS (attempts 2, removeOnComplete count 100) only applies to jobs added through getQueue(). Also removeOnFail for emails/notifications is age-only (7d, no count), so a provider outage retains every failed payload (with ics + branding HTML fields) unbounded for 7 days. The rollup uses a fixed 24h 'every' interval, so a missed run (worker down/deploy during its slot, DB error, no retry) permanently skips that day: daysAgo is always 1.
confirmed.breaks_at: ~140k completed scheduler jobs/year (tens of MB of Redis on an unlimited-memory instance on the 4GB shared box) and a Redis KEYS/Workbench slowdown; a single failed or missed rollup leaves analytics_*_daily gaps; an SES outage with 20k queued mails retains ~20k failed jobs for a week.
confirmed.fix: Pass opts in upsertJobScheduler(id, repeat, { name, data, opts: { ...QUEUE_DEFAULTS[queue], removeOnComplete: {count: 50}, removeOnFail: {count: 200} } }) and build the Queue with buildQueueOptions(). Add count caps to every removeOnFail in QUEUE_DEFAULTS (e.g. age 7d + count 5000). Replace the daily 'every' with a cron pattern (e.g. '15 0 * * *' UTC) and make the rollup backfill all days since max(date) in analytics_org_daily (catch-up loop, bounded to ~14 days). Delete the one-off existing completed scheduler jobs once (Queue.clean).
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin analytics dashboards (read rollup tables) and media job reaper. upsertJobScheduler replaces by scheduler id, so changing options is safe on next boot; changing 'every' to a cron pattern with the same id updates in place. Backfill is idempotent (UPSERT) so re-runs are safe.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed against bullmq@5.76.5: Queue.upsertJobScheduler merges this.jobsOpts (the Queue defaultJobOptions) with the template opts. The worker-side `new Queue(name,{connection})` objects in maintenance.ts and notifications.ts have no defaultJobOptions, so scheduler jobs get BullMQ defaults (kept forever, attempts 1). Volume is about 105k reap jobs plus 35k scan jobs per year, roughly tens of MB, so low urgency. QUEUE_DEFAULTS removeOnFail is age-only for emails and notifications. The rollup job has attempts 1 and a fixed daysAgo=1, so a missed or failed run leaves a permanent gap.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Pass opts in the template (or buildQueueOptions) with removeOnComplete {count:50} and removeOnFail {count:200}, and give the rollup attempts 2-3. Changing the scheduler `every` to a cron under the same id updates in place. Make the rollup catch up from max(date) with a bounded loop; it is idempotent via UPSERT. The one-off Queue.clean of old completed scheduler jobs is a data operation, so get the owner's approval.

confirmed.title: One FIFO emails queue and shared concurrency means bulk fan-outs delay time-critical mail; notifications worker reuses EMAIL_WORKER_CONCURRENCY
confirmed.current: All templates (invite, welcome, session reminders, quiz nudges, newsfeed, cohort goal reminders, submission/grade alerts) share one queue, FIFO with no job priority, one Worker with concurrency 5. The notifications worker (which itself fans out thousands of enqueues) is tuned by the same EMAIL_WORKER_CONCURRENCY variable. Every worker (media, transcribe, emails, notifications, maintenance, agent) runs in ONE Node process/container (apps/jobs/src/index.ts), alongside ffmpeg children, on the same 2 vCPU as API and dashboard.
confirmed.breaks_at: A 5,000-recipient quiz-assigned or reminder burst occupies the queue for minutes at the SES rate, so an invite, grade notification or password-related mail enqueued just after waits behind it; an ffmpeg transcode or agent run in the same process can delay email/notification processing and event-loop-sensitive lock renewals (stalled jobs).
confirmed.fix: Give BullMQ priority to transactional templates (priority 1 for invite/grade/auth, 10 for bulk reminders/newsfeed) in enqueueEmailSend via a template->priority map, or split bulk templates into an 'emails-bulk' queue with its own limiter. Add NOTIFICATIONS_WORKER_CONCURRENCY. Run media/transcribe workers as a separate container (Dockerfile.jobs comment already supports overriding CMD) with cpus/mem limits so ffmpeg cannot starve api/dashboard.
confirmed.flow_risk: Ordering of emails changes (priority) but no per-recipient ordering contract exists; dedupe jobIds unaffected. Compose change needs the on-droplet image build window; media jobs for tutors/admins uploading videos unaffected functionally.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: a single emails queue, FIFO, no priority, one Worker with concurrency 5. The notifications worker takes concurrency from EMAIL_WORKER_CONCURRENCY. All six workers are imported in apps/jobs/src/index.ts into one process. The ffmpeg-blocks-the-event-loop sub-claim is weak: ffmpeg runs through execFile as a child process, so lock renewal is not event-loop blocked. The CPU contention on the 2 vCPU box is real.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: A priority map in enqueueEmailSend is a cheap S-effort fix (BullMQ priority; dedupe jobIds are unaffected). Add a separate NOTIFICATIONS_WORKER_CONCURRENCY. Splitting the media workers into a separate container with cpus/mem limits is valid but belongs with the deploy-limits work and needs the on-droplet build window. Do not drop media concurrency below current need.

confirmed.title: Worker fan-out processors and newsfeed/cohort mail do N+1 sequential DB lookups per recipient
confirmed.current: Each processor awaits shouldSend + enqueueEmailSend serially per member; getPersonalSettings issues one query per profile (cache only helps repeats). Newsfeed post passes the recipient array with preference:{organizationId} but no profile ids, so for each course member getProfileByEmail then a personal-settings query run in the API process (fire-and-forget but still holds pool connections). runCohortGoalReminderScan calls enqueueTransactionalEmail per row, which constructs a fresh preference cache each time, so nothing is reused across rows. notify-course-exercise rethrows on a single enqueue error (whole job retried), while notify-session-update swallows the error and only logs (recipient silently skipped, 'notified' undercounted).
confirmed.breaks_at: 2,000-learner course: 2,000-6,000 sequential round-trips per nudge/newsfeed post/session edit (minutes, ties the single-concurrency pool). Inconsistent error handling loses invites on transient Redis/DB blips.
confirmed.fix: Add a batch method to EmailPreferenceLookupCache (prefetchPersonalSettings(profileIds, orgId) using inArray) and preload before the loop; resolve profile ids in the member query (already joined) so getProfileByEmail is never needed; use queue.addBulk in chunks of 500 for enqueue; share one cache across the whole scan in cohort goal reminders (add cache param). Normalise error policy: collect failures, retry only failed recipients (idempotency keys make re-enqueue safe), never silently drop. Move newsfeed post fan-out to a notifications queue job.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner mail for quizzes, sessions, newsfeed, cohort goals. Preference semantics must be identical (resolveEmailDelivery with org+personal settings); keep STUDENT-only role filter; newsfeed author exclusion must be preserved.
confirmed.verifier_note: Mostly confirmed. EmailPreferenceLookupCache.getPersonalSettings is one query per (profile, org). notify-course-exercise and notify-session-update loop serially. The newsfeed path passes only organizationId, so for each member it runs getProfileByEmail and then the personal-settings query, though it does share one cache per enqueueTransactionalEmail call. runCohortGoalReminderScan builds a fresh cache per row. The error-policy complaint is partly wrong: notify-course-exercise rethrowing is safe because the idempotency key `quiz-assigned:${jobId}:${email}` is stable across retries of the same job, so retry only re-adds the missing ones. notify-session-update swallowing is the inconsistent one and under-counts `notified`.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add prefetchPersonalSettings(profileIds, orgId) using inArray on organizationmember_email_notifications. Pass profile ids from the member query so getProfileByEmail is never needed. Share one cache across the cohort reminder scan. Make notify-session-update rethrow-or-collect like notify-course-exercise (keys already include sequence). Keep the STUDENT-only filter and the author exclusion. addBulk is optional; Redis round-trips are not the bottleneck.

confirmed.title: Compliance/cohort-goal scans run as long synchronous HTTP handlers, with per-row transactions, and have no scheduler
confirmed.current: check-expiry, send-reminders, evaluate-cohort-goals and send-cohort-goal-reminders execute the entire scan inside the request: runComplianceExpiryCheck opens one db.transaction per record (3 writes each), runComplianceReminderScan does a sequential update/insert per row over all latest records, evaluateGoal runs per goal (loads all cohort members), and the reminder scan enqueues mails per row with a fresh preference cache. Nothing in compose/BullMQ calls them (docs confirm), so as built the reminders never run; if someone adds an external cron, they hit HTTP/proxy timeouts (and a retry from the cron client reruns the scan concurrently).
confirmed.breaks_at: Thousands of compliance records/assignments: scans take minutes, exceed Caddy/client timeouts, hold pool connections, and overlap on retry (two scans race on status updates).
confirmed.fix: Turn each scan into a maintenance/notifications queue job with an upsertJobScheduler cron (daily 02:00/02:30 UTC per PRD), keep the /internal routes as thin 'enqueue now' endpoints returning a job id (like send-session-reminders already does). Inside, process in keyset-paginated chunks of ~500 with set-based UPDATE ... WHERE id = ANY, one transaction per chunk; use a Redis/BullMQ jobId or pg advisory lock so only one scan runs at a time.
confirmed.flow_risk: Compliance courses (admin/manager dashboards, learner status) and cohort goals; status transitions must remain idempotent (they already compare previous status); do not change the due-date/grace semantics; enabling the scheduler turns on emails that have never run in prod, so enable behind an env flag and confirm with the owner.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed no scheduler calls /internal/compliance/check-expiry, send-reminders, evaluate-cohort-goals or send-cohort-goal-reminders (grep finds only the route definitions). runComplianceExpiryCheck does one db.transaction per record; runComplianceReminderScan updates row by row. So compliance expiry cycles never roll over today. Correction: runComplianceReminderScan only writes course_completion_notification_event rows and status changes and does NOT send email, so 'enabling the scheduler turns on emails' applies only to the cohort-goal reminder scan. Only relevant if compliance or cohort goals are in use.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Schedule these as maintenance or notification jobs with a cron pattern, and make the route a thin enqueue. Add a single-run guard (jobId or advisory lock). Enable cohort-goal reminders behind an env flag after owner sign-off. Keep status transitions idempotent.

confirmed.title: Retention jobs are stubs or unscheduled; analytics page events, notifications and dead letters grow without bound, and the daily rollup scans the full event table
confirmed.current: deadLetterCleanup and retentionCompact have handlers but no scheduler (retentionCompact is a logged no-op: 'not-yet-implemented'); only system_event_log is purged (90d). analytics_page_event (written per page view), analytics_login_events, notification (one row per recipient per event) and media_job/job_step have no retention. The rollup queries filter only on occurred_at ranges, but the indexes are (org_id, occurred_at), (course_id, occurred_at) etc. with no leading occurred_at index, so each of the 3 parallel aggregates is a sequential scan of the whole table. notification has only idx_notification_user and (user_id, read_at): listing sorts per user, and nothing prunes read rows. Dead-letter rows have no replay UI/endpoint (markDeadLetterReplayed/listDeadLetterJobs have no callers) and emails/notifications dead letters store organization_id NULL.
confirmed.breaks_at: Thousands of learners x page views: tens of millions of event rows within months, daily rollup minutes of seq-scan load on the shared Supabase DB, bloat; notification table growth with each broadcast; failed mail becomes unrecoverable dead-letter rows.
confirmed.fix: Schedule dead-letter-cleanup (daily, 90-180d) and implement retention-compact: delete analytics_page_event older than ~90-180d in batches of 10k (after rollup has covered them), read notifications older than 90d, completed media_job/job_step older than 90d. Add index idx_ape_occurred_at on analytics_page_event(occurred_at) (BRIN is ideal for append-only) and drop low-value indexes (idx_ape_event_type, idx_ape_user if unused per advisor). Add index notification(user_id, created_at DESC). Add a replay admin action (or script) for dead letters and populate organizationId where known.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin analytics (reads *_daily rollups, so raw deletion after rollup is safe; keep unrolled days), learner notification bell (keep unread rows regardless of age). Batch deletes to avoid long locks on the pooler; index creation must use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (migrations run via session pooler).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: deadLetterCleanup has a handler but no scheduler; retentionCompact is a logged no-op; only system_event_log is purged; analytics_page_event indexes are (org_id, occurred_at), (course_id, occurred_at), session, event_type, user, with no leading occurred_at index, so the rollup scans the whole table; notification has only user and (user, read_at) indexes with no pruning. Volume is overstated: page events look like landing and course-page views rather than every learner page view, and notification is one row per recipient per event, so growth is gradual. Dead letters store the full payload (recipient email, HTML), with organization_id NULL for emails, no replay path and no cleanup, which is a PII retention concern.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (not allowed inside a transaction migration) for any new index, and add them only after checking pg_stat_user_indexes since 74 unused indexes were already flagged. The BRIN on occurred_at is a good fit. Delete in batches of 10k only after the rollup has covered the day. Keep unread notifications regardless of age. Schedule dead-letter-cleanup at 90 days.

confirmed.title: Graceful shutdown is not coordinated, containers have no stop grace/limits/healthcheck, and ffmpeg/Redis are unbounded on the shared 4GB droplet
confirmed.current: Each of the six workers registers its own SIGTERM handler that awaits worker.close() then calls process.exit(0): whichever finishes first terminates the process while other workers (e.g. a running ffmpeg/Whisper job or an email mid-send) are still active; compose has no stop_grace_period (Docker default 10s) so a long ffmpeg job is SIGKILLed anyway and the child ffmpeg process is orphaned. Interrupted jobs are re-run by BullMQ stall recovery (maxStalledCount default 1, then 'job stalled more than allowable limit' failure) giving at-least-once duplicate emails. ffmpeg/ffprobe run via execFile with no timeout and no -threads limit (uses all cores of the 2 vCPU that also serve API/dashboard); there is no mem_limit/cpus for any service, no maxmemory for redis, no jobs healthcheck, and uncaughtException is only logged so the process can continue in a bad state. reapStuckMediaJobs fails queued/running media jobs not updated for 30 min (updatedAt only changes at step boundaries), so a long transcode or a job waiting behind concurrency 2 is marked failed while still alive.
confirmed.breaks_at: Every redeploy (the on-droplet build/restart) during a media upload or notification burst; 1-2 concurrent long video jobs saturate CPU and slow every learner request; a hung ffmpeg holds a concurrency slot forever; Redis AOF rewrite + fork on a memory-tight box risks the OOM killer taking down api/redis.
confirmed.fix: Single shared shutdown in index.ts: SIGTERM -> close all workers in parallel with Promise.allSettled, wait up to N s, then exit; set stop_grace_period: 120s on jobs. Add timeout (e.g. 30-60 min, scaled by size) and -threads 1 / nice to execFile calls, kill the child on cancel. Add compose limits (jobs cpus 1.0, mem 1g; redis mem 512m with --maxmemory 400mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction; api/dashboard reservations). Add a jobs healthcheck (Redis ping + worker.isRunning). Make the reaper heartbeat-based (updateMediaJob touch from ffmpeg progress or reap only if no BullMQ active job exists) or raise the window to >= 2x the longest expected transcode. Exit on uncaughtException after logging so restart: unless-stopped recovers cleanly.
