confirmed.flow_risk: Admin/tutor video upload, thumbnail and transcript flows (media_job status), and email delivery during deploys. Do not lower worker concurrency below what current uploads need; the HLS/transcribe steps are idempotent via job_step ledger, so retries after a kill are safe; changing limits may OOM-kill ffmpeg on very large source videos, so test with the largest real upload first.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. Each of media.ts and emails.ts (and the others) registers its own SIGTERM handler that does worker.close() then process.exit(0). worker.close() waits only for that worker's active jobs, so an idle worker exits the whole process while an ffmpeg job is still running. compose has no stop_grace_period (Docker default 10s), no mem_limit or cpus, and redis runs with --appendonly yes and no maxmemory. ffmpegRun and ffprobeJson use execFile with no timeout and no -threads. reapStuckMediaJobs fails queued or running jobs whose updatedAt is older than 30 min while the BullMQ job can still be alive, and a job queued behind concurrency also ages. That reaper race is real and also marks the DB row failed while the worker later overwrites it.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: One shared shutdown in index.ts using Promise.allSettled and a grace period, plus stop_grace_period. Add timeouts and kill the child process. Make the reaper heartbeat-based or only reap when no BullMQ active job exists. Redis limits: use maxmemory with noeviction and a container limit, not an eviction policy. Limits on the jobs container must be tested against the largest real upload so ffmpeg is not OOM-killed; the box has 4 GB shared with api and dashboard.

confirmed.title: Quiz-assigned nudge has no cooldown or recipient cap, and session-update ICS method does not match the calendar semantics
confirmed.current: enqueueNotifyCourseExercise deliberately uses a fresh job per click ('no dedupe across clicks') and the idempotency key embeds the notify job id, so repeated clicks (or a double click) email the entire course every time with no rate limit/cooldown. Separately, the nodemailer path hard-codes icalEvent method: 'PUBLISH' regardless of the ICS body, while session updates are generated with METHOD:REQUEST and a higher SEQUENCE; the MIME method and the body disagree, so some clients treat the update as a new event instead of updating the existing one (Zoho path sends a plain attachment).
confirmed.breaks_at: A tutor/admin clicking 'notify' 3 times on a 2,000-learner course sends 6,000 mails; stacked calendar entries for learners after each session time edit.
confirmed.fix: Use a jobId of notify-exercise:{courseId}:{exerciseId}:{15-minute bucket} (or a Redis SET NX cooldown key) and return 429/'already sent recently' with the previous job id so the dashboard poll still works. Derive the MIME method from the ICS (parse METHOD line or add a method field on the payload and pass it through ZSendTemplateEmailPayload).
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor/admin 'notify learners' button and live-session edit flow; the dashboard polls getNotifyCourseExerciseStatusService with the returned job id, so a deduped click must return the existing id (not an error); legitimate re-nudge after the cooldown must still work.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: enqueueNotifyCourseExercise deliberately has no jobId, and the email idempotency key embeds the notify job id, so each click re-mails the whole course. The ICS mismatch is real: nodemailer.ts hard-codes icalEvent method 'PUBLISH' while notify-session-update builds METHOD:REQUEST with a SEQUENCE. Low impact, behaviour-only; the click frequency is bounded by staff.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: A cooldown must return the existing job id so the dashboard poll still works, and a deliberate re-nudge after the cooldown must still send. Derive the MIME method from the ICS body. Also the 24h reminder ICS uses sequence 0 and the same UID as later updates, so a re-sent reminder after an update would carry a stale sequence.

confirmed.title: AI course-generation runs share one global lane (concurrency 1) with 3 expensive retries and no per-org fairness
confirmed.current: AGENT_COURSE_GENERATION_WORKER_CONCURRENCY defaults to 1 for the whole platform; the queue is FIFO, so one org's long LLM run blocks every other org/tutor's course generation. The default job options retry a failed run 3 times with 60s backoff (each retry can re-spend OpenAI tokens), the job id is run+attempt, and there is no per-org/day rate limit or cost cap visible in the worker. Transcription uses a new OpenAI client per call with no timeout/backoff beyond BullMQ attempts (4, 60s).
confirmed.breaks_at: Many tutors building courses in the same week: queue wait grows linearly with runs; a failing prompt triple-bills tokens.
confirmed.fix: Add a group-concurrency limit per org (BullMQ Pro) or emulate with a Redis per-org semaphore and requeue-with-delay; raise concurrency to 2-3 once memory allows; set attempts to 1-2 for LLM runs (runner is stateful/resumable via run state, so use explicit user retry) and add an org-level daily run/credit cap check at enqueue.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor/admin AI course builder only; the runner is resumable via ai_agent_run state, so lowering attempts must keep the UI 'retry' action working; do not break credit accounting.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: AGENT_COURSE_GENERATION_WORKER_CONCURRENCY defaults to 1, the queue defaults give attempts 3 with a 60s backoff, and the job id is run+attempt. Speculative at today's usage (2 courses); a single lane is a safe memory choice on the shared 4 GB box. Per-org fairness and cost caps are product work rather than a scalability defect now.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do not raise concurrency before the jobs container has memory limits. Reduce attempts only if the runner is resumable from ai_agent_run state; verify the UI retry action first. A per-org daily cap check at enqueue is the cheapest control.

confirmed.title: Download-all ZIP buffers every file in RAM, fetches sequentially, and blocks the event loop
confirmed.current: zipDocumentObjects loops over entries one at a time (for/await getFromS3), calls Body.transformToByteArray() for each file and zip.file()s it. All files are held in memory. Then zip.generateAsync({type:'nodebuffer', compression:'DEFLATE'}) builds a second full copy, and caseload.ts hands that Buffer to c.body(), a third copy. The route first runs getAssessmentSubmissions, which loads the full version history, feedback and feedbackFiles for the whole roster just to read the latest files. Unreadable objects are skipped silently (getFromS3 swallows errors), so the zip can be incomplete with no warning. DEFLATE is applied to PDF/DOCX, which are already compressed, so CPU is wasted. Compose sets no memory limit on any container. The browser call uses the shared classroomio client, whose 30s timeout is in constants.ts:7.
confirmed.breaks_at: Document limit is 50MB per file. 100 learners x 2 files x 5-10MB is already 1-2GB, times about 2-3 copies. That OOM-kills the api container, or the whole 4GB droplet since nothing is capped, taking dashboard, jobs and Redis with it. Even for small rosters, roughly 100 sequential S3 GETs at about 100-300ms each exceed the 30s client timeout. The tutor sees 'Could not download submissions' while the server keeps burning CPU and memory for an abandoned request. JSZip compression runs on the single Node thread and stalls every other API request during the build.
confirmed.fix: 1) Replace JSZip with a streaming zip (archiver, or fflate's Zip, or yazl). Use STORE (no compression) for .pdf/.docx/.doc. Pipe each S3 Body stream into the archive and return the archive as a streamed Response, so memory stays at a few MB regardless of size. 2) Fetch with bounded concurrency (about 4), or since archives append in order, prefetch the next object while writing the current one. 3) Add guard rails: max entries and max total bytes (sum file.size from the metadata before starting), returning a clear 413 or 'too many files, download by learner'. Append a MANIFEST.txt listing any files that failed to fetch instead of skipping silently. 4) Query only the latest submission's files for the roster: a slim query instead of getAssessmentSubmissions. 5) For large rosters, enqueue a BullMQ job that writes the zip to the documents bucket under a requester-scoped key. Return a job id, then a short-TTL presigned URL once ready. The dashboard polls the job instead of holding a 30s request. 6) Give the dashboard call a longer per-request timeout (the Request config already supports `timeout`) and add mem_limit to the compose services.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor/admin 'Download all submissions' only (requireStaff). Access scope must stay exactly allocated-intersect-enrolled for a tutor and all enrolled for an admin. Keep calling resolveRoster/visibleLearnerIdsForCourse, and do not widen the slim query beyond the roster ids. If moved to an async job, re-evaluate the actor's scope when the job runs, or capture the roster at enqueue time, and bind the result URL to the requesting user. Otherwise a de-allocated tutor could fetch a stale zip. Edge cases: duplicate learner names (existing '(2)' de-dupe must be kept), Zip-Slip sanitising (keep sanitize()), Content-Disposition filename, an empty roster (404 'no files'), a learner with 10 files, and a partial failure.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed in zip.ts: sequential for/await getFromS3, transformToByteArray per file, zip.generateAsync nodebuffer with DEFLATE, then c.body(buffer). docker-compose.deploy.yaml has no mem_limit on any service. Client timeout is real: apps/dashboard api/index.ts clears the timeout once response headers arrive, and the buffered route only sends headers after the whole zip is built, so the 30s limit covers the entire build (AbortError -> 'Could not download submissions', server keeps working). A 5xx also triggers one client retry (retries:1), re-running the heavy build. Rated high rather than critical: today is 7 submissions, and a tutor roster is capped by allocation. The OOM only bites for an admin zipping a very large roster. The Manager role is already refused by resolveRoster.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Streaming (archiver or fflate Zip, STORE for pdf/docx/doc, bounded prefetch of ~4) is enough on its own and also fixes the timeout, because headers are sent immediately. Skip the BullMQ/presigned-result design: it adds result storage and a stale-scope problem for little gain. Do the pre-checks (entries empty -> 404, max entries/total bytes -> 413) BEFORE sending headers. After headers are sent a mid-stream failure yields a truncated zip, so append a MANIFEST.txt of failed files rather than throwing. Keep resolveRoster-derived scope, the sanitize() Zip-Slip guard and the '(2)' folder de-dupe unchanged. Replace getAssessmentSubmissions with a slim latest-files query restricted to the roster ids from visibleLearnerIdsForCourse (empty roster -> 404, never 'no filter'). Add mem_limit plus a matching node --max-old-space-size, or the container limit will just OOM-kill node.

confirmed.title: Every HLS segment goes browser to Caddy to dashboard to api to Supabase S3 and runs the full session/actor/rate-limit chain, with no shared cache
confirmed.current: HLS playback URLs are /hls/{assetId}/... served by the api, proxied through the SvelteKit dashboard (hooks.server.ts:100). The api is never bypassed. The Cloudflare Worker described in the comments does not exist in this deploy. Each segment request runs logger, correlationId, secureHeaders, auth.api.getSession (DB read plus the session updated_at write), resolveActor (organizationmember plus profile), the Redis rate limiter (4 Redis commands, 100 req/min per user), then GetObject from Supabase and streams the bytes back. The route does not skip any of that when a valid HMAC cookie is present. Segments are 'private, max-age=31536000, immutable', so only the single browser caches them. The cookie TTL is 15 minutes (assets.ts:676) and it is minted once, at player start (onBeforeHlsLoad). After 15 minutes every segment falls through to the session path with a DB getAssetById per segment.
confirmed.breaks_at: A viewer consumes roughly 10-20 requests/min per rendition. N concurrent viewers means N x that many Node requests, each with 3+ DB roundtrips and 4 Redis commands, on 2 vCPU. This is the most plausible source of the 335k per-request org/session lookups and the 166k storage.objects lookups, which are one per S3 GET. It scales linearly with watch-hours, not logins. Bytes also traverse the droplet twice: Supabase egress, then DO egress. About 2GB per learner-hour at 1080p exhausts the droplet's transfer allowance and the Supabase egress quota at a few thousand learners. Bursts when seeking or buffering, plus normal API calls, can push a user past 100 req/min and return 429 on segments (playback stalls). Videos longer than 15 minutes silently shift to the heavy DB path.
confirmed.fix: Short-term, S: in app.ts, treat /hls/ as a public-cors-style path. If a valid cio_hls cookie for the asset is present (pure HMAC verify, no DB), skip getSession/resolveActor and skip the global rate limiter. Only fall back to the session path when the cookie is missing or invalid. Also: (a) re-mint the cookie before expiry (timer at about 10 min from the player, or raise TTL to 2-4h; it is HMAC-scoped to one asset); (b) raise the segment rate bucket or exempt valid-cookie requests; (c) drop `logger()` for /hls. Medium-term, M-L: take bytes off the droplet. Put Cloudflare (or any CDN) in front, caching /hls/{assetId}/* for the immutable files and validating the existing HMAC cookie in a small Worker. Alternatively rewrite the manifests to presigned Supabase URLs. Also move Cache-Control to 'public, immutable' only if the CDN enforces the token.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner, tutor, admin and manager playback, plus the public course page (issuePublicHlsCookie) and the authoring preview (hls-encoder.ts:1003). The cookie is SameSite=None; Secure and per-asset; a longer TTL means a copied cookie works longer, and the cookie is minted by orgMemberMiddleware for any org asset, not scoped to enrollment. Consider also binding the mint endpoint to course access. Skipping session resolution for /hls/ must not drop CORS handling. The route already does its own CORS and 403. The master.m3u8 is mutable (p1080 patch) so keep its short max-age. Edge cases: expired or absent cookie must still allow a logged-in member via the session path, HEAD requests, Range requests (currently ignored by GetObject), and p1080 rendition upgrades.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. app.ts runs logger, correlationId, secureHeaders, then auth.api.getSession + resolveActor for every non-public path (PUBLIC_CORS_PATH_PREFIXES is only /public-api/, /widgets/, /health), then the global Redis rateLimiter (100/min keyed user:id or ip:). /hls/* is not exempt. hls.ts verifies the HMAC cookie only inside the handler, after all that work. Dashboard hooks forward /proxy/* before any session work, so bytes go Caddy -> dashboard -> api -> Supabase S3. The cookie TTL is 15 min (HLS_COOKIE_TTL_SECONDS) and the only mint is onBeforeHlsLoad. Nothing re-mints, so after 15 min each segment takes the session path plus getAssetById. Segments are Cache-Control private so no shared cache. Playback never breaks, because the session fallback works. The 429-on-seek risk is real, since segments share the 100/min per-user bucket with all other API calls. One attribution in the auditor's text is wrong: the 335k organization/organization_plan lookups come from dashboard SSR/layout and the org middleware, not /hls. The HLS route does not run orgMemberMiddleware. HLS plausibly explains the session updated_at writes and the storage.objects lookups (one per S3 GET).
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Implement as an early middleware/prefix branch in app.ts: for /hls/:assetId/*, if the cio_hls_<assetId> cookie verifies (pure HMAC, no DB), set anonymous actor and skip getSession/resolveActor, and give a separate generous limiter keyed by assetId+ip instead of fully exempting it. Keep the sessionCors/own-CORS handling and the OPTIONS handler. The invalid/missing cookie path must still fall through to the full session path unchanged. Raise cookie TTL modestly (1-2h) and/or re-mint on a timer, but note a longer TTL is a bearer token that outlives de-enrolment or de-allocation. Do not exempt master.m3u8 caching (max-age=10). The CDN/Worker option is a separate larger project. The comment block in hls.ts describing the Cloudflare Worker is stale for this deploy.

confirmed.title: Tutor exercise-submissions overview fetches, enriches and presigns every learner's submissions, then filters to allocated learners
confirmed.current: listExerciseSubmissionsOverview calls listSubmissionsByExercise(courseId, exerciseId) with no learner filter for both ADMIN and TUTOR. That loads all submissions with answers and groupmember, then runs a Promise.all over every submission that calls enrichFileUploadAnswersArray. Each of those does its own Redis mGet plus an S3-sign pipeline, for FILE_UPLOAD and VIDEO_RECORDING answers. Only after that does it compute visibleLearnerIdsForCourse and filter in memory for a TUTOR.
confirmed.breaks_at: With thousands of learners, each opening of an exercise's submission list by any tutor does O(all learners) DB rows, O(all learners) Redis round-trips and signing CPU, to return a small subset. Many tutors repeating this concurrently saturates the 2 vCPU droplet and the Redis connection. First hits after the 50-min cache expiry sign everything again. The response for an admin is also unbounded (no pagination), so payloads grow without bound. Unbounded Promise.all fan-out also exhausts the Redis and DB pool.
confirmed.fix: Compute the visible learner set first (visibleLearnerIdsForCourse for a TUTOR), then pass the profile/groupmember ids into getSubmissionsByCourseIdWithDetails (add an optional inArray filter on groupmember.profileId) so unauthorised rows are never loaded or signed. Do enrichment only on the returned page. Batch all keys for the whole result into one generateDocumentDownloadPresignedUrls plus one generateVideoDownloadPresignedUrls call (one mGet, one pipeline) instead of one per submission. Add pagination (limit/offset or cursor) for the admin and tutor views, plus bounded concurrency.
confirmed.flow_risk: Direct access-control surface (docs/ACCESS.md section 8, ad92abcf5). The tutor view must remain strictly allocated-learner-only. Pushing the filter into SQL narrows it further and must not widen it: an empty allocated set must return an empty list, not 'all' (do not treat an empty IN list as no filter). The learner's own `mySubmission` path (submittedBy = own groupMemberId) must be untouched. Edge cases: a submission whose groupmember.profileId is null, a learner in the course but with no allocation, a tutor who is also course-team, and ordering (createdAt asc) must be preserved after paging.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. listExerciseSubmissionsOverview calls listSubmissionsByExercise(courseId, exerciseId) with no learner filter for ADMIN and TUTOR, then visibleLearnerIdsForCourse and an in-memory filter for TUTOR. getSubmissionsByCourseIdWithDetails also loads all question_answer rows and does questionAnswers.filter per submission (O(n*m)). enrichFileUploadAnswersArray runs per submission, but it returns early when there are no FILE_UPLOAD/VIDEO_RECORDING answers, so Redis/sign cost only applies to exercises with those question types. Cost is bounded per exercise, not per course. It is a real linear-in-cohort waste but not an outage risk, and no data is returned to unauthorised tutors (filtered before the response), so there is no access-control leak, only wasted work. Medium, not high.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Resolve the visible learner set first. For TUTOR with an empty visible set, return [] immediately (never an empty inArray, which is invalid in drizzle or may be treated as no filter). Push inArray on groupmember.profileId into the SQL (profileIds; rows with null profileId stay excluded as today). Replace the per-submission filter with a Map grouped by submissionId. Do one batched enrich over the whole result instead of per submission. Pagination is optional and would change the dashboard contract, so defer it. Leave mySubmission (submittedBy = own groupmember id) untouched.

confirmed.title: Dashboard proxy buffers entire request bodies (limit raised to 25MB) for every /proxy/* and /api/auth/* call before any auth or rate limit
confirmed.current: proxyRequestToApi does init.body = await request.arrayBuffer() for every non-GET and forwards it with fetch (no signal, no timeout, no client-disconnect propagation). BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=26214400 (25MB) is global to the SvelteKit server, but the largest legitimate proxied body is a 5MB image (UPLOAD_MAX_IMAGE_MB) plus multipart overhead. Unauthenticated callers are also forwarded (shouldForwardToApi is path-only), so the api's auth and Redis limiter run only after the dashboard has buffered the entire body. On the api side /media/image does c.req.parseBody() (whole multipart in memory), then file.arrayBuffer(), then Buffer.from(), and only then checks file.size > MAX_IMAGE_SIZE. It is guarded by authMiddleware only: any logged-in learner, with no upload rate limit, can write to the public media bucket with a 1-year cache header.
confirmed.breaks_at: 20 parallel 25MB POSTs from one anonymous client pin about 500MB+ in the dashboard process, then again in the api (parseBody + arrayBuffer + Buffer = about 3 copies each) for authenticated ones. On a 4GB droplet with 3 Node services plus Redis and no memory limits, a small number of concurrent large uploads, or a stalled upstream (no fetch timeout), OOMs a container. As learner counts grow, accidental concurrent avatar and cover uploads become routine. Hung upstream requests also accumulate, since fetch has no AbortSignal.
confirmed.fix: 1) Lower DASHBOARD_BODY_SIZE_LIMIT to about 8-10MB (5MB image + multipart/b64-envelope overhead) and document it. 2) Stream the proxy body (body: request.body, duplex: 'half') instead of arrayBuffer(), and pass signal: request.signal plus an overall timeout (about 60-120s) to fetch so client aborts and stalls release resources. 3) In the api, add hono/body-limit: about 1MB default JSON and about 6-8MB for /media/image and the agent upload, so oversized bodies are rejected on Content-Length before parsing. 4) Put createRateLimiter (like uploadRateLimit) on /media/image, and consider restricting it to staff or to specific purposes (avatar, logo), or move image upload to presigned PUT into the public media bucket like documents. 5) Keep the file.size check but also check Content-Length first.
confirmed.flow_risk: Org logo, cover, avatar, certificate and thumbnail image uploads (HLS encoder uploads several thumbnail candidates through /media/image), agent document upload (5MB), and the b64-envelope bodies (base64 inflates by 1.33x, and AI-generated course HTML can be large). Choosing too low a global limit would break large course-content saves; measure the largest legitimate JSON body first. Streaming the body requires Node 18+ undici duplex and care that adapter-node's own limit is still enforced. Learner avatar upload must remain allowed under any rate limit. Edge cases: 413 error shape expected by the upload widgets, retries on 5xx (the client retries POSTs, so streaming bodies cannot be replayed; this is another reason to keep uploads one-shot).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: proxyRequestToApi does await request.arrayBuffer() for every non-GET and fetches with no signal or timeout. BODY_SIZE_LIMIT defaults to 26214400 in compose. shouldForwardToApi is path-only, so unauthenticated bodies are buffered before the api's auth. No bodyLimit exists anywhere in apps/api (grep empty). media.ts does parseBody then arrayBuffer then Buffer.from, and the size check runs only after parsing, but it is behind authMiddleware plus the global 100/min limiter, so the api-side multi-copy cost needs an authenticated user. Caddy is the only exposed service, so there is no direct api exposure. This is mostly a DoS/robustness issue rather than normal-growth scaling, so medium. The missing upstream timeout is the more realistic scale risk (hung api requests pile up in the dashboard).
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do the low-risk parts first: AbortSignal.timeout (about 60-120s) on the proxy fetch, hono bodyLimit on /media/image and the agent upload (about 6-8MB), and a content-length precheck. Lowering DASHBOARD_BODY_SIZE_LIMIT requires measuring the largest legitimate b64-envelope JSON (course HTML/AI content) first, because 8-10MB could break large course saves; do not change it blind. Streaming the proxy body is optional and riskier (undici duplex:'half', and the SvelteKit adapter limit wraps the stream), so treat it as phase 2. Existing global rate limiting already covers /media/image per user. Add a dedicated limiter, but keep avatar upload open to learners. Do not restrict to staff.

confirmed.title: Coursework download guard resolves each key with an unindexed jsonb containment scan, sequentially, plus a separate allocation query per key
confirmed.current: getSubmissionByFileKey does `files @> '[{"key":...}]'::jsonb` on coursework_submission and getSubmissionByFeedbackFileKey does `feedback_files @> ...` on coursework_result joined to submission. Neither column has a GIN index (only btree on learner+lesson, course, and submission_id exist). assertCourseworkDownloadAccess loops over up to 20 keys with await in sequence. For each key it runs the submission scan, falls through to the feedback scan on a miss, then canReadCoursework, which for a TUTOR does an isTutorAllocatedToLearner DB lookup. Learner feedback-file downloads always miss the first scan, so every feedback open is two full scans.
confirmed.breaks_at: Every file open by a tutor, admin or learner is a sequential scan of the entire coursework_submission table, and of coursework_result for feedback. Cost is linear in total submissions. With thousands of learners x multiple units x multiple versions this is hundreds of thousands of rows of jsonb being detoasted and compared per click. Concurrent tutors marking in a deadline rush multiply this. Added latency also blocks the Supabase pooler connections.
confirmed.fix: Preferred, no migration: the key already encodes the owner (coursework/{courseId}/{learnerId}/{lessonId}/{slug}/{version}/... and coursework-feedback/...). Parse the prefix, route to the right table by prefix (which removes the double lookup), and query by (learner_id, lesson_id) using the existing idx_coursework_submission_learner_lesson. Then confirm the key appears in files/feedback_files in SQL or JS. Fall back to the containment query only for keys that don't match the pattern. Also add GIN indexes (jsonb_path_ops) on coursework_submission.files and coursework_result.feedback_files via CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY as a drizzle migration. Run the key checks with Promise.all and cache the per-request isAllocatedTutor result per learnerId.
confirmed.flow_risk: This guard is the only door to coursework bytes and enforces 'tutors see only allocated learners' (ACCESS.md section 8). The authorisation outcome must be identical: still resolve the real submission and still call canReadCoursework on the owning learner. Do not trust the parsed learnerId from the key by itself (a forged key must not grant anything; always verify the key exists in the row's files). Keep the 403-not-404 behaviour. A GIN index adds a little write cost on submit/mark (drizzle migration, and the 74 unused-index advisory should not be made worse with unneeded ones). Edge cases: legacy keys from before the prefix scheme, keys with `coursework-feedback/` vs `coursework/`, version rows deleted after resubmission, and the 20-key cap.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. getSubmissionByFileKey uses files @> ... and getSubmissionByFeedbackFileKey uses feedback_files @> ... with no GIN index (the schema only has btree idx on learner+lesson, course and submission_id). assertCourseworkDownloadAccess loops keys sequentially, falling to the feedback scan on a miss, then canReadCoursework, which does an isTutorAllocatedToLearner lookup per key for a tutor. 'Hundreds of thousands of rows per click' is overstated: the table is one row per submission version (7 today). Even at tens of thousands of rows a seq scan costs tens of ms. It is a real linear cost on the only door to coursework bytes, but medium, not high.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Both options are safe if the authorisation outcome is unchanged. (a) Add GIN jsonb_path_ops indexes on coursework_submission.files and coursework_result.feedback_files in a normal drizzle migration (plain CREATE INDEX is fine at this table size; CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transactional migration). This is the simplest, with no logic change. (b) Prefix routing: parse coursework/ vs coursework-feedback/ and learnerId only as a lookup hint, then still require the key to appear in the row's files/feedback_files and still call canReadCoursework on the owning row's learnerId, never the parsed one. Keep the legacy containment fallback and the 403-not-404 behaviour. Also dedupe isAllocatedTutor per learnerId within a request. Run keys in parallel only if the 20-key cap stays.

confirmed.title: Server-side S3 clients have no connect/request timeouts and use the default 50-socket pool
confirmed.current: getS3Client() creates S3Client with no requestHandler configuration, so there is no connectionTimeout or requestTimeout, and the default Node agent allows maxSockets 50. The project already hit this class of bug: a no-timeout Supabase Storage PUT hung uploads. The HLS route, getFromS3 (zip), deleteFromS3, uploadToS3 and the jobs worker all share this behaviour.
confirmed.breaks_at: A stalled Supabase Storage response holds the HLS handler and its dashboard-proxy connection open forever, with no client abort propagation. A burst of segment requests beyond about 50 in flight queues behind the socket cap, so segment latency spikes and hls.js shows stalls. During any Supabase storage incident the api accumulates hung requests until it is restarted.
confirmed.fix: Construct the clients with NodeHttpHandler({connectionTimeout: 5000, requestTimeout: 30000, httpsAgent: new https.Agent({keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 200})}) and set maxAttempts to 3. For the streaming HLS GET, use an AbortSignal tied to the incoming request (c.req.raw.signal) so a client disconnect destroys the upstream stream. Apply the same handler to apps/jobs/src/config/storage.ts.
confirmed.flow_risk: All server-side storage reads, writes and deletes (HLS playback, media image upload, zip build, og-cache, transcript, HLS abort/cleanup). Too-low requestTimeout would break large legitimate GetObject streams (a requestTimeout in the AWS Node handler is a socket idle timeout, so streaming is safe if data flows, but verify). Presign clients only sign locally and are unaffected. Edge cases: the 800MB direct browser uploads do not go through these clients; jobs downloading large videos need a longer or idle-based timeout.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: getS3Client() in packages/core/src/config/storage.ts passes no requestHandler, so the SDK v3 default NodeHttpHandler applies (no connect/request timeout, 50 sockets per agent). This matches the prior no-timeout PUT hang noted in project memory. The HLS route, getFromS3 (zip), uploadToS3 and deleteFromS3 all use it. apps/jobs has its own client with the same gap.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Use NodeHttpHandler with connectionTimeout about 5s and requestTimeout as a socket-idle timeout (about 30-60s; it is idle-based in v3, so streaming is safe while data flows). Use keepAlive and maxSockets about 200. Give the jobs client a longer idle timeout for big video downloads. Presign clients are unaffected. Treat the HLS abort-on-disconnect wiring as optional. Rollout is low risk but needs a test of a long streamed GET.

confirmed.title: Presign cache hands out URLs with as little as 10 minutes of life, but the player assumes a fresh hour
confirmed.current: URLs are signed with expiresIn=3600 but cached in Redis with TTL 3000s. A cache hit can therefore return a URL with only 600s of validity left. The lesson player schedules its refresh at 50 minutes after receiving the URL (PLAYBACK_URL_REFRESH_MS), and refreshes only if the video has not been played yet (refreshPlaybackUrlIfIdle returns null once hasPlayed). Every lesson GET (enrichLessonWithPresignedUrls) returns the cached URLs.
confirmed.breaks_at: This gets worse as traffic grows, because the hit rate rises and the average remaining life of a returned URL falls toward 10 minutes. A learner who opens a lesson late in the cache window and watches a progressive MP4 longer than the URL's remaining life gets 403 on the next range request after expiry, and playback fails. Learners parked on a tab and returning later hit the same expired links in document openers.
confirmed.fix: Make the cache TTL at most half the signing expiry (for example sign 3600s, cache 1500-1800s) so every served URL has at least 30 min left, and/or return an expiresAt with the URLs so the client schedules refreshes from the true expiry. Let the player refresh while playing at a keyframe-safe moment or on error (handlePlaybackReload already exists) rather than only before first play.
confirmed.flow_risk: All download-URL consumers: lesson video and document views, tutor material open, submission file links, video-recording playback. A shorter cache TTL slightly increases signing CPU (negligible, local HMAC) and Redis writes. The refresh timer constant must be reduced to match, or learners could still hold a URL past expiry. Edge cases: long videos, browser tab sleeping, multiple devices.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: signs with presignDownloadExpiresSeconds=3600 but caches for PRESIGN_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=3000, so a cache hit can return a URL with 600s left. The player's refresh timer is 50 min from receipt and only refreshes pre-play. Impact is limited to long progressive MP4 playback or parked tabs. HLS videos use the cookie path, not presigned URLs, and handlePlaybackReload exists as a recovery. Low, not medium.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Lower the cache TTL to about 1500-1800s (or raise expiresIn to 2h while keeping the cache TTL) so every served URL has at least 30 min left. This is a one-constant change with no flow risk. Adjust the player's PLAYBACK_URL_REFRESH_MS to match.

confirmed.title: Material presign endpoints accept unbounded key lists, run about 8-10 queries per click, and re-scan lessons twice
confirmed.current: ZCourseDownloadPresignedUrl.keys has min(1) but no max count and no per-key length cap, and courseId is min(1) rather than uuid. For a learner, assertCourseMaterialDownloadAccess runs canReadCourseContent (membership plus course lookups), getCourseMaterialKeys (full scan of the course's lessons' documents/videos jsonb), getMaterialKeyLessonMap (the same scan again), then for each key serially an isUnitUnlocked call. Each isUnitUnlocked does getCourseSequentialUnlock, getOrderedUnitsForCourse and hasLearnerPassedUnit. generateDownloadPresignedUrls then does mGet on all keys and an unbounded Promise.all of getSignedUrl.
confirmed.breaks_at: A single request with tens of thousands of keys (a staff caller bypasses the currency check, see the next finding) does a huge mGet and synchronous HMAC signing in one tick, blocking the event loop for seconds. For learners, every 'Download brief' / open-material click costs about 8-10 DB queries on the same hot tables, repeated per concurrent learner. With thousands of learners this is a large share of the lesson-time query volume.
confirmed.fix: Add .max(50) (or 100) on keys, .max(1024) per key, and z.uuid() on courseId. Replace the two lesson scans with a single getMaterialKeyLessonMap call (its keys are the current-materials set). Compute isUnitUnlocked once per distinct lessonId (Set of lesson ids), in parallel, using one getOrderedUnitsForCourse/getCourseSequentialUnlock fetch per request. Dedupe keys before signing. Cap signing concurrency (p-limit about 20) and chunk Redis mGet.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learners opening materials and briefs (they must still be refused for locked units, removed or cross-course keys and unpublished courses, with the same 403 messages), staff authoring flow (add-document-modal signs a just-uploaded key; staff bypass of the currency check must remain), media-manager preview. The learner-facing response must remain identical for valid keys. Edge cases: duplicate keys in a request, a key present in two lessons (map keeps the last lesson; the current behaviour is unchanged, but decide deliberately), course with sequential unlock toggled off.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: ZCourseDownloadPresignedUrl.keys is min(1) with no max, and courseId is min(1). getCourseMaterialKeys and getMaterialKeyLessonMap each scan the course's lessons (a double scan). The per-key isUnitUnlocked loop is real, but it returns early when sequential unlock is off. The unbounded-signing DoS needs a staff caller, since a learner is bounded to the course's current material keys. Bounded by course size, so low.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add keys.max(100) (not 50; check the lesson-level callers in presign.svelte.ts first), per-key max length, and courseId uuid. Fetch getMaterialKeyLessonMap once and derive the key set from it. Dedupe lessonIds before the isUnitUnlocked checks. Keep identical 403 messages.

confirmed.title: Presigned uploads cannot enforce size, are open to any authenticated role, and nothing ever reclaims orphaned objects
confirmed.current: Size is checked only against the client-supplied fileSize (the code comments admit it is advisory), and the presigned PutObject does not sign content-length. /video/upload (800MB limit) only needs requireActor(), so any learner or manager gets 100 URLs/hour (staff 500), unbound to any course. /document/upload without courseId (50MB) is likewise open. initVideoRecordingUpload accepts any positive size (no maximum), creates a 'pending' asset row each time, has no rate limit, and completion never verifies the object exists or its real size. Nothing reaps objects that were uploaded but never registered (a coursework PUT without the follow-up POST, abandoned HLS or recordings, pending asset rows). The maintenance worker's retentionCompact is a logged no-op.
confirmed.breaks_at: Storage cost and Supabase quota grow with abandoned or hostile uploads rather than with real usage. At thousands of learners, 100 x 50-800MB per learner per hour is unbounded. Pending asset rows accumulate. The only real ceiling is the Supabase bucket file_size_limit, which the docs note must be set manually.
confirmed.fix: 1) Sign content-length: pass ContentLength: fileSize into PutObjectCommand and sign it with signableHeaders: new Set(['content-length']) (and make fileSize required on all upload presigns), so the URL only accepts an upload of exactly that size. 2) Restrict /video/upload to staff roles (ADMIN/TUTOR) if learners never need it, and cap video-recording size by the question's max duration and bitrate. 3) Add uploadRateLimit to video-recording init and to coursework presign, and set the bucket file_size_limit and allowed_mime_types in Supabase. 4) Add a maintenance job: list objects under coursework/, exercise-recordings/ and un-referenced flat keys older than 48h that have no referencing submission/asset, and delete them and any stale 'pending' asset rows. 5) HEAD the object on completion to verify existence and size.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner coursework and feedback uploads, exercise FILE_UPLOAD answers (flat keys via /document/upload without courseId, so any change here must keep this learner path working), staff material authoring and the browser HLS encoder. Content-length signing requires the browser PUT to send exactly that size; axios sets it automatically, but a mismatched or missing fileSize would turn into a 403 from storage. The orphan sweeper must not delete keys of in-flight uploads (use an age threshold) and must check references in coursework_submission.files, coursework_result.feedback_files, lesson.documents/videos, asset.storage_key and question_answer.answer_data. Edge cases: resubmission versions, draft submissions, restored backups.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly overstated. Size is advisory only (confirmed: assertPresignFileSizeWithinLimit comment and the presign PutObject without content-length). However /video/upload does have uploadRateLimit (100/h learner, 500/h staff), and video-recording init requires course membership (groupmember lookup) plus the global limiter. Pending asset rows and orphaned objects are real (retentionCompact is a logged no-op), but this is a slow cost drift, not a scale break.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Prefer setting Supabase bucket file_size_limit and allowed_mime_types as the primary control. Signing ContentLength into the presigned PUT is risky on Supabase S3 compatibility and must be tested before relying on it. Verify the learner exercise FILE_UPLOAD flow (flat key via /document/upload without courseId) and the browser HLS encoder still work; check who actually calls /video/upload before restricting to staff. A cap on video-recording size by duration*bitrate is reasonable. The orphan sweeper is destructive: ship as report-only first, use an age threshold of at least 48h, and check every referencing table (coursework_submission.files, coursework_result.feedback_files, lesson.documents/videos, asset.storage_key, question_answer.answer_data).

confirmed.title: Tutor course-view and material endpoints load the whole enrolled roster just to run an access check
confirmed.current: resolveRoster calls visibleLearnerIdsForCourse. For an ADMIN that is listEnrolledLearnersWithName(courseId), the entire enrolled roster with names. getTutorUnitContent and signCourseMaterialsForTutor call resolveRoster only as an access gate and discard the ids, then also fetch the whole course outline (getCourseOutline) or the unit.
confirmed.breaks_at: With thousands of learners in a course, every admin click on a unit or material runs a roster query returning thousands of rows, and this is repeated for each document sign. For tutors the call is bounded by their allocation, but each also does extra queries (isCourseTutor on empty roster).
confirmed.fix: Split the gate from the roster. Add a canAccessCourse(actor, courseId) that returns immediately for ADMIN, for a TUTOR uses a cheap EXISTS on allocation-intersect-enrolled OR isCourseTutor, and throws 403 for others. Use it in getTutorUnitContent and signCourseMaterialsForTutor, and keep resolveRoster only where the ids are actually used (grid, outline stats, zip). For signCourseMaterialsForTutor, fetch the key set with the single-scan getMaterialKeyLessonMap instead of the full outline.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor read-only course content and the materials download. Access must stay unchanged: ADMIN all, TUTOR only if on the course team or with an allocated learner enrolled, Manager and Learner refused (403/401). Do not let the new gate return true for a TUTOR with neither condition. A course-team tutor with no allocations must still get content with an empty roster elsewhere. Edge case: a tutor allocated to learners who are not enrolled in this course.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: getTutorUnitContent and signCourseMaterialsForTutor call resolveRoster only as a gate. For ADMIN that is listEnrolledLearnersWithName (the full roster). The admin population is small, and the call is per click, so the impact is modest.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: A canAccessCourse(actor, courseId) must reproduce resolveRoster exactly: ADMIN true; TUTOR true iff (allocated learner enrolled in this course) OR isCourseTutor; everyone else 403/401. Do not give any TUTOR access based on org alone. Mirror the existing semantics rather than inventing a new one.

confirmed.title: Staff bypass of the material-currency check lets any tutor or manager sign non-coursework/ keys such as feedback, recordings and other learners' exercise files
confirmed.current: After canReadCourseContent, any content staff (ADMIN/TUTOR/MANAGER) returns immediately (ownership.ts:289) with only a block on keys starting with 'coursework/'. coursework-feedback/..., exercise-recordings/... and flat nanoid keys of learners' exercise FILE_UPLOAD answers are not blocked and are signed on request, for either bucket. Together with the unbounded keys list, a tutor can mint URLs for non-allocated learners' data given a key.
confirmed.breaks_at: Not a perf problem, but it undermines the allocated-learners-only guarantee as the number of tutors grows (more people hold keys, e.g. via exported data or notification emails). Keys include learnerId and are guessable only by someone with a source, but the trust boundary widens with the number of tutors.
confirmed.fix: For non-admin staff, apply the same default-deny as learners: require every key to be in the course's current material set (getMaterialKeyLessonMap), or in the narrow authoring-upload case a key under materials/{courseId}/. Block coursework-feedback/ and exercise-recordings/ prefixes explicitly in the materials door, as already done for coursework/. For the authoring flow, restrict the bypass to ADMIN and check the key starts with materials/{courseId}/ or is a flat key only the uploader just created.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin authoring (sign a just-uploaded document key), tutor material view, media manager previews (no courseId, staff-only org assets path: keys there are asset storage keys, so validate against the asset table for the actor's org). Tightening could break org-level asset downloads if keys are not checked against assets. Edge: Manager role reading materials, and HLS thumbnails.
confirmed.verifier_note: The gap is real: ownership.ts blocks only keys starting with 'coursework/', and 'coursework-feedback/' does not match that prefix (it diverges at the 11th char), so a Manager or non-allocated tutor passes the staff bypass for coursework-feedback/ and exercise-recordings/ keys. It is mitigated: every key contains a nanoid (generateFileKey) and the signer does not check existence, so exploitation needs a leaked key. Defence-in-depth gap, not an exploitable-by-guessing hole. Low.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The minimal safe fix is to extend the deny check to coursework-feedback/ and exercise-recordings/ (route them to their own guarded doors). Do NOT apply the auditor's default-deny-by-currency for staff: it would break the authoring just-uploaded-key flow, media-manager previews and flat exercise-file keys. If anything, restrict only non-ADMIN staff and only for these prefixes.

confirmed.title: ffmpeg/transcription workers share the 2 vCPU droplet with the API, with no container limits and one shared Redis without maxmemory
confirmed.current: The jobs container runs ffmpeg audio extraction and thumbnail work (MEDIA_WORKER_CONCURRENCY default 2) on the same host as api and dashboard. HLS extract-audio downloads every segment of a video one at a time via downloadObjectToTempFile (hundreds of sequential S3 GETs per lecture, each a storage.objects lookup). Compose has no mem_limit/cpus on any service. Redis (appendonly yes, no maxmemory or eviction policy) holds BullMQ, the rate-limiter zsets and the presign cache together. uploadFileToBucket reads the whole file into memory.
confirmed.breaks_at: As tutors upload more lectures, ffmpeg bursts consume both CPUs and starve the API and dashboard, which degrades playback and grading exactly when load is highest. One misbehaving container can OOM the whole 4GB droplet. A Redis growth spike (many presign keys or rate-limit members) has no cap and can evict nothing.
confirmed.fix: Set mem_limit/cpus per service (for example api 1.2G, dashboard 0.8G, jobs 1G with cpus 0.75 and nice on ffmpeg), set redis --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy volatile-lru (BullMQ keys have no TTL; use a separate Redis db or instance for the cache and rate-limiter, or allkeys-lru only on that one). Download HLS segments with bounded concurrency (about 6), and for transcription fetch only the audio rendition. Consider running jobs on a separate droplet once video volume grows.
confirmed.flow_risk: Media post-processing (transcripts, thumbnails), playback during uploads. Memory limits that are too low will OOM-kill ffmpeg mid-job, so the reaper must requeue those jobs (reapStuckMediaJobs exists). Redis eviction must never evict BullMQ queue keys, so use a volatile policy or separate instances and test a deploy rehearsal. Edge: images are built on the droplet (20-45 min), so changes to limits also need an off-peak rollout.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: compose has no mem_limit/cpus on any service, redis runs 'redis-server --appendonly yes' with no maxmemory, and apps/jobs extract-audio downloads each HLS segment sequentially. The one-droplet blast radius is real for the planned growth, but ffmpeg usage is limited (audio extraction and thumbnails, with the HLS encode in the browser), so low-medium.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The proposed 'redis --maxmemory-policy volatile-lru' is WRONG for BullMQ, which requires maxmemory-policy noeviction (it warns otherwise). Correct approach: keep BullMQ on a noeviction Redis with a generous maxmemory, and run the presign cache and rate-limiter on a second Redis instance (allkeys-lru) or a separate db with its own instance, since the policy is instance-wide. Add mem_limit together with node --max-old-space-size, and test limits off-peak given on-droplet builds.

confirmed.title: Every page load AND every client navigation (__data.json) re-validates the session at the API and re-fetches the single org (source of the 335k org/session queries)
confirmed.current: hooks.server.ts handle() calls getSessionData -> authServerClient.getSession (HTTP to the API, which runs the Better Auth customSession org-role lookups) for every non-proxy request, including every SvelteKit __data.json navigation. The root +layout.server.ts also re-runs on every navigation because getBaseMetaTags reads url.pathname for the canonical URL (metaTags.server.ts:141). Each run calls getOrgSiteInfo, which under PUBLIC_IS_SELFHOSTED=true (the prod compose setting) always calls getFirstOrg, i.e. classroomio.organization.first.$get, i.e. 'select id from organization order by created_at limit 1' + the org row + organization_plan. Nothing is cached in the dashboard process. Page-level SSR loads then call the API again with the user cookie (getApiHeaders), which re-validates the session a second time.
confirmed.breaks_at: Request count is linear in navigations x users, with no cache. At ~2,000 active learners doing ~20 navigations per session, that is tens of thousands of identical org/plan/session queries per hour from the dashboard alone, through the Supabase pooler on a 2 vCPU droplet. Latency of every click includes 1 session RTT + 1 org RTT before the page-specific load can start.
confirmed.fix: (1) In layout-setup.ts add a module-level TTL cache (60-300s, keyed by mode/siteName/host) around getFirstOrg / getOrgBySiteName / getOrgsByCustomDomain, with in-flight promise de-dupe; invalidate on a short TTL only (org settings change rarely). (2) Make metaTags canonical use data computed client-independent or move canonical to a +layout.ts / <svelte:head> from page.url so the server layout stops depending on url.pathname; then the root server load is cached by SvelteKit and does not rerun on client navigations. (3) In hooks.server.ts skip getSessionData for requests that do not need it (static-ish public routes, /api/auth is already proxied) and add a short per-session-cookie cache (5-15s, in-memory Map keyed by hash of the cookie string, max N entries) so __data.json bursts and parallel loads reuse one session lookup. (4) Pass the already-resolved session through to downstream API calls via a server-to-server trusted header or reuse locals.actor in SSR loaders instead of re-validating.
confirmed.flow_risk: All roles. Staleness window: a suspended/deactivated user or role change must still take effect fast, so keep the session cache TTL very short (<=15s) and never cache the actor beyond the API's own authoritative resolveActor check, which stays the enforcement boundary (tutor-allocation rule untouched because the API still decides per request). Org cache must be cleared when super admin edits org settings (or accept <=60s staleness). Logout must delete the cache entry for that cookie. Custom-domain lookups must key on hostname so tenants never cross.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed in code. hooks.server.ts handle() calls getSessionData before the isPublicRoute check, so every non-/proxy and non-/api/auth request (including __data.json) makes an HTTP getSession round trip. root +layout.server.ts calls getOrgSiteInfo, which in self-hosted mode always calls getFirstOrg with no cache. getBaseMetaTags reads url.pathname for canonical and og:url, which makes the root server load re-run on each pathname change. Two nuances. First, the API getSession is partly softened by Better Auth cookieCache (1h) in packages/db/src/auth.ts, though the SSR fetch discards Set-Cookie so the cache only refreshes via browser /api/auth calls. Second, the 335k org/plan figure is attributable only in part to this path (see missed item about the OG warm fetch). Critical is overstated at today's volume; high is right.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Fix parts (1), (2) and a very short (<=10-15s) session cache are safe. Drop part (4): do not reuse locals.actor in SSR loaders or add a trusted header to skip API re-validation. locals.status comes from customSession and is not authoritative, the API resolveActor is the enforcement boundary, and a spoofable header would weaken the tutor-allocation rule. A session cache must be keyed on the full cookie value (hash it), be deleted on logout, and never cache null or failed results. Org cache TTL 30-60s keyed by mode plus siteName or hostname. Do not cache an API failure. Also add an AbortSignal timeout to the SSR getSession call (see missed).

confirmed.title: Four independent 45-60s pollers run in every open tab, including hidden/backgrounded tabs
confirmed.current: (app)/+layout.svelte posts /account/heartbeat every 60s for every signed-in user on every page (this is the session updated_at write, ~33k in pg_stat). notification-bell.svelte GETs /notifications every 60s (plus again every time the popover opens). header-context.svelte GETs the org summary every 45s on every admin page, and admin-dashboard.svelte separately GETs online-now every 45s on the dashboard page (duplicating the 'online' figure the summary already carries). None of them check document.visibilityState, none back off, none add jitter, and the intervals are never cleared when a tab is hidden. Each request additionally pays a session validation + resolveActor at the API.
confirmed.breaks_at: Steady background load = users x tabs x (2 requests/min learners/tutors, 3-4/min admins). 3,000 learners with one tab open (many left open all day) = ~6,000 req/min = 100 req/s of pure polling plus 50 DB writes/s on the session table, all synchronised to the same 60s cadence after a deploy/restart (thundering herd). This alone will saturate the single api container and the Supabase pooler (advisor already warns auth_db_connections_absolute).
confirmed.fix: Create one shared 'presence/poll' module: pause when document.hidden (visibilitychange), resume with an immediate refresh on focus, add +-20% jitter, lengthen to 120-300s for notifications/heartbeat (a heartbeat window of 5 min tolerates a 120s ping), and fold unread-count into the heartbeat response so the bell needs no separate poll (or use the cheaper unreadCount-only endpoint instead of the full list). Remove the admin-dashboard online poll in favour of the header summary's 'online' value (one source). Only call orgSummaryApi from the header when the section needs it, and share one in-flight request. Add exponential backoff on non-2xx/5xx.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learners/tutors: notification badge becomes up to 2 min stale unless refreshed on focus (do that). 'Online now' presence for admins is defined as sessions refreshed within 5 minutes (comment at +layout.svelte:31) so a 120s heartbeat is safe, but a hidden tab will drop out of 'online', which is arguably correct. Make sure a final heartbeat/refresh fires on visibilitychange->visible so users returning after a long idle are not shown as offline/stale. Do not suppress the heartbeat entirely for active tabs or the live-presence panel breaks.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. (app)/+layout.svelte heartbeat every 60s, notification-bell 60s, header-context 45s, admin-dashboard online 45s, with no visibilityState checks and no jitter. Each call is a full authMiddleware pass at the API. Request math is right (~2 req/min/open tab), but 3,000 simultaneous tabs is a worst case, and a post-deploy thundering herd is not really present because intervals start at mount time. Real, but high rather than critical. The heartbeat itself is a single-row UPDATE (touchSession), which is cheap.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Visibility pause plus refresh on focus is safe and correct. Two corrections. (a) There is NO unreadCount-only endpoint (grep finds unreadCount only in services); GET /notifications returns the full list, so a cheap count endpoint or folding unread into the heartbeat response needs an API change and is size M, not S. (b) Do NOT remove the admin-dashboard online poll in favour of the header summary: adminDashboardApi.loadOnline feeds OnlineUsersPanel, which lists users, while the summary carries only a count. Just gate that poll on visibility and share the interval. Also HeaderContext is mounted by AppHeader inside org/[slug]/+layout and calls an admin-only summary endpoint; for non-admin shells that call fails every 45s, so skip polling when the actor is not an admin. Keep the heartbeat at <=120s because the online window is 5 min, and send an immediate ping on visibilitychange to visible.

confirmed.title: Root server layout serialises the whole session/org payload into every navigation response
confirmed.current: load() returns `locals` (App.Locals: user, session row, profile, organizations[] with plan and member, orgRoles, actor) as page data. Because this server layout reruns on each navigation (see ssr-session-and-org-per-navigation) the full object is re-serialised into every __data.json and the initial HTML. The session object is the DB session row type (TSession), so a token-bearing row can be embedded in page data readable by any script on the page. The client already fetches /account and the Better Auth session separately (init.svelte.ts setupApp, authClient.useSession), so this is duplicated data.
confirmed.breaks_at: Payload grows with organizations/plan data and is re-sent on every click; also a standing XSS-amplifier (a script can read the session token from page data despite the httpOnly cookie).
confirmed.fix: Return only the fields the client actually reads from data.locals (routes/+layout.svelte:onMount uses data.locals.user id/email/name; +layout.ts uses locals.profile.locale; (app)/+layout.svelte passes data.locals through). Replace with `{ user: {id,email,name}, locale, role }` and drop session/organizations/token fields. Verify no component reads data.locals.session or organizations.
confirmed.flow_risk: All roles. Anything reading page.data.locals.* breaks silently (grep `locals` in svelte files and +layout.ts before shipping). Locale selection in +layout.ts:12 relies on locals.profile.locale; keep that field. Impersonation banner and verify-email modal read session via authClient not locals, but confirm.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed that load() returns locals (user, session row incl. token column, profile, organizations, orgRoles, actor) as page data and it is serialised into HTML and every re-run __data.json. TSession has a token column and Better Auth getSession returns it. This is mainly a hygiene and XSS-amplification issue and a payload cost, not a throughput issue. The suggestion that the client already fetches /account separately is true but the data is NOT purely redundant: appInitApi.setupApp(locals) stores this.session=locals and reads locals.orgRoles for tenant-membership checks, and +layout.ts reads locals.profile.locale.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Trim rather than replace. Keep user (id,email,name,image etc. whatever consumers read), profile.locale, orgRoles, status and actor; strip session.token/ipAddress/userAgent and the organizations[] plan payload if unused. grep every consumer first: init.svelte.ts (this.session, isMemberOfOrg using orgRoles, line ~287-295 currentSession), +page.svelte setupApp(data.locals), (app)/+layout.svelte props type, and routes/+layout.svelte:33 console.log('Layout', data), which also dumps the whole payload including the session row into every user's browser console. Remove that log.

confirmed.title: Root layout does an outbound CDN HEAD (up to 2s) and a fire-and-forget warm fetch on every navigation
confirmed.current: For org sites the layout fires `void fetch(warmUrl)` on every server load, and getBaseMetaTags -> resolveOgImageUrl -> resolveOrgSiteOgImageUrl does `await fetch(cdnUrl,{method:'HEAD', timeout 2000ms})` against the media CDN whenever PUBLIC_MEDIA_CDN_URL is set, blocking the layout load (and therefore every page's first byte) for up to 2s if the CDN is slow or the object is missing. Result is not cached.
confirmed.breaks_at: Each navigation can block on an external HEAD request; with a missing CDN object this adds a 2s stall to every page for every user and doubles outbound sockets on a 2-vCPU droplet.
confirmed.fix: Memoise the resolved OG URL and warm-fetch per siteName in a module-level Map with a 10-60 min TTL (negative results too). Better, skip OG resolution entirely for authenticated app routes: OG tags are only needed for public org-site/landing pages and bots, so compute them only when !locals.user or on routes under (org-site).
confirmed.flow_risk: Only link previews for public org pages. Make sure public share URLs (course landing pages, invites) still emit correct OG tags; keep the fallback to the proxied PNG route.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly real, but the finding misidentifies the damaging part. The HEAD request only runs when PUBLIC_MEDIA_CDN_URL is set (self-hosted default is empty) and docker-compose.deploy.yaml does not set it, so in prod there is NO 2s HEAD stall. The warm fetch IS real and runs on every root layout load for the org site (isOrgSite is true in self-hosted): void fetch(PRIVATE_SERVER_URL/org-site/og/<siteName>.png). That API route (apps/api/src/routes/org-site/og.ts -> services/org/og.ts generateOrgSiteOgImage) does getOrganizationBySiteName + getActiveOrganizationPlan (org row + organization_plan select) and then S3 HeadObject + GetObject on the media bucket (og-cache.ts getCachedOrgSiteOgBuffer), the latter being Supabase Storage storage.objects lookups. This very plausibly explains much of the 335k org/organization_plan counts and the ~166k storage.objects lookups. So the severity is higher than stated for the wrong reason.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Primary fix: module-level per-siteName TTL (10-60 min) guard so the warm fetch is issued at most once per interval per process (and skip it entirely when the persisted OG object is known to exist or when PUBLIC_OG_IMAGE_URL is set). Also add an in-process etag/buffer cache in the API generateOrgSiteOgImage so even external crawler hits do not repeat 2 DB + 2 S3 calls. Compute meta/OG only for unauthenticated or org-site landing routes. Keep the CDN HEAD memoisation as a secondary item, negative results cached too.

confirmed.title: Tutor dashboard loads the full nested roster plus five unbounded queue arrays on every visit, and fetches announcements twice
confirmed.current: caseload.svelte onMount fires loadCaseload() (every allocated learner x course x unit with state) AND loadPipeline() (stats + awaitingMarking, resubmissions, awaitingDraftFeedback, overdue, dueSoon arrays of PipelineItem + programmes) AND announcementsApi.loadFeed(); BroadcastBanner (rendered on the same page) calls loadFeed() again in its own onMount, so the feed is fetched twice. The nested roster from loadCaseload is only used for the 'Your Learners' drill-down table and as a fallback for a count that stats.learners already provides. Queue arrays are rendered whole in a plain <Table> with no cap or pagination. For an Admin viewing /caseload, 'Admin sees the org', so the roster is the entire org.
confirmed.breaks_at: A tutor with 150-300 learners x 2-4 courses x ~10 units = tens of thousands of nested objects per dashboard open; an admin viewing the same page gets thousands of learners. Payload in the MBs and a slow Svelte reactivity pass ($state deep proxy) on each open. Overdue/awaiting queues grow unbounded during a marking backlog.
confirmed.fix: Drop eager loadCaseload; call it lazily only when activeView === 'learners', and replace its use with a paginated 'GET /caseload/learners?page&limit&search' (flat rows: id, name, email, submissionCount). Cap each pipeline queue server-side to the first 25-50 with a total count, and add 'load more'/paging when a queue is opened (or a per-queue endpoint). Remove the duplicate loadFeed (let BroadcastBanner own it, or have the page read announcementsApi.items without re-loading). Render long tables with a Show more button or virtual list.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutors and admins. Must keep allocation scoping on the server for the new paged endpoints (tutor = allocated learners only, docs/ACCESS.md s8 / ad92abcf5): the pagination/search must be applied AFTER the allocation filter, and totals must be computed from the filtered set so no count leaks unallocated learners. KPI tiles must keep using stats (not the paged list). Edge cases: empty roster, tutor allocated mid-session, search with special chars.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: caseload.svelte onMount fires loadCaseload, loadPipeline and announcementsApi.loadFeed; BroadcastBanner calls loadFeed again in its own onMount, so the feed is fetched twice. The nested roster (caseloadApi.learners) is used only for the learners drill-down table (line ~295-313) and as a fallback count. Announcements service has no limit. Scale impact is real for admins viewing /caseload and for large caseloads, but a tutor sees only allocated learners so per-tutor volume is bounded (tens to low hundreds), so high is overstated.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Lazy-loading loadCaseload only when activeView==='learners' is safe and the easiest win. If adding a paged /caseload/learners endpoint, apply the allocation filter BEFORE search/offset/limit, compute totals from the allocation-filtered set, and keep admin = org-wide. Capping pipeline queues must keep stats counts computed on the full allocated set. Remove the duplicate loadFeed.

confirmed.title: Admin learners, allocations, registrations, and progression tables fetch the entire org and paginate (or do not paginate) client-side
confirmed.current: learners.$get returns every learner row with its embedded courses[] array and KPI counts; filtering, search and pagination (slice) are all client-side. After every create/suspend/reactivate (learner-management.svelte.ts:80,121) load() re-downloads the whole roster. allocation.list() returns every tutor-learner pair and the page renders every group as its own <Table> with no paging; loadAssignable() returns all tutors AND all learners into two <Select.Content> lists (allocation.svelte:150-175) with no search, i.e. thousands of DOM options. registrations.load() with status 'approved'/'rejected'/'' returns the full history forever and refetches after each decision. progression (tutor and admin variants) computes metrics for every learner server-side, ships them all, then paginates client-side, and refetches the whole set on every course-filter change.
confirmed.breaks_at: ~1,000-2,000 learners: multi-MB JSON per open/refresh, multi-second server aggregation per load (the progression and learners endpoints compute per-learner joins), janky filtering on each keystroke (no debounce, full re-filter of N rows), and a <Select> with thousands of items freezes the Assign dialog. Registrations history grows without bound.
confirmed.fix: Adopt the pattern already used correctly by users.svelte / usersApi.list (server-side page/limit/search, 300ms debounced) for: learners (add status/activity/course filters server-side; return KPIs from a separate cheap endpoint), allocations (paginate by tutor or learner, plus per-tutor lazy expand), registrations (page + status, default limit 25), and progression (page/limit/search/activity/band params). Replace the two assign dialogs' <Select> with a searchable async combobox (reuse announcementsApi.searchLearners style endpoint). After mutations, patch the single row locally (or refetch the current page only) instead of reloading everything.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin and manager (registrations, allocation use requireManagerOrAdmin). Preserve admin-only guards and org scoping on the new query params; keep KPI totals independent of the page filter. CSV export (downloadCsv in learner-management.svelte:158) currently exports whatever is in memory, so after server paging it needs a dedicated export endpoint (streamed or chunked) or it silently exports only one page. Page number must reset to 1 on filter/search change (learner-management.svelte does not reset pageNum on search, only clamps). Tutor allocation uniqueness and 'unallocated learners' indicators on the admin dashboard must not rely on the full list being loaded.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: learner-management.load() fetches the whole roster and filters/pages client-side (filtered.slice at learner-management.svelte:90); allocation assign dialogs render every tutor and learner as Select.Item (allocation.svelte:150-175); registrations and progression are also full-set. Real at thousands of learners, but these are admin/manager-only screens with a handful of concurrent users, so the effect is slow pages and big payloads for few users rather than a throughput risk to the shared droplet. The claim that pageNum does not reset on search is accurate but harmless because it is clamped (line 88). Severity high is overstated; medium.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do it incrementally. CSV export must move to a dedicated endpoint before the roster is paged, or it silently exports one page. KPI totals must stay independent of page filters. Keep requireManagerOrAdmin/requireAdmin guards and org scoping on new query params. The searchable async combobox for assign dialogs is the highest value, lowest risk piece (a Select with thousands of options is the first thing that will freeze). Effort L is right, so do not bundle it with the quick wins.

confirmed.title: Tutor submissions grid loads every roster learner with all versions and file lists, refetches whole grid after each grade, and never clears on assessment switch
confirmed.current: loadSubmissions returns rows[] for every allocated learner each with versions[], files[], feedbackFiles[]. All rows are rendered in one table (the {#each filteredRows} at line 267 expands nested file/version rows). Search/status filtering is client-side. onGraded() re-requests the entire grid after every single grade. submissionsGrid is never reset in loadSubmissions, so when the user changes lessonId/assessmentKey the old assessment's rows stay on screen until the new response lands (the `!grid` spinner only shows on the very first load), and the #submissionsReqId guard only protects against races, not stale display. If the request fails the page shows an endless Spinner (onError only raises a snackbar).
confirmed.breaks_at: A popular course workbook with 500+ allocated learners (or an admin viewing the course-wide set) produces a very large nested payload and a DOM of thousands of nodes; grading 100 submissions in a session triggers 100 full re-downloads.
confirmed.fix: Server-side paginate the grid (limit 50, page, plus state filter and search) and return files only for expanded rows (lazy detail endpoint). After grading, patch the single row from the POST result (or refetch just that learner's row). Set submissionsGrid = null (or a stale flag) at the start of loadSubmissions for a different assessment, and render an error state with a Retry button when the request fails.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor and admin grading flow is the core marking path: the gradeTargetId logic (page line ~120) and the 'download all' zip must keep operating on the full allocated set, not just the visible page. Allocation scoping stays server-side. Edge cases: a learner is graded by another tutor/admin concurrently (409 on stale gradeTarget), draft vs final versions, filter state preserved across refetch.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: loadSubmissions sets submissionsGrid only in onSuccess and never clears it when lessonId/assessmentKey change, so the previous assessment's rows stay visible until the new response (the !grid spinner only covers the first load); on error only a snackbar is raised and the first-load spinner stays forever. The reqId guard only handles ordering. Per-assessment rows are bounded by allocated learners for a tutor, so the payload risk is mainly for admins or very large cohorts; stale-display and no-error-state are the more immediate correctness bugs.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Clearing the grid on assessment change is a safe one-line fix, and a retry/error state is cheap. Paging the grid needs care: gradeTargetId logic and the 'download all' zip must operate on the full allocated set, and server paging must be applied after the allocation filter. Prefer patching the single row after grading instead of a paged rewrite.

confirmed.title: Course layout loads the full member roster into the client store and re-fetches the entire course after any people change
confirmed.current: courseApi.get returns the course with group (all members/people with profile), lessons, sections and attendance (route doc: 'group, members, lessons, sections, attendance'). Every course page (lesson view for learners, admin settings, etc.) mounts this layout and holds courseApi.group.people in memory; the layout and several pages do `.find(person => person.profileId === $profile.id)` to resolve the viewer's own membership, and people.svelte renders all members unpaginated, running a double sort and filterPeople inside the {#each} expression (line 142) on every reactive update. refreshCourse() (after add/remove) re-downloads the entire course; the people layout's refresh also calls invalidateAll(), which reruns the root server layout (org fetch, OG HEAD) and all page loads. console.log('response', response.data) at course.svelte.ts:216 prints the whole payload on every fetch.
confirmed.breaks_at: A course with a few thousand enrolled learners makes every learner and admin download the roster just to open a lesson; people table renders thousands of rows with avatars; refreshing after a single enrolment is a full roster + lessons re-download. member-visibility.ts trims it for tutors but not for admins.
confirmed.fix: Split the course payload: (a) core course + sections/lessons + the caller's own membership ({isMember, roleId}) for the layout/permission check, (b) a paginated, searchable members endpoint for people.svelte/attendance/compliance (limit 25-50, role filter, search). Patch the local list on add/delete instead of refreshCourse(); use invalidate('app:course') keyed dependencies instead of invalidateAll(). Remove the console.log. Compute sorted/filtered people once with $derived, not inside the template.
confirmed.flow_risk: RoleBasedSecurity (features/ui/role-based-security.svelte:23), certificates, attendance, compliance and the layout isPermitted check all read courseApi.group.people to find the current user's role, so the new 'my membership' field must replace these lookups or learners/tutors will be rejected as non-members. Attendance and compliance pages need the full learner list (page it or load on demand). Tutor visibility rules from member-visibility.ts must be retained for the new members endpoint.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed that courseApi.get returns group/people and the layout/RoleBasedSecurity resolve the viewer's role via .find over group.people, and that console.log('response', response.data) at course.svelte.ts:216 dumps the whole payload on every fetch (verified). With ~40 learners today it is trivial; it only matters when a single course has thousands of members, and member-visibility.ts already trims for tutors. Not a near-term break. The invalidateAll() in people layout re-running the root layout (org fetch, OG warm) is a real extra cost.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Remove the console.log immediately (safe). The full redesign (split payload, my-membership field) is the riskiest change in this list because RoleBasedSecurity, certificates, attendance, compliance and the layout permission check all read group.people; do it last, add a 'myMembership' field first and migrate readers one by one before slimming the roster. Replace invalidateAll() with keyed invalidate().

confirmed.title: HTTP client retries every 5xx, including POST/PUT, and the retry attempt has no timeout
confirmed.current: ApiClient.makeRequest retries once (retries=1, 1s backoff) on any >=500 response and on network TypeErrors for ALL HTTP methods. The timeout timer is cleared right after the first attempt (clearTimeout(timeoutId) at line 177 / 210), so the retried request has no timeout at all and can hang indefinitely (the abort signal is still merged but nothing triggers it).
confirmed.breaks_at: When the single droplet is overloaded and returns 502/503/504, every client immediately doubles its traffic (retry storm exactly when capacity is lowest). Non-idempotent calls (record a grade, send a message, create learner, approve registration, submit coursework) can be executed twice if the first attempt succeeded server-side but the response was a gateway 5xx, producing duplicate messages/submissions. A hung retry leaves the UI in a permanent loading state.
confirmed.fix: Only retry idempotent methods (GET/HEAD) and only on 502/503/504 + network errors, with jittered backoff and a Retry-After honour; never auto-retry POST/PUT/DELETE unless the caller opts in with an idempotency key. Create a fresh AbortController/timeout per attempt. Add a global in-flight GET de-dupe (same URL within ~1s shares a promise) to remove double fetches caused by effects firing twice.
confirmed.flow_risk: All roles. A few flows may currently depend on the silent retry to mask cold-start 5xx after deploys (users will now see an error snackbar instead; pair with proper error/retry UI). Ensure the opt-in idempotency key exists server-side for submission/message POSTs before enabling retries on them.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed in apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/services/api/index.ts. The retry loop retries any >=500 and network TypeError for every HTTP method, and clearTimeout(timeoutId) runs after the first attempt so the retried attempt has no timeout (the merged signal is only aborted by the timer that was cleared). Retries are 1, so worst-case traffic doubling under 5xx, not unbounded storms. Duplicate side effects need a server-side commit followed by a gateway 5xx, which is rare.
