Real defect, but medium; high overstated.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Restrict retries to GET/HEAD (and 502/503/504 plus network errors), create a fresh timeout per attempt, add jitter. Before turning retries off for POST, check for flows that rely on it to mask post-deploy 5xx (an accompanying error/retry UI is advisable). The proposed global GET de-dupe is optional and riskier (shared Response bodies can only be read once; clone them).

confirmed.title: Message threads load full history, conversation inbox is unpaginated, and there is no update path so users reload to see replies
confirmed.current: loadThread/open return view.messages for the whole conversation history; the thread renders every message. loadConversations returns every conversation a tutor participates in with no limit. The learner entry does a serial waterfall: loadMyTutor then open (a POST that upserts the thread on every visit). There is no polling or refetch, so a user waiting on a reply reloads the page, which re-runs the full chain above. Sends append locally only.
confirmed.breaks_at: Long-running tutor-learner threads (months of messages) become large payloads; a tutor with 200+ learners downloads and renders every conversation row. Reload-driven refreshing multiplies page loads.
confirmed.fix: Add cursor pagination (latest 30, 'load older' via before=<id>) to the thread endpoint, and limit+cursor to the conversations list. Return myTutor + thread in one call for the learner entry. Add a lightweight visibility-gated refresh (e.g. check unread counts via the existing notification poll and refetch only the open thread's new messages with ?after=<lastId>).
confirmed.flow_risk: Only participants may read (API participant + allocation enforcement) so pagination params must not bypass it; archived/read-only threads (reallocation) must stay readable by their new rules. Unread dots should come from the server's unread flag; ensure marking-as-read happens when the thread is opened, not per poll. Admin oversight view (read-only) shares the endpoint.
confirmed.verifier_note: Plausible: messaging service has no limit (grep of services/comms/messaging.ts finds none), and the thread renders full history with no refresh path. Today's volume is trivial; thread length grows slowly (human messages), and a tutor's conversation count is bounded by allocation. This is a UX and future-size issue, not an immediate scale risk.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Cursor pagination for thread history is fine. Keep participant plus allocation enforcement in the API for any before/after params. Do not add a new poll unless it is visibility-gated and shares the notification poll.

confirmed.title: Announcements feed (including archived items) is fetched unbounded on every tutor/learner home and by multiple components
confirmed.current: loadFeed() GETs /announcements with no limit; archived items come back too (BroadcastBanner filters !a.archived and slices to 3 client-side). It is called from the tutor dashboard page, again from the BroadcastBanner on that same page, and from the learner dashboard. The tutor page then renders the whole items list through AnnouncementsList. Dismissed ids accumulate in localStorage forever.
confirmed.breaks_at: Years of broadcasts to 'all learners' are downloaded by every learner on every home visit (N learners x full history). Duplicate request per tutor dashboard load.
confirmed.fix: Server: default to unarchived, limit 10-20, with ?before cursor for a history page; add a tiny ETag/Cache-Control (private, max-age=60). Client: single owner for loadFeed (BroadcastBanner or the page) and a short client-side freshness window (skip refetch if loaded <60s ago); prune dismissed ids not in the feed.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin broadcasts management page (org/[slug]/broadcasts) needs the archived items, so keep an explicit includeArchived=true for manage mode. Audience scoping (learner: all_learners + enrolled + targeted + their tutor's group) must remain server-side.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: loadFeed is called on the tutor page, again by BroadcastBanner, and from the learner dashboard; the services layer has no limit, and BroadcastBanner filters archived and slices to 3 client-side. Broadcast counts are small (tens per year), so the payload is negligible; the duplicate request is the only immediate waste.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Remove the duplicate loadFeed and add a freshness window; default the feed to unarchived with a limit; keep includeArchived for the admin broadcasts manage page and keep audience scoping server-side.

confirmed.title: Per-request console.log in server hot paths, including a log of the session cookie string
confirmed.current: getApiHeaders() does console.log('headers', headers) where headers.cookie is the user's Better Auth session cookie string, on every SSR load that uses it (marks, submissions, analytics, org courses/audience...). getSessionData logs 'has locals' per request and getThroughAuthClient logs baseURL per request; root and org layouts log timing lines per navigation; layout-setup logs 'it is custom domain'. Docker's default json-file driver on the 4 GB droplet has no rotation configured by these files.
confirmed.breaks_at: At thousands of requests/min the container log grows by tens of MB per hour (disk fill on a small droplet, extra CPU in stringifying objects), and the session cookie of every user rendering these pages is written in clear text to the container logs, so anyone with log access (or a log shipper) can hijack sessions. This contradicts the HP/LOG-1 note in hooks.server.ts.
confirmed.fix: Delete the cookie/headers log immediately and gate the remaining logs behind a LOG_LEVEL/dev flag; log slow requests only (>500ms). Set `logging: driver json-file, options max-size/max-file` on every service in docker-compose.deploy.yaml.
confirmed.flow_risk: None functionally. Make sure no on-call runbook depends on the [+layout.server] timing lines (replace with a slow-request log).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed and the most concrete security item: getApiHeaders in lib/utils/services/api/index.ts:322 does console.log('headers', headers) where headers.cookie is the full session cookie string, on every SSR load that calls it, so session tokens land in the container logs. Also confirmed: console.log('has locals'), 'baseURL' per request (session.ts:15,44; auth/server.ts:11), per-navigation timing logs in root and org layouts, and docker-compose.deploy.yaml has no logging: max-size/max-file options on any service. The hooks.server.ts HP/LOG-1 cleanup removed the cookie log there but missed this one. Scale cost is modest; the credential exposure is the real issue.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Delete the two console.log lines in getApiHeaders immediately (zero functional risk), then gate or remove the rest, and add json-file max-size/max-file to every compose service. Consider rotating sessions if logs were ever shipped or shared.

confirmed.title: Heavy libraries are statically imported into chunks that learners load (video encoder, AI chat, Sentry replay, sourcemaps)
confirmed.current: video.svelte -> lesson-video-simple-card -> video-card-dropdown -> hls-encoder statically imports `mediabunny` (an in-browser video transcoder), so any learner opening a video lesson downloads the encoder, although only admins upload. The course layout imports the ai-assistant barrel (AiCourseChat, @ai-sdk/svelte, ai) and calls sidePanel.register only if AI_ENABLED, but AI_ENABLED is a hard-coded false (utils/constants/features.ts:8) so that code is dead weight in the layout chunk for every course page. hooks.client.ts imports all of @sentry/sveltekit including replayIntegration even though Sentry.init is skipped when PUBLIC_IS_SELFHOSTED=true. build.sourcemap=true emits .map files into the client build that adapter-node serves.
confirmed.breaks_at: Larger first-load JS per course page on mobile/slow links (learners are the mass audience), more bytes parsed per navigation, longer on-droplet builds (the 20-45 min build that degrades the live site) and a larger image; public sourcemaps expose the source.
confirmed.fix: Dynamic-import hls-encoder/mediabunny only inside the upload/encode handlers (`const { encodeAndUploadHls } = await import('./hls-encoder')`); lazy-load AiCourseChat and the ai-assistant barrel behind `if (AI_ENABLED)` with dynamic import (or remove the code path); make the Sentry import conditional/dynamic and skip entirely for self-hosted; set sourcemap to false (or 'hidden' and don't ship the .map files). Run `vite build` with rollup-plugin-visualizer once to confirm the biggest chunks.
confirmed.flow_risk: Video upload/re-encode flow (admin) must still load the encoder on demand: verify the first click is not blocked by an unhandled chunk-load failure (add a retry/loading state). AI assistant is disabled, so no learner flow depends on it. Error monitoring: self-hosted already has Sentry disabled, but client errors still flow through client-error-log.ts to /log/client.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly confirmed. hls-encoder.ts statically imports mediabunny and is imported statically by video-card-dropdown.svelte and upload-video.svelte, so it is in the lesson chunk learners load. build.sourcemap is true. hooks.client.ts imports the whole Sentry SDK though init is skipped self-hosted. The AI claim is unverified: AI_ENABLED is a literal const false in features.ts, but the course layout statically imports the ai-assistant barrel (aiAssistantPanelDefinition, ContentAskAiBar) and I could not confirm Rollup drops it, so this needs a bundle visualizer before acting. Impact is first-load bytes only; no throughput effect. Public sourcemaps are low risk since the code is AGPL and the repo URL is already exposed.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Dynamic-import the encoder in the upload handlers (admin-only) with a loading/retry state; measure with rollup-plugin-visualizer before touching the AI barrel; turn off sourcemaps only if build time matters (it also shortens the on-droplet build). Low priority.

confirmed.title: Several list screens show a permanent spinner or 'Loading…' when the API is slow or fails, with no retry
confirmed.current: Pages gate on `!data` / `!loaded` and the API classes' onError only raises a snackbar (or nothing, e.g. registrations/learner-management/allocation just keep the previous state). A timeout (30s) or 5xx leaves the Spinner/'Loading…' forever, and BaseApi.isLoading is a single boolean per singleton, so concurrent calls (loadCaseload + loadPipeline on the tutor dashboard) flip it false as soon as the first one finishes and show 'No programmes yet' while the other is still in flight.
confirmed.breaks_at: Under load (slow API, overloaded droplet) users cannot tell failure from loading and hit refresh, which adds more load; empty-state messages ('Nothing awaiting marking, you are all caught up') can be shown to a tutor while the request is actually still pending or failed, which is misleading in a marking workflow.
confirmed.fix: Give each load a status of idle/loading/error/loaded (track per request key, not one shared isLoading); render skeletons while loading, an inline 'Could not load. Retry' on error, and only show the empty-state copy after a successful empty response. Add AbortController cancellation on route change.
confirmed.flow_risk: UI-only, all roles. Keep the existing reqId staleness guards (progression/submissions/unit) when switching to per-key status so old responses cannot overwrite new ones.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed for the submissions page (spinner gated on !grid, error only raises a snackbar) and BaseApi.isLoading is a single boolean per singleton (base.svelte.ts: sets true at start, false at end), so concurrent loadCaseload plus loadPipeline can flip it early. UX-only; a timeout is 30s and then a snackbar shows, so users are told something failed. Not a scalability issue per se.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Per-request status and retry button is fine; keep the existing reqId guards.

confirmed.title: Admin Users list loses the active search and has an unguarded race after role/status/create mutations
confirmed.current: usersApi.list({search}) never stores the search (the `search` field at line 51 is unused). changeRole/setStatus call this.list() with no opts, so after acting on a searched row the table silently reverts to the unfiltered page; createUser/onboardLearner jump to page 1 without the search. There is no request-id guard, so a slow earlier debounced search response can overwrite a newer one.
confirmed.breaks_at: With thousands of users, searching then changing a role causes the admin to lose their place and may act on the wrong visible row after the list re-renders; out-of-order responses show stale search results.
confirmed.fix: Persist `this.search = opts.search ?? this.search` in list(), reuse it in no-arg refetches, add a monotonic request id (like caseloadApi.#progressionReqId) and AbortController, and enforce a minimum query length of 2 chars.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin user-management only. Role changes for the earliest admin / super-admin protection are enforced server-side and unaffected.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: UsersApi.list never stores opts.search into this.search; changeRole/setStatus/createUser call list() or list({page:1}) without search, and there is no request-id guard. Admin-only convenience bug, no scale impact.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Persist the search and add a request counter. Trivial. Not worth bundling with scale work.

confirmed.title: Client IP is taken from attacker-controlled headers, so every IP-keyed rate limit can be bypassed
confirmed.current: extractClientIp trusts cf-connecting-ip first, then x-real-ip, then the FIRST x-forwarded-for hop. There is no Cloudflare in front (proxy-api-request.ts comments say so) and the Caddyfile neither strips nor overwrites those headers. The dashboard proxy copies ALL browser headers (`new Headers(request.headers)`) to the api. A client can send `cf-connecting-ip: <random>` on every request to get a fresh bucket. This defeats the global anonymous limiter, unsplashRateLimit, invite preview/accept limiters, widget payload limiters, clientLogRateLimit and the enroll limiter's ip fallback. The registration per-IP cap (services/registration/rate-limit.ts) is fed from the dashboard-set XFF so it is less exposed. Better-auth's own login throttle uses only x-forwarded-for, which is correct.
confirmed.breaks_at: As soon as the site is public and discoverable: any scripted client can hammer the unauthenticated endpoints (invite token guessing/preview, /unsplash credit burn, /log/client, widget payload, public course/org-site reads) with no effective cap, each costing a DB query on a 10-connection pool.
confirmed.fix: 1) Caddy: inside the site block add `request_header -CF-Connecting-IP`, `request_header -X-Real-IP`, and `header_up X-Forwarded-For {remote_host}` so Caddy is the single source of truth. 2) In the dashboard proxy, delete cf-connecting-ip and x-real-ip from upstreamHeaders and only forward XFF. 3) In extractClientIp, drop cf-connecting-ip/x-real-ip unless an env flag (e.g. TRUSTED_PROXY=cloudflare) is set; use the LAST hop Caddy appended (or the single value) rather than split(',')[0]. 4) Keep a per-route limit that is independent of IP (e.g. per invite token / per course) for the most sensitive public endpoints.
confirmed.flow_risk: Anonymous flows (invite preview/accept, public course pages, registration, widgets) all key off this. If Caddy ever gets a CDN in front, the XFF logic must be revisited or all users collapse into one bucket. SSR calls with PRIVATE_SERVER_KEY are exempt from the limiter and must stay so. Admin, tutor, learner, manager authenticated flows are keyed by user id and are unaffected.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. extractClientIp (key-generators.ts:20-50) prefers cf-connecting-ip, then x-real-ip, then the first XFF hop. The Caddyfile does not strip those headers. proxyRequestToApi (proxy-api-request.ts:~117) starts from `new Headers(request.headers)` and only overwrites XFF, so a browser-sent cf-connecting-ip reaches the api. The code comment says 'cf-connecting-ip is NOT used', which is false for extractClientIp. One header per request gives a fresh bucket for the invite, unsplash, log-client, payment-request and anonymous global limiters. Correction to the finding: the registration limiter is not safe either, but for a different reason (see missed items). Better-auth login throttling uses only x-forwarded-for, as the auditor says. Caddy v2 reverse_proxy already overwrites an untrusted client's XFF by default, so XFF is trustworthy as the first hop.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Simplest safe fix: in extractClientIp, drop cf-connecting-ip and x-real-ip entirely (no Cloudflare), keep XFF first hop then socket address. Also delete those two headers in proxyRequestToApi. The Caddy `request_header -CF-Connecting-IP -X-Real-IP` lines are optional defence in depth. Do not switch to the LAST XFF hop without checking: Caddy sends a single value, so first and last are the same, but the change adds risk if a CDN is added later. Keep the SSR PRIVATE_SERVER_KEY exemption. Add a unit test that a request with cf-connecting-ip keys on the XFF value.

confirmed.title: Broadcast to all learners does N sequential DB writes inside the HTTP request
confirmed.current: publishAnnouncement awaits emitNotification for every recipient. emitNotification loops recipients sequentially and per recipient does an INSERT into notification, then (because emailTemplateId is set) a getNotificationPreference SELECT, then enqueueTransactionalEmail. getOrgLearnerIds loads every learner id. Nothing is chunked or moved to the jobs worker.
confirmed.breaks_at: ~2,000-5,000 learners: 2-3 round trips each over the Supabase transaction pooler (5-20 ms) is 20-300 s for one request. The dashboard proxy and Caddy have no timeout, the browser gives up, the admin clicks Publish again and a duplicate announcement plus a second full fan-out starts (no idempotency key). It also pins a pool connection for the whole duration, starving other users. Same pattern in registration.submitted, course notifications and message.received but those have few recipients.
confirmed.fix: Insert the announcement row, return 201 immediately, and enqueue ONE BullMQ job (apps/jobs) carrying announcementId. The worker resolves recipients, bulk-inserts notifications in chunks of ~500 (`insert().values([...])`), fetches notification_preference for the whole chunk with one `inArray` query, and uses queue.addBulk for emails. Add an idempotency guard (unique (announcement_id, user_id) on notification or a published_at claim) so a retry or double click cannot fan out twice. Make emitNotification accept a batch API (emitNotificationBatch) and keep the single-recipient path for the small cases.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin publish flow: recipients now see the announcement slightly later (seconds), and the in-app feed query (listAnnouncementsForLearner) does not depend on notification rows so visibility is unchanged. Tutor-targeted ('tutor' audience) must keep using listLearnersForTutor so the allocation rule is preserved. Edge cases: learner enrolled/removed mid-fan-out, worker crash mid-way (needs resumable chunks), archived/deleted announcement before the job runs (job must re-check deletedAt).
confirmed.verifier_note: Fan-out inside the request is real (announcements.ts:185-212 awaits emitNotification, which loops recipients sequentially, notify.ts:51). The cost is overstated. publishAnnouncement builds recipients as {userId, emailFields} with NO email field, so emitNotification does `if (!input.emailTemplateId || !recipient.email) continue` and never runs the preference SELECT or enqueues any email. Today it is exactly one INSERT per learner, not 2-3 round trips. At 5,000 learners that is roughly 25-100 s, which is still a real timeout and double-click hazard. Admin-only and infrequent, so medium. Side finding: announcement emails are effectively never sent because recipients carry no email, so the opt-in announcement email category is dead code.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: For in-app only, a chunked multi-row INSERT (500 per statement) inside the request finishes in about 1 s at 5k learners and needs no job, so it is a much smaller change than a BullMQ job. Do the job route only if email is wired in. If email is added, fetch notification_preference with one inArray per chunk and use queue.addBulk. Add an idempotency guard (reject a duplicate title/body/audience from the same author within a short window, or a claim column), because the announcement row is inserted before the fan-out. Keep the 'tutor' audience on listLearnersForTutor.

confirmed.title: Message thread returns the OLDEST 200 messages, and the inbox query scans every message of every thread
confirmed.current: listMessages orders by created_at ASC and applies LIMIT 200, although the doc comment says 'the newest limit are returned'. After a thread passes 200 messages the view is frozen on the first 200 and new messages (including the one just sent) never appear; the thread also cannot be paged. listConversationsForParticipant uses selectDistinctOn(thread_id) over a join of ALL messages of ALL the user's threads, ordered by thread_id, created_at desc, then sorts in JS. There is no rate limit on POST /messages/threads/:id/messages beyond the global 100/min.
confirmed.breaks_at: A busy tutor-learner pair crosses 200 messages within weeks, then chat looks broken (tutor and learner stop seeing each other's replies). A tutor with 100 learners x 300 messages = 30k rows read and sorted on every inbox load and on every poll.
confirmed.fix: listMessages: select newest N (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT n) then reverse, and add a `before` cursor (created_at,id) param to the GET thread route (zod max 100) for older pages. Inbox: add last_message_at/last_message_id/last_message_sender_id columns on message_thread updated in the same statement/transaction as insertMessage (or use a LATERAL join `... JOIN LATERAL (select ... from message where thread_id=t.id order by created_at desc limit 1)`), plus an index on message(thread_id, created_at desc). Add a per-user rate limiter (e.g. 30/min) on send. Add message.sender index if missing.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner and tutor chat views (both use buildView). Admin read-only oversight shares buildView so it gets the same fix. Keep the participant/allocation/archived checks in messaging.ts untouched (tutors still only reach allocated learners). Edge cases: unread logic compares last message time to read cursor, so moving to a denormalised last_message must keep that comparison; backfill the new columns in the migration.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed functional bug. listMessages (packages/db/src/queries/comms/message.ts:~98) orders ASC with limit 200 while the doc comment says the newest are returned, so past 200 messages the thread is frozen on the first 200 for both tutor and learner. One thread per pair (message_thread_pair_unique), so a busy pair reaches 200 in weeks. The inbox DISTINCT ON query does read all messages of all of the user's threads and sorts in JS, but at realistic caseloads (tens of threads) this is moderate, not severe. Correction: an index on message(thread_id, created_at) ALREADY exists (idx_message_thread_created, schema.ts:4293), so the 'add index' suggestion is moot.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Fix listMessages with an inner query ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT n, then reverse. Add an optional `before` cursor later. For the inbox, a LATERAL join (latest message per thread) using the existing index is enough; denormalised last_message columns are not needed yet. A per-user send limiter (e.g. 30/min) is cheap and fine. Do not touch isParticipant or isTutorAllocatedToLearner checks in buildView.

confirmed.title: Allocation picker silently truncates tutors and learners at 100; allocation list is unbounded
confirmed.current: getAssignablePeople fetches getOrganizationUsers(..., limit: 100) for tutors and for learners; getOrganizationUsers hard-caps limit at 100 (users.ts:31) and orders by member id desc, with no search. Learner number 101+ can never be selected to allocate to a tutor. GET /organization/allocations returns every allocation row (joined to two profiles) in one response.
confirmed.breaks_at: Immediately functional at >100 active learners (core allocation workflow, and therefore the tutor-sees-only-allocated-learners model, cannot be completed for new learners). The unbounded allocations list grows to tens of thousands of rows (tutors x learners) and is sent on every page load.
confirmed.fix: Replace the 100-row dump with a server-side searchable picker: reuse searchOrgAudience / getOrganizationUsers with `search` + small page size (20) and a debounced query from the form, and exclude already-allocated pairs server side. Paginate GET /organization/allocations (page/limit max 100, optional tutorId and learnerId filters, ORDER BY created_at, id) and add an index on tutor_allocation(organization_id, created_at). Keep createTutorAllocation's role validation exactly as is.
confirmed.flow_risk: Manager and Admin allocation screen (frontend change needed to call a search endpoint). Do not loosen requireManagerOrAdmin. Edge cases: learner with no profile row yet (userId null filtered), deactivated users, duplicate pair still handled by the DB unique constraint (409).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. getAssignablePeople (allocation.ts:38-41) calls getOrganizationUsers with limit 100, which also hard-caps at 100 (users.ts:~31), with no search and ordered by newest member. Past 100 active learners or tutors, some people can never be picked in the allocation UI, which blocks the tutor-sees-only-allocated-learners workflow. listAllocationsByOrg (allocation.ts query:133-152) has no limit or pagination and returns every row. Not a problem at today's 40 learners but a hard functional break just past 100. Note getAssignablePeople is also used by management.ts / tutor-management (manage-courses-dialog), so those consumers need the same change.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: getOrganizationUsers already supports search and page, so reuse it with a debounced picker (page size 20), and exclude already-allocated pairs server side. Update every consumer of getAssignablePeople (allocation and tutor-management features), not just the allocation page. Paginate the allocations list with tutorId/learnerId filters and an index on tutor_allocation(organization_id, created_at). Do not change createTutorAllocation role validation or requireManagerOrAdmin.

confirmed.title: Redis client queues commands forever when Redis is down; several callers have no timeout
confirmed.current: createClient has an infinite reconnectStrategy but node-redis' default offline queue (disableOfflineQueue=false, no commandsQueueMaxLength). While Redis is unreachable every command is parked in memory until reconnect. The rate limiter wraps its MULTI in withTimeout(2s) but the timed-out multi is still sitting in the queue (4 commands per request, flushed later). The presigned-download path (`await redis.mGet(...)` in a try/catch) never errors, it just hangs, so every document/video download request hangs until Redis returns. Same for the dash and analytics caches and OAuth handoff.
confirmed.breaks_at: A Redis container restart/OOM on the shared 4 GB droplet (it is in the same compose, appendonly on): all presign-download calls hang and the queued-command memory grows with request rate; after reconnect the backlog replays. Learners cannot open materials and tutors cannot download coursework during the outage.
confirmed.fix: createClient({ disableOfflineQueue: true, ...}) (or commandsQueueMaxLength: 1000) so commands reject immediately while disconnected and every existing try/catch fails open as intended; also wrap non-limiter Redis calls (s3.ts mGet/multi, dash cache, analytics cache, oauth-handoff) in withTimeout(…,1000). Set `maxmemory 256mb` + `maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` on the redis service (cache + rate-limit keys only) but keep BullMQ on noeviction (separate Redis DB/instance, since BullMQ requires noeviction).
confirmed.flow_risk: Rate limiter keeps failing open (already designed). BullMQ producers in apps/api (enqueueTransactionalEmail etc.) use their own connections from @cio/jobs; check they are not the same client, otherwise disabling the offline queue changes their startup behaviour (connectRedis is awaited before serve so the happy path is unaffected). Presign cache becomes best-effort only, which is already the intent.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: createClient in packages/core/src/utils/redis/redis.ts sets no disableOfflineQueue, so node-redis queues commands while disconnected. generateDownloadPresignedUrls (s3.ts:~71) awaits redis.mGet inside try/catch but with no timeout, so while Redis is down it hangs rather than failing open. The limiter's withTimeout does time out but leaves the command queued. dash.ts:126 and analytics reads behave the same way. It only bites during a Redis restart or OOM, which is rare, so medium rather than high.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Two corrections. (1) Setting disableOfflineQueue:true turns the hang into an immediate ClientOfflineError rejection. Any Redis caller WITHOUT try/catch (oauth-handoff, fire-and-forget callers) then produces an unhandledRejection, and process-error-guards.ts exits the API for it, because 'The client is offline' does not match the transient-Redis regex. Add that message to TRANSIENT_REDIS_MESSAGE_PATTERN (or fix the guards first) before flipping this flag. Prefer wrapping presign/dash/analytics reads in withTimeout(1000) as the lower-risk change. (2) The maxmemory-policy advice is wrong as written: the policy is per Redis instance, not per DB, so a separate DB does not protect BullMQ from allkeys-lru eviction. The same Redis serves BullMQ (REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379 for api and jobs). Use a separate Redis instance for cache and rate limits, or skip eviction tuning (or use volatile-lru with care).

confirmed.title: No timeouts on S3, SMTP, fetch calls, request bodies or whole requests
confirmed.location: packages/core/src/config/storage.ts:96-112 (S3Client); packages/core/src/utils/s3.ts:19-43; packages/email/src/utils/services/nodemailer.ts:26-37; apps/api/src/routes/unsplash/unsplash.ts:36; apps/api/src/services/org/domain.ts:74; apps/api/src/utils/cloudflare.ts:12,47; apps/api/src/services/course-import/course-import.ts:148; packages/core/src/services/course/landing-page.ts:67; apps/api/src/app.ts (no bodyLimit/timeout middleware)
confirmed.current: grep finds no AbortSignal/timeout/bodyLimit anywhere in apps/api. The S3Client has no requestHandler (no connection/request timeout, default SDK retries 3), nodemailer createTransport has no connectionTimeout/greetingTimeout/socketTimeout and no pool (new TLS+AUTH connection per message), and every fetch() to Unsplash/Approximated/Cloudflare/YouTube/Tinybird uses Node's 5-minute undici defaults. uploadImage (/media/image) and /agent/upload call c.req.parseBody() which buffers the whole multipart body before the MAX_IMAGE_SIZE check; /media/image only needs authMiddleware, so any learner can use it. The dashboard SvelteKit proxy fetch() to the api also has no timeout and buffers request bodies with arrayBuffer().
confirmed.breaks_at: One slow Supabase Storage or SMTP incident turns into stuck requests that hold pool connections and memory until 5 min later; with thousands of users this exhausts the single Node process (event loop memory) and the 10-connection DB pool. A burst of 25 MB image POSTs from many learners buffers 25 MB each in RAM.
confirmed.fix: S3: `new S3Client({ requestHandler: new NodeHttpHandler({ connectionTimeout: 3000, requestTimeout: 15000 }), maxAttempts: 2 })`. Nodemailer: `pool: true, maxConnections: 5, maxMessages: 100, connectionTimeout: 10000, greetingTimeout: 10000, socketTimeout: 20000`. fetch: `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` on each external call (wrap in a tiny fetchWithTimeout helper). Hono: add `bodyLimit({ maxSize })` per route group (JSON 1 MB, media image 6 MB, agent upload MAX_AGENT_DOCUMENT_SIZE) and a global `timeout(30000)` middleware excluding streaming routes (/agent/chat, /hls, download-all). Restrict /media/image to staff (requireStaff) or add an upload rate limiter like presign has. Add `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` to dashboard proxyRequestToApi.
confirmed.flow_risk: Uploads: size limit must exceed the legitimate multipart envelope (dashboard BODY_SIZE_LIMIT is 25 MB). Learners uploading avatars use /media/image: if restricted to staff, learner avatar upload breaks, so give learners a per-user limiter instead. The AI chat and HLS routes are long-lived streams and must be excluded from any global timeout. Retried SMTP sends from the jobs worker must remain idempotent (idempotencyKey already used).
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly real, overstated. Confirmed: getS3Client (storage.ts:96-112) has no requestHandler timeouts. The fetch calls to unsplash.ts:36, domain.ts:74, cloudflare.ts:12/47, course-import.ts:148 and landing-page.ts:67 have no AbortSignal, and the dashboard proxy fetch has none. No hono timeout or bodyLimit exists. Overstated: nodemailer is not unbounded (its defaults are connectionTimeout 2 min, greetingTimeout 30 s, socketTimeout 10 min), and email sends run in the jobs worker, not on a request path, so a pool is a nicety. The dashboard adapter-node BODY_SIZE_LIMIT (26214400, docker-compose.deploy.yaml:101) already caps request bodies at 25 MB before the api, and the api is not publicly exposed, so the 'unbounded multipart buffering' claim is weak. /media/image and parseBody (media.ts:10) accept any authenticated user, but the 25 MB cap and the MAX_IMAGE_SIZE check limit the harm.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Do the per-dependency timeouts: S3 NodeHttpHandler with connectionTimeout 3 s and requestTimeout 15-30 s (longer for the zip and upload paths), AbortSignal.timeout(8-10 s) on the external fetches and the dashboard proxy (but NOT for streaming/long routes). Skip the global hono timeout() middleware: it does not cancel the handler, and it would wrongly cut /agent/chat, HLS, download-all and course import. Use a per-user limiter on /media/image rather than restricting it to staff (learner avatars). Drop the nodemailer pool item or defer it.

confirmed.title: 'Download all submissions' builds the entire ZIP in memory, sequentially, with no cap
confirmed.current: zipDocumentObjects downloads each object one after another with getFromS3, calls transformToByteArray (whole file in RAM), adds it to JSZip, then generateAsync returns one Buffer which is sent with c.body(buffer). No limit on number of files or total bytes, no timeout, and the dashboard proxy then buffers the response again.
confirmed.breaks_at: An Admin downloading a workbook for 500 learners x 1-3 docs of 5-20 MB = several hundred MB to 1+ GB held in the api process (plus the proxy copy) on a 4 GB box shared with redis/dashboard/jobs: OOM kill restarts the whole API. Sequential S3 GETs make it take minutes and hold a request open past any reasonable timeout; two admins at once doubles it.
confirmed.fix: Cap the request (e.g. max 200 files / 300 MB, return 413 with a clear message to filter by tutor/cohort), fetch with bounded concurrency (4), and stream the archive (archiver/fflate streaming into a ReadableStream) instead of building a Buffer. Better: make it an async job (BullMQ in apps/jobs) that writes the zip to the documents bucket under a private key and returns a signed URL via a notification. Reuse getAssessmentSubmissions so the allocated-learners scope (tutor sees only allocated learners, admin all) is unchanged.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor and admin 'Download all' button on the submissions grid. Keep the Zip Slip sanitising in download-all.ts. Edge cases: unreadable object is currently skipped silently (keep, but report skipped count), duplicate learner names (folder de-dupe), job result expiry and access check on the signed link (must be re-checked against allocation, never a bare public URL).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed (zip.ts:11-23; download-all.ts). It fetches objects sequentially, calls transformToByteArray on each, JSZip holds all data, generateAsync builds a full Buffer, and it is returned via c.body. No count or size cap. Peak memory is roughly 2-3x the archive size. Scope is one assessment (workbook) per call and admin/tutor only, so it is infrequent, and today there are 7 submissions. At thousands of learners with multi-MB files, one click can OOM the single API container, which takes down everything. Severity medium for trigger rarity, but the blast radius is the whole API.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The cheap, safe first step is a hard cap (e.g. 200 files / 250 MB, 413 with a message) plus bounded concurrency of 4. Streaming (archiver/fflate) is the proper fix. A BullMQ job plus signed link adds an access-control surface, so re-check allocation at download time if you do it. Keep getAssessmentSubmissions scoping and the sanitize() Zip Slip handling. Also fix duplicate names: two files with the same sanitized name in one learner folder overwrite each other in JSZip silently (see missed).

confirmed.title: Coursework file download guard does jsonb @> lookups with no GIN index, one query per key
confirmed.current: assertCourseworkDownloadAccess loops over keys and for each runs `files @> '[{"key":...}]'::jsonb` on coursework_submission, and when that misses, a second @> on coursework_result.feedback_files joined to submissions. There are no GIN indexes in schema.ts or migrations, so each lookup is a sequential scan over every submission (jsonb detoasted). The route for coursework downloads caps keys at 20, but the generic presign routes (/course/.../presign/video|document/download, ZCourseDownloadPresignedUrl) accept an UNBOUNDED keys array and, for non-staff, then call isUnitUnlocked per key in a loop (ownership.ts:306-312).
confirmed.breaks_at: With ~50k+ submissions each download click costs 20+ full-table jsonb scans; a tutor opening a learner with many files, or a script posting thousands of keys to the presign endpoints, saturates the DB pool. Also drives up the storage-side request volume that Supabase already shows (166k storage.objects lookups).
confirmed.fix: Add migrations: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_cw_submission_files_gin ON coursework_submission USING gin (files jsonb_path_ops);` and the same on coursework_result(feedback_files). Add `.max(50)` to ZCourseDownloadPresignedUrl.keys and max length per key. Batch the guard: one query `where files @> any(...)` or resolve owners for the whole key list at once, and batch unit-unlock checks per distinct lesson instead of per key. Longer term store file keys in a child table coursework_file(submission_id, key) with a btree index on key.
confirmed.flow_risk: Download guard is the security lynchpin (learner self / allocated tutor / admin). The batched version must still return 403 when ANY key is unknown or not readable (current all-or-nothing behaviour) and must keep treating a de-allocated tutor and a Manager as denied. Index creation is non-blocking only with CONCURRENTLY (cannot run inside a drizzle migration transaction, apply via the session pooler 5432).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. getSubmissionByFileKey and getSubmissionByFeedbackFileKey (coursework.ts:~205-230) use jsonb @> with no GIN index anywhere in schema.ts or the migrations. assertCourseworkDownloadAccess (ownership.ts:373-391) runs up to two such queries per key, serially. ZCourseDownloadPresignedUrl.keys (course.ts:150-156) has min(1) and no max, and the non-staff material path then loops isUnitUnlocked per key (ownership.ts:~306-312). A seq scan over ~50k rows is roughly tens of ms each, so the cost is real but not catastrophic until the tables are much bigger. The unbounded keys array is the more immediate abuse vector.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add .max(50) (and a key length cap) to the presign schema first. GIN with jsonb_path_ops is correct for @>. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a drizzle or Supabase migration transaction; at current table sizes a plain CREATE INDEX is a fraction of a second, so do that now (or apply CONCURRENTLY manually via the 5432 session pooler). When batching the guard, keep all-or-nothing semantics: every requested key must match a submission AND canReadCoursework must pass for each distinct owning submission; a missing key must still 403. Batch the unit-unlock checks per distinct lessonId.

confirmed.title: Single 10-connection pool, no statement/idle-in-transaction timeouts, and a transaction held open across external calls
confirmed.current: postgres-js max is 10 (DATABASE_POOL_MAX unset in docker-compose.deploy.yaml) with no statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout. Every authenticated request spends at least one query in resolveActor before the handler, plus guard queries. approveRegistration opens a transaction, claims the row and then inside the same transaction runs onboardLearner (auth user creation and invite mail enqueue) so a pooled connection is held across non-DB I/O. Heavy aggregate endpoints (caseload, progression, reports, admin overview) run several large queries in Promise.all.
confirmed.breaks_at: A handful of concurrent slow aggregate requests (admin reports, caseload for a big roster) or approvals during an auth/SMTP slowdown consume all 10 connections; every other request (heartbeats, lesson views, session/actor resolution) queues behind them and the site looks down although /health (no DB) stays green. Runaway queries are never cancelled.
confirmed.fix: Set DATABASE_POOL_MAX explicitly (e.g. 20) after checking the Supabase pooler client limit, and put timeouts on the app DB role instead of startup params (the transaction pooler ignores them): `ALTER ROLE <app_role> SET statement_timeout='15s'; SET idle_in_transaction_session_timeout='10s';` with a separate longer-timeout role for migrations/jobs. Restructure approveRegistration: claim row in a short tx, run onboardLearner outside it, and on failure run a compensating update back to 'pending' (the claim is already a compare-and-swap so concurrency safety is kept). Add a readiness check that runs `select 1` with a timeout.
confirmed.flow_risk: Registration approval (Manager/Admin) behaviour on failure changes from tx rollback to compensating update: needs a test for crash between the two steps (row stuck 'approved' without a user). Statement timeout can cut off legitimate long admin reports, so heavy reports should be paginated/cached first. jobs worker should use its own role/timeouts.
confirmed.verifier_note: Partly real. drizzle.ts:22-30 uses max 10 with no statement/idle-in-tx timeouts (the transaction pooler ignores startup params, so role-level settings are the right place). approveRegistration (decisions.ts:77-125) does hold a pooled connection in runInTransaction across onboardLearner, which uses other connections. Pool exhaustion by slow aggregate endpoints is plausible. The approval transaction hazard is low-frequency because approvals are human-paced.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Role-level statement_timeout is a sound change, but the jobs worker and migrations share the same DATABASE_URL role, so give them a separate role (or set longer timeouts there) to avoid killing legitimate long jobs and migrations. Do NOT blindly raise DATABASE_POOL_MAX to 20: Supabase's pooler client limit is shared by api, jobs and the project's own services (advisor already shows auth_db_connections_absolute), so check the limit first. Do NOT restructure approveRegistration into claim, onboard, compensating-update: the current rollback-on-failure semantics are valuable and the compensating path adds a stuck-'approved' failure mode. Leave it as is unless approvals become bulk or concurrent.

confirmed.title: Several list/report endpoints return the whole org with no pagination or cap
confirmed.current: getTutorCaseload loads the full roster then EVERY submission (with files jsonb, course and lesson joins) for those learners and groups them in JS; for an Admin that is every allocated learner in the org. getProgression/getOrgProgression build rows for the whole roster and run per-course report queries; Learners and Completions reports call it without any cache. listRegistrations returns all registrations of all statuses oldest-first. listAnnouncementsForLearner/Tutor/Org/Course return the full history. getCourseMembers returns every member (also exposed through the public API students endpoint). ZAddCourseMembers is an unbounded array processed sequentially. inArray(learner_id, [...thousands]) also approaches the Postgres 65,535 bind-parameter limit.
confirmed.breaks_at: Roughly 2,000-5,000 learners / 20k+ submissions: multi-MB JSON responses, seconds of CPU per request in the single Node thread (blocks other requests), and high memory. Registration queue and announcement feeds grow forever (never archived).
confirmed.fix: Add page/limit (max 100) or cursor pagination plus server-side filters to: registrations (default status=pending), announcements (cursor by published_at), course members, allocations, caseload (paginate learners; compute 'awaiting marking' via a SQL query limited to the latest unmarked version per unit instead of loading all rows and dropping the `files` column), progression (page the learner rows; compute aggregates in SQL). Cache admin report bundles for 60 s in Redis (not per-process) keyed by org. Cap ZAddCourseMembers at ~200 per request. Replace `inArray(ids)` over a large roster with a join on tutor_allocation.
confirmed.flow_risk: Tutor caseload and pipeline, admin reports, registration queue, announcement feeds: frontend tables must send page params (dashboard changes). Roster scoping must keep going through tutor_allocation (tutor sees only allocated learners; admin union incl. course-team learners) so any SQL rewrite must be reviewed against docs/ACCESS.md section 8. Aggregates (counts, averages) must be computed over the whole roster, not the current page.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed on the paths I opened. listRegistrations (registration.ts:105-130) has no limit and orders oldest-first across all statuses. listAnnouncementsForLearner (announcement.ts:58-100) has no limit. getTutorCaseload (caseload.ts:99-130) loads every submission for the roster in one query and also runs `roster.find(...)` inside the per-submission loop (O(n*m) CPU). listAllocationsByOrg is unbounded. Impact is CPU and JSON size on a single Node thread at thousands of learners. Not an issue at 40 learners. Not every cited item was re-opened (progression, course members), but the pattern is consistent.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Treat as a phased backlog. Quick wins are safe: registrations default to status=pending with a limit; announcements limit 50 with a cursor; replace roster.find with a Map. Larger rewrites (caseload and progression in SQL) must keep roster scoping via tutor_allocation, and aggregates must cover the whole roster, not the page. Avoid inArray over thousands of ids by joining tutor_allocation. Frontend changes are required for paged tables.

confirmed.title: AI chat has no per-user rate limit, no abort/timeout, and its usage cap is check-then-act
confirmed.current: The key generators for agent chat/upload exist but no createRateLimiter uses them, so only the global 100/min per-user limit applies. streamText is called without abortSignal or timeout, so a client disconnect or provider stall keeps the provider call (and cost) running. enforceStudentTutorPolicy reads the monthly message count, but incrementStudentTutorCount only runs in onFinish after the stream completes, and recordTokenUsage also happens there; enforceTokenBalance is likewise read-only up front. onFinish awaits DB writes with no try/catch.
confirmed.breaks_at: A learner firing N parallel chat requests passes the cap check N times before any increment lands, overshooting the per-learner cap and the org token pool (real provider cost). Hundreds of simultaneous streams hold sockets, memory and provider quota on one Node process; there is no cap on concurrent streams.
confirmed.fix: Add createRateLimiter with agentChatKeyGenerator (e.g. 10/min and 200/day per user) and agentUploadKeyGenerator. Pass `abortSignal: AbortSignal.any([c.req.raw.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(120_000)])` to streamText. Make the cap atomic: increment (or reserve) the monthly count with a single `UPDATE ... SET message_count = message_count + 1 WHERE message_count < cap RETURNING` BEFORE calling the model and refund on failure; reserve a token estimate against the pool similarly. Wrap onFinish bodies in try/catch with logging. Add a per-org concurrent-stream counter in Redis (INCR/EXPIRE).
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner AI tutor and teacher course-authoring chat. Long agent runs by teachers are legitimately many steps, so the timeout must exceed MAX_STEPS_PER_ROUND runtime or use per-step timeouts. Reserve-then-refund must not double count when the user retries after a 429. Cap messages shown in the UI (capRemaining) should read the same counter.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. agentChatKeyGenerator/agentUploadKeyGenerator are defined (key-generators.ts:113,131) but referenced nowhere else, so only the global 100/min applies. streamText (agent.ts:598) has no abortSignal. onFinish (agent.ts:608-648) awaits recordTokenUsage and incrementStudentTutorCount with no try/catch, so a DB error there is an unhandled rejection, which exits the process. enforceStudentTutorPolicy only reads the monthly count up front, so parallel requests can overshoot the cap (check-then-act). Impact is real provider cost, but only for users of the AI feature.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add the rate limiters (cheap, safe), the abortSignal combined with a generous timeout (teacher authoring runs are long, so use a per-step or large timeout), and try/catch in onFinish. For the cap race, an atomic reserve-then-refund adds double-count risk on retry; a conditional UPDATE...WHERE message_count < cap RETURNING at request start is fine if the refund path is tested. Optional first step: keep increment in onFinish but add the per-user concurrency limit so overshoot is bounded.

confirmed.title: Any unhandled rejection kills the only API process
confirmed.current: reportFatalProcessError calls process.exit(1) for every uncaughtException/unhandledRejection except transient Redis errors. There is exactly one api replica (compose), restart is `unless-stopped` with a 40 s healthcheck start period. Fire-and-forget async work exists (streamText onFinish DB writes, preloadVerifiedCustomDomainOriginsRegistry().then(...) with no .catch, trackAgentEvent, notification fan-out) and a Postgres/network blip in any of them is an unhandled rejection. handleError also returns 500s without calling Sentry/recordApiError (only app.onError does), so most 500s are not captured in the system event log.
confirmed.breaks_at: One transient DB error in a background callback restarts the API: every in-flight request, upload registration and AI stream fails and users see 502 for ~20-40 s. At thousands of users this happens repeatedly under load.
confirmed.fix: Treat unhandledRejection as log+Sentry only (keep exit for uncaughtException), and add .catch to the known fire-and-forget calls (index.ts preload, onFinish bodies). Call Sentry.captureException and recordApiError from handleError for statusCode >= 500 so route-level 500s are observable. Run two api replicas behind Caddy (see in-memory-state finding) so a restart is not an outage.
confirmed.flow_risk: No user flow changes; risk is masking a genuinely corrupted state: keep exit(1) for uncaughtException and for startup failures. Verify Sentry volume/cost when 500s start being reported.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. process-error-guards.ts:reportFatalProcessError exits 1 for any non-Redis unhandledRejection. index.ts:30 runs preloadVerifiedCustomDomainOriginsRegistry().then(...) with no .catch; the DB query inside is unguarded, so a DB blip at boot gives an unhandled rejection, exit, and a restart loop. agent.ts onFinish also awaits DB writes with no try/catch. There is one api replica. Also confirmed handleError (errors.ts:61-109) logs the full error object for every error and does not call Sentry or recordApiError (only app.onError does), so route-level 500s are logged to console but not captured in Sentry or the system event log.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Add .catch to the preload and wrap onFinish bodies first (smallest, safest). Then consider logging+Sentry only for unhandledRejection while keeping exit for uncaughtException. Add Sentry.captureException and recordApiError for status>=500 in handleError, but watch Sentry quota. Note: this interacts with the Redis disableOfflineQueue change (see redis finding); do not enable that without fixing the guard's transient pattern.

confirmed.title: Per-user heartbeats cost several DB queries and a write each, plus 2 Redis MULTIs
confirmed.current: POST /account/heartbeat runs every ~60 s per open tab and does `UPDATE session SET updated_at=now()` (the ~33k session writes seen in pg_stat_statements). PUT /course/:courseId/lesson/:lessonId/time runs about every 30 s per learner viewing a unit: authMiddleware, global limiter MULTI, unitTimeRateLimit MULTI, courseMemberMiddleware query, assertEnrolledStudentContentAccess queries, then addUnitTimeSpent upsert. The heartbeat route has no dedicated limiter.
confirmed.breaks_at: 3,000 concurrent learners = 50 heartbeat updates/s + 100 time-beat requests/s, i.e. several hundred queries/s from background pings alone, competing with real work on a 10-connection pool; session table bloat from constant updates.
confirmed.fix: Heartbeat: only write when the stored updated_at is older than ~2-4 min (compare against the cookie-cached session.updatedAt, or keep presence in Redis `SET presence:<user> EX 120` and read 'online now' from SCAN/ZSET), add a limiter (6/min per user). Time beats: batch client-side to 60-120 s, cache the enrollment/membership decision in Redis for ~60 s keyed by (user, course), and combine into one SQL upsert. Add index on session(updated_at) if online-now keeps reading it.
confirmed.flow_risk: Online-now panel (Manager/Admin) becomes slightly less precise (minutes). Tutor progression 'active time' totals must keep the 120 s per-beat cap and enrolled-learner-only rule; staff previewing must still accrue nothing. Cached membership must be invalidated on unenrol or deactivation (resolveActor already reads fresh status so keep that check).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. POST /account/heartbeat (account.ts:114-124) does touchSession, an UPDATE on session.updated_at, per open tab per ~60 s, and has no dedicated limiter. The time beat route (lesson.ts:370-410) runs authMiddleware, the global limiter, unitTimeRateLimit, courseMemberMiddleware, the assertEnrolled queries and an upsert on every beat. This matches the ~33k session writes seen. The arithmetic (3,000 concurrent learners = 50 writes/s plus ~100 beats/s) is plausible but 3,000 concurrent is a high bar; a 10-connection pool handles hundreds of q/s, so medium.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Throttle the write server-side (skip the UPDATE if the cached session.updatedAt is under ~2 min old), keeping 'Online now' within its 5-minute window (must stay <5 min, so use 2 min max). Client-side batching of time beats to 60 s is fine, keeping the 120 s per-beat cap and the LEARNER-only rule. Caching enrollment decisions in Redis adds an invalidation risk (unenrol/deactivation); only do it with a short TTL, and keep resolveActor's fresh status check.

confirmed.title: Concurrent-request races: submission version numbering, mark vs new submission, duplicate pending registrations
confirmed.current: Version = max(version)+1 is computed at presign time and echoed back by the client at create time. The unique constraint (learner, lesson, assessment, version) makes the second of two concurrent submissions fail with 409 'This version already exists - please retry your upload' AFTER both uploaded their files (orphaned objects under the same prefix, no cleanup). A learner can also register version N, skip presign, or replay an old presign. recordResult checks 'latest version' via getLatestSubmissionResultState outside the transaction that inserts the result, so a new version submitted between the check and the insert gets the older version marked (the unique result-per-submission prevents double marking, which is handled with 409). Registration duplicate check (hasOpenRegistrationForEmail then insertRegistration) has no unique index (only idx_registration_org_status_created), so double-clicks or concurrent bots create duplicate pending rows. Allocation create and thread open are race-safe (unique constraint / ON CONFLICT upsert).
confirmed.breaks_at: Under many concurrent learners and flaky mobile networks (double tap, two tabs, retry after timeout) 409s and orphaned uploads become routine; duplicate pending registrations double the manager's queue and the second approval then fails with 'account already exists'.
confirmed.fix: Assign the version server-side at create time inside one statement: `INSERT ... SELECT coalesce(max(version),0)+1 ...` with retry on 23505 (or take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(learner||lesson||assessment))), and make the client send only the uploaded keys plus presign nonce; keep the prefix binding but derive the version from the presign record (store presign version+expiry in Redis). Do the 'is latest' check in recordResult inside the same transaction with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the submission/latest row. Add a partial unique index on registration(organization_id, lower(email)) WHERE status='pending' and map 23505 to the existing neutral 409. Add an S3 lifecycle rule or sweeper for unreferenced coursework/ keys older than 24 h.
confirmed.flow_risk: Learner submission flow (presign then upload then register) must stay backward compatible with the current dashboard client for a deploy window (accept the old version field but validate against server value). Marking flow for tutors/admin: an extra FOR UPDATE can briefly serialise two staff marking the same learner, which is the intended behaviour. Registration index needs a data check for existing duplicate pending rows before applying.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed mechanics, but low impact. getNextSubmissionVersion is read at presign time and the client echoes the version at create time (coursework.ts:~80-172); the unique constraint turns a double submit into a 409 with orphaned S3 objects. createCourseworkSubmission validates the key prefix against the client-supplied version but does not check it equals the next version. Registration duplicate check (registration.ts:~90-110) is check-then-insert with no unique index, so double clicks can create duplicate pending rows; the later approval is already guarded by checkEmailExistsInOrg. A learner can only create duplicate versions of their own work, and orphans are small. The marking race is already safe via the unique result per submission.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Highest value and lowest risk: partial unique index registration(organization_id, lower(email)) WHERE status='pending' (first check for existing duplicate pending rows in prod) and map 23505 to the existing neutral 409. For versions, keep the client-supplied field for backward compatibility and just retry/validate server-side on 23505. Skip the FOR UPDATE in recordResult unless a real double-mark has been observed.

confirmed.title: Per-process state and unbounded logging would break or fill the disk with a second replica or high traffic
confirmed.location: apps/api/src/services/registration/rate-limit.ts:10-29; apps/api/src/routes/dash/stats.ts:276-287; packages/db/src/auth.ts:132-142 (better-auth rateLimit uses default memory storage); apps/api/src/utils/origins.ts:17; apps/api/src/utils/errors.ts:62; apps/api/src/app.ts:94 (hono logger); docker-compose.deploy.yaml (no logging options or resource limits)
confirmed.current: The registration rate limiter is a module-level Map keyed by IP that is never evicted (keys of idle IPs stay with empty arrays) and is not shared across replicas; the admin overview cache is a per-process Map (stale/inconsistent across replicas); better-auth's login/password-reset throttles use in-memory storage (no secondaryStorage), so with 2 replicas the effective limit doubles and restarts reset it. Every request logs a hono access line, every cross-origin request logs `check origin`, and handleError logs the full error object (including DB errors with parameters/PII) for every 4xx as well as 5xx. No json-file log rotation or container memory/CPU limits are configured for api/dashboard/jobs/redis on the 4 GB droplet.
confirmed.breaks_at: Horizontal scaling (second api replica for headroom) silently weakens login/registration throttling and returns different cached admin numbers per request; unbounded Docker json logs fill the droplet disk and a memory-hungry container (download-all, AI streams) can OOM-kill redis or the dashboard because no limits isolate them.
confirmed.fix: Move registration limiting to the Redis limiter (keep the in-memory one as a fallback) and prune empty keys; cache the admin overview in Redis with 60 s TTL; configure better-auth `secondaryStorage` (Redis) for rate-limit storage. Remove `console.log('check origin')`, downgrade 4xx logging in handleError to a one-line summary (no error object), and add compose `logging: { driver: json-file, options: { max-size: '10m', max-file: '3' } }` plus `mem_limit`/`cpus` per service (e.g. api 1.5g, redis 512m with maxmemory).
confirmed.flow_risk: Redis-backed limits must fail open the same way as today (rate-limiter.ts catch). Memory limits that are too tight cause OOM restarts of the api during large zips/AI streams, so size them after fixing download-all. Changing the better-auth rate-limit store affects login throttling for all roles, so test sign-in 429 behaviour.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed but only matters if a second replica is added or disk fills. rate-limit.ts uses a module-level Map that is never pruned of idle keys. Better-auth rateLimit has no secondaryStorage (memory default). The overview cache is per-process. apps/api origins.ts:17 does console.log('check origin') on every cross-origin request, and docker-compose.deploy.yaml has no logging or mem_limit options (grep found none). Docker json-file logs growing unbounded on a small droplet is a realistic ops risk; the in-memory items are not a problem on one replica.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Highest value is cheap: add compose `logging: json-file max-size 10m max-file 3` for all services and remove the origins.ts console.log. Skip the better-auth secondaryStorage and Redis-limiter migration until a second replica is real. Set container mem_limit only after the zip and AI-stream memory is fixed, otherwise OOM kills the api.

confirmed.title: Admin overview loads every submission in the org into Node twice and computes marking stats in JS
confirmed.current: getAdminOverview calls computePipelineForRoster over the whole org roster (admin-overview.ts:155). That runs getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners, which does inArray(learnerId, ALL learner ids) and selects every submission row. Each row joins course, lesson and coursework_result and carries files jsonb, comment and feedback text. All of it is grouped, filtered and sorted in JS. Then for every tutor (line 259) the same function runs again over that tutor's allocated learners, so the allocated slice is loaded a second time, plus getLastSeenForUserIds, getProfileStatusForIds, getCoursesForLearners, getLessonIdsForCourses and getAssessmentItemsByLesson (caseload.ts:368-389). The overview needs only counts, but computePipelineForRoster also builds five full PipelineItem lists that are discarded. It selects columns the stats never use: files, comment and feedback.
confirmed.breaks_at: Roughly 5,000 learners x about 10 units x 1.5 versions is about 75k submission rows (tens of MB of JSON including feedback text), loaded twice on every cache miss and every admin refresh after 60s. That is seconds of CPU on the single event loop of a 2-vCPU box shared with the learner-facing API, plus hundreds of MB transient heap, and the whole thing runs again per tutor. At 20k+ learners it risks OOM or timeouts. The inArray with thousands of uuids also builds a huge bind list. Postgres allows 65,535 bind parameters, and the roster queries fail outright past that.
confirmed.fix: Add a packages/db query layer function getMarkingStatsByScope(orgId) that returns the same TutorPipelineStats fields via SQL. Use DISTINCT ON (learner_id, lesson_id, assessment_key, submission_type) ORDER BY version DESC joined to coursework_result. Compute per group: latest_final_unmarked, latest_draft_unmarked, assessment_passed (bool_or of a verdict that is a pass), prior_refer (bool_or of a final non-pass verdict). Do all counting with FILTER aggregates. Do the org-wide result and the per-tutor result in ONE query: group by tutor via tutor_allocation (GROUPING SETS or a UNION ALL for the org-wide row). Drive due-soon from lesson.documents with jsonb_array_elements filtered to assessment kinds (key, name, dueAt), joined on (lesson_id, key). Take the SLA hours as a bound parameter from resolveMarkingSlaHours. Compute turnaround as avg(extract(epoch from recorded_at - submitted_at)) over verdict rows. Keep computePipelineForRoster only for the tutor's own pipeline page, where the item lists are needed and the roster is small. Add a parity test that feeds the same fixtures to the JS and SQL versions.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin overview, the Marking report and the Tutor performance table are affected. Tutor pipeline and caseload are untouched, so the access rule (tutors see only allocated learners) is unaffected. Edge cases to keep identical: (1) DEACTIVATED learners are excluded from the activity buckets (suspendedLearners) but their submissions still count in the queues. (2) A learner allocated to several tutors appears in each tutor's row but only once in org-wide counts. (3) Legacy rows with assessment_key NULL ('Coursework', no dueAt). (4) isPassingResult is config-driven (PASSING_RESULTS), so pass the list as a parameter instead of hardcoding 'PASS'. (5) dueSoon uses the latest final if present, else the latest draft. (6) The org-wide roster is organizationmember STUDENT, while the per-tutor roster is tutor_allocation with no org filter. Keep both definitions.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. admin-overview.ts:155 runs computePipelineForRoster over the whole org roster. It calls getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners (coursework.ts:252), which selects every submission with files/comment/feedback and a 3-table join, then groups and sorts in JS. It then runs the same function once per tutor via listLearnersForTutor (admin-overview.ts:259), so allocated learners' submissions are loaded again, plus lastSeen, status, programmes, lesson ids and assessment items each time. Five PipelineItem lists are built and discarded. Marked 'critical' is overstated today: it is admin-only and cached 60s, with 7 submissions in prod. It becomes critical only past a few thousand learners. The bind-parameter point (65,535) is correct but only bites past about 65k ids, which is not the near-term risk.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The full SQL rewrite (L effort) is risky. Do a cheap interim step first. (a) Load the org-wide submissions ONCE with a narrow select (no files/comment/feedback) and partition them in memory by a learnerId->tutorIds map built from ONE tutor_allocation query. That removes the per-tutor reload with no semantic change. (b) Add a counts-only mode to computePipelineForRoster that skips item lists and enrichment queries. (c) Only then consider SQL. Semantics to keep: passCount/referCount/totalGraded count EVERY verdict row on every version, not just the latest. overdue is based on latestFinal only. dueSoon uses latestFinal ?? latestDraft. Pass-ness comes from isPassingResult, so pass the PASSING_RESULTS array as a SQL parameter. avgTurnaround uses all verdict rows with d>=0. The per-tutor roster has no org filter and the org roster is STUDENT organizationmembers; preserve both. The tutor-allocation access rule is untouched because only admin/manager paths change. Parity-test the SQL against the JS on fixtures.

confirmed.title: Unbounded Promise.all fan-out (tutors x queries, courses x queries) on a 10-connection pool starves every other request
confirmed.current: One overview request fires 17 concurrent queries. It then fires, per tutor, listLearnersForTutor plus the full pipeline (about 7 queries, one of them the big submissions read). It also fires, per published course, getCourseProgressReport (5 queries). All of these sit in Promise.all with no concurrency cap. The postgres-js pool is max 10 (DATABASE_POOL_MAX default). Connections are the Supabase transaction pooler, and there is an auth_db_connections_absolute advisor warning.
confirmed.breaks_at: With 50 tutors and 20 published courses that is about 17 + 350 + 100 queries queued onto 10 connections. Each cache miss holds the pool for the duration of the slowest chain. Learner logins, resolveActor lookups, uploads and marking requests wait behind it (head-of-line blocking), which shows up as site-wide latency spikes whenever any admin opens the dashboard. The 60s cache only makes spikes periodic, not smaller.
confirmed.fix: Primary fix is finding 'overview-pipeline-in-js' (a constant number of grouped queries per overview, independent of tutor and course count). Until then, cap concurrency: a small p-limit(3) around the per-tutor and per-course maps, and a dedicated low-priority connection (a second postgres client with max 2, used only by dash/report reads) so reports cannot take interactive traffic's connections. Run the report work from the jobs worker and write the result to a snapshot (see 'overview-cache-weak').
confirmed.flow_risk: Only the admin and manager dashboard latency changes. The risk with a dedicated report pool is the total Supabase connection budget: it is pooled via :6543 but still counts towards the pooler client limit across api, jobs and dashboard. Raise per-process max only after checking the Supabase pooler limit. Do not run the report client inside transactions (the pooler is in transaction mode).
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. admin-overview.ts:136-172 fires 17 concurrent calls, one of which is the full pipeline. Lines 238-246 fan out getCourseProgressReport per published course (5 queries each). Lines 259-275 fan out per tutor (listLearnersForTutor plus the ~7-query pipeline). None of it is capped. drizzle.ts creates a single global postgres-js client with max 10 (the code defaults to 5 if the parse fails). postgres-js queues rather than errors, so the result is head-of-line latency for other requests, not failures. Severity is high rather than critical. It is bounded by the 60s cache and by admin-only access, but it is real as tutors and courses grow.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Prefer a small hand-rolled concurrency limiter (chunking, or an in-file semaphore) over a new p-limit dependency. A second 'report' postgres client needs a code change to the drizzle.ts singleton and counts against the Supabase pooler client budget, so do it last, or only after checking the pooler limit. Do not hold a transaction on it. The real fix is the constant-query rewrite from overview-pipeline-in-js and overview-course-completion-n. Add in-flight single-flight so concurrent cache misses share one computation.

confirmed.title: Per-course completion % re-runs a full per-learner progress report for every published course
confirmed.current: For each published course the overview calls getCourseProgressReport(courseId). That runs getOrderedUnitsForCourse, listEnrolledLearnersWithName (joins group, groupmember and user for every enrolled learner), getLatestMarkedResultsForCourse (DISTINCT ON over every final verdict in the course), getCompletionsForCourse and getAssessmentKeysByLesson. It then assembles per-learner rows in JS, only to count rows with completed=true and divide by the row count. The overview already fetches per-course completion counts (getCompletionStats.byCourse) and enrolled counts (getOrgCoursesWithEnrolment).
confirmed.breaks_at: Cost is courses x learners-per-course x verdicts. With 3,000 learners on one course it reads about 30k verdict rows and 3,000 name rows just to produce one integer. Across 20 courses, about 100 queries per overview miss.
confirmed.fix: Replace with one SQL query: completed = count of course_completion rows for the course (already written idempotently by recordCompletionIfComplete and the backfill script) divided by enrolled students. Reuse byCourse from getCompletionStats and enrolled from getOrgCoursesWithEnrolment, so the overview needs zero extra queries. If strict live-rule semantics are wanted instead, compute 'learners whose count of passed non-exempt units equals the total' in one grouped SQL, not a loop per course.
confirmed.flow_risk: The Courses report and the Course overview table change. The number can differ from today's live computation if a course_completion row is missing (course edited after completion, units added, or backfill not run). Edge cases: courses with total=0 non-exempt units are never completable; if a unit is added after completion, the live rule says incomplete but the durable row says complete, so decide which one the dashboard should show and say so in the label. Learner-facing progress is not touched.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. admin-overview.ts:236-246 calls getCourseProgressReport per published course. That runs units, enrolled learners with name, DISTINCT ON of all final verdicts, completions and assessment keys. It then assembles per-learner rows in JS only to count completed rows. Cost grows with courses x learners x verdicts. Medium rather than high: it is cached, admin-only, and the course count is small.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: The proposed swap to course_completion counts is NOT semantically equal. getCompletionStats.byCourse counts course_completion rows with no check that the learner is still an enrolled STUDENT, so unenrolled or removed learners inflate the numerator and the percent can exceed 100. It also reflects the durable rule rather than the live rule. Either join course_completion to groupmember (role 3) for the per-course count, or compute the live rule in one grouped SQL. State clearly in the UI which rule is shown. Cap at 100. Include the exempt-unit rule (isNonGatingUnit) if the live rule is used.

confirmed.title: Overview/report caching is a per-process Map with no stampede protection or invalidation, and the other reports are uncached
confirmed.current: admin-overview is cached in a module-level Map for 60s per org. There is no single-flight: concurrent misses (several admin tabs, or a restart) each run the full computation. The Map is lost on every deploy and not shared across instances. There is no explicit invalidation when a result is recorded, a learner is enrolled or an allocation changes. /reports/learners, /reports/completions, /reports/referrals, /reports/tutor-feedback, /compliance-overview, /stats (getOrganisationAnalytics) and /online-now have no cache at all, so each page view runs full recomputation. Redis is already running and used for the analytics cache (services/analytics/reads.ts) and login activity.
confirmed.breaks_at: With 10 admins/managers each opening 3-4 report pages per session, there are dozens of full aggregations per minute. Each deploy empties the cache and the next 'thundering herd' lands on the box just recovering from a 20-45 min build.
confirmed.fix: Add a small shared helper cachedAggregate(key, ttl, fn) on Redis with: (1) single-flight via SET NX lock or an in-process promise map keyed by org; (2) stale-while-revalidate (serve the last value and refresh in the background); (3) key = org id + report name (+ role if the payload differs); (4) explicit DEL from the few write paths that change the numbers (recordResult/mark, enrol/unenrol, allocation create/delete, registration approve) with a 30-60s TTL as the safety net. Better long term: a BullMQ repeatable job in apps/jobs computes the heavy bundles every 5 min into an admin_report_snapshot(org_id, kind, payload jsonb, computed_at) table and the endpoints just read the row and show computed_at.
confirmed.flow_risk: Admin and manager read paths only. Do not cache anything for tutors or learners with a shared key, since the tutor views are allocation-scoped; keep those per user. Managers see the same org-wide bundle as admins today, but ADMIN-only reports (referrals, tutor-feedback) must keep the role check before the cache read. Snapshots give 'stale by up to N min' semantics: show computed_at in the UI so an admin does not mistake it for live data after marking.
confirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed. stats.ts:277-286 is a module-level Map with a 60s TTL. There is no single-flight (the read/compute/write at 195-199 is non-atomic), no invalidation, and it is lost on restart. /reports/*, /compliance-overview, /stats and the online-now route have no cache. Redis does exist and is already used by services/analytics/reads.ts and the login-activity cache (dash.ts:66-121). Real, but the user impact is modest until the heavy queries get slower. It is a multiplier for the other findings rather than a root cause.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Start with an in-process promise map (single-flight) plus the existing TTL. It is cheap and has zero cross-instance risk (one api container). Add Redis stale-while-revalidate only if the api is ever scaled out. Keep requireAdmin and requireManagerOrAdmin before any cache read. The overview payload is identical for admin and manager, so an org-only key is fine for it. Never share a key for allocation-scoped tutor views. A BullMQ snapshot table is overkill at this stage.

confirmed.title: Learners report rebuilds the entire org progression in memory per page view (duplicate reads per course), and 403s for Managers
confirmed.current: getLearnersReport calls getOrgProgression, which loads all org learners (listOrgLearners, selectDistinct with a full name sort), then getProfileStatusForIds, getLastSeenForUserIds, getEnrolmentsForLearners and getCoursesForLearners with inArray of every learner id. For each target course it runs buildCourseCatalog (getOrderedUnitsForCourse + getAssessmentItemsByLesson), buildCoursePassSet (getLatestMarkedResultsForCourse) and getCourseProgressReport (which calls getOrderedUnitsForCourse and getLatestMarkedResultsForCourse again). The same course-wide DISTINCT ON and unit list are therefore read twice per course. It then returns nothing to the DB for aggregation: every bucket, average and the at-risk list are computed in JS over full rows. Also a correctness bug: the route is requireManagerOrAdmin, but getOrgProgression throws 403 'Admins only' for MANAGER, so Managers cannot load this report.
confirmed.breaks_at: 3,000-10,000 learners: tens of thousands of IDs in 4 inArray queries (each also scanning with no profile_id index on groupmember), plus per course 2 x full verdict scans. Each page view is seconds to tens of seconds of CPU, and each admin refresh repeats it.
