Tutor-allocation visibility (ACCESS.md section 8) is enforced in the api/DB layer, so replicas/LB don't change it. Prices are rough list prices and need confirming.
confirmed.verifier_note: This is a roadmap, not a defect. The current-state description is accurate (one droplet, one replica of everything). Cost numbers are unverified list prices and the thresholds are guesses. It is directionally reasonable, but several 'NOW' items duplicate the findings above. One conflict: suggesting a Cloudflare proxy in front of Caddy contradicts proxy-api-request.ts:128-133, which trusts only Caddy's x-forwarded-for, and auth.ts:120, which keys on x-forwarded-for. Behind Cloudflare, Caddy would need trusted_proxies, or every per-IP limit collapses to Cloudflare IPs or becomes spoofable.
confirmed.fix_adjustment: Treat as advisory. Do not add a CDN or LB until real-client-IP handling is designed. The tutor-allocation rule is enforced in api/DB code and is independent of infrastructure shape.

missed.note: packages/db/src/queries/dash/admin-overview.ts:~383 getOrgMessagingStats: messagesLast7d filters message.created_at with no created_at-leading index (only (thread_id, created_at)), so it seq-scans message; add message(created_at) or drop the org join.

packages/db/src/queries/group/group.ts:44-56 getExistingGroupMembers + :64-89 enrollUsersInCourseGroups: inArray(group ids) AND inArray(profile ids) builds a cross-product lookup and the single multi-row INSERT is unchunked, so a bulk import of ~13k+ memberships hits the 65,535 bind-parameter limit.

apps/api/src/services/comms/announcements.ts:~195: announcement recipients are { userId, emailFields } with no email, so emitNotification's `!recipient.email` check skips the email leg for every announcement. This is either a latent bug or an intended in-app-only behaviour, and it changes the fan-out cost estimate. Needs an owner decision before batching.
apps/api/src/services/caseload/caseload.ts:~120: awaiting.push uses roster.find(...) inside the per-unit loop, which is O(roster x units) in JS for admin org-wide rosters; use a Map built once.

packages/db/src/queries/group/group.ts:25-33 addGroupMembers (and addGroupMember): `return db.insert(...)` inside try/catch without await, so the catch never handles insert errors; failures surface as raw driver errors instead of the wrapped message.

FK cascade/NO ACTION scans on user or profile delete and deactivation: groupmember.profile_id, session.user_id, account.user_id and lesson_completion.profile_id are all unindexed, so deleteSessionsByUserId and any profile delete scan whole tables (only partly noted in the session finding).

apps/dashboard/src/lib/features/app/layout-setup.ts:28 -> apps/api/src/routes/organization/organization.ts:116 (GET /organization/first) -> services/organization.ts:110 getFirstOrganizationWithPlans (queries/organization/organization.ts:~950): in self-hosted mode the root +layout.server.ts calls getOrgSiteInfo on every SSR layout load (including invalidations), and each call runs exactly the three queries seen at about 335k executions in pg_stat_statements (org select, 'select id from organization order by created_at limit 1', organization_plan select). This is the top DB load. Fix: a process-local TTL cache (30-60s) in the dashboard server (or in the API route) keyed on the single org, invalidated on org update. Safe, since the data is read-only per request and the route is already API-key gated.

apps/api/src/app.ts:144 resolveActor (organizationmember+profile) runs on EVERY authenticated request, on top of better-auth getSession and its customSession plugin (packages/db/src/auth.ts:280-296: getUserOrgRolesMap plus a profile status lookup). That is duplicate identity lookups per request, which matches the roughly 90-110k resolveActor counts. Fix: merge or short-TTL-cache (5-10s, busted on role change or deactivation) the actor and orgRoles resolution. Care is needed: deactivation must still take effect immediately (docs say 'next request'), so use a small TTL and explicit invalidation on deactivate/role change.

packages/db/src/schema.ts:113-130: the session table has no index on user_id (only the pk and the token unique). getLastSeenForUserIds, getOnlineOrgMembers, deleteSessionsByUserId and FK cascades all filter by user_id, so they seq-scan a table that grows with every login (and is never shown to be purged of expired rows). Add session(user_id) (and possibly (user_id, updated_at)). This is cheap and additive.

apps/api/src/services/dash/reports.ts:41-43 getLearnersReport asserts MANAGER-or-ADMIN but calls getOrgProgression, which throws 403 'Admins only' for non-ADMIN (progression.ts:~142), so a Manager gets 403 on /reports/learners (routed requireManagerOrAdmin). This is a functional bug that any refactor of this path must not silently change or must explicitly fix.

apps/api/src/services/comms/announcements.ts:194-200: announcement recipients never carry an email, so the 'announcementPublished' email leg in emitNotification is dead code and announcement emails are never sent regardless of preference. That is a correctness gap and means the finding's email-batching premise does not apply today. Decide intentionally before wiring email, since enabling it would re-introduce the 2-3 queries per recipient.

packages/db/src/drizzle.ts:24: a single shared pool with max 10 (default) serves interactive requests, heartbeats and heavy report aggregation alike, so any long Promise.all (overview, progression) causes head-of-line blocking. Besides fixing the queries, consider a bounded concurrency helper for report fan-outs and raising DATABASE_POOL_MAX (Supavisor transaction mode tolerates it) while watching the auth_db_connections advisor warning.

packages/db/src/queries/progress / completion: recordCompletionIfComplete runs isCourseComplete's serial per-unit walk inside the marking transaction (marking.ts runInTransaction), holding a pooled connection and a tx open while ~2N queries execute. Batching the pass check (finding per-unit-roundtrips-progress) is therefore also a lock-time/contention fix on the marking write path, not only a read optimisation.

packages/db/src/queries/coursework/coursework.ts:252-300 getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners uses inArray(learnerId, ids) with no chunking; with a roster beyond about 65k ids it would hit the bind-parameter limit. Not reachable at the stated scale, but a chunking helper should be added when the lean variant is written.

apps/api/src/routes/course/lesson.ts:370-405 plus apps/dashboard/src/lib/features/course/utils/unit-time-heartbeat.ts: the unit-time beat (PUT /:lessonId/time, every ~30s per learner in a lesson) is probably the heaviest steady-state write path. Each beat pays 3 identity queries, two Redis limiters (global plus unitTimeRateLimit), the courseMemberMiddleware query, assertEnrolledStudentContentAccess, and two upserts (unit_time_spent and unit_time_monthly in timespent.ts:33-74). The auditor marked it 'not reviewed'. Raise the cadence to 60s, batch or gate the writes, and cache the enrolment check.

apps/api/src/utils/redis/key-generators.ts:27-30 plus apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/proxy-api-request.ts:~122: extractClientIp trusts client-supplied cf-connecting-ip and x-real-ip first. The dashboard proxy forwards every inbound header verbatim (new Headers(request.headers)), and Caddy does not strip them. Unauthenticated per-IP limits can therefore be bypassed by header spoofing, despite the comment in the proxy saying cf-connecting-ip is not used. Strip those headers in the proxy and derive the IP from Caddy's trusted XFF.

apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/proxy-api-request.ts: all browser API traffic is double-hopped through the single Node dashboard process. It buffers request bodies (await request.arrayBuffer()) and the upstream fetch has no AbortSignal/timeout. The dashboard becomes a throughput ceiling and a SPOF for the API, and a slow API pins dashboard sockets. Consider routing /proxy/* and /api/auth/* from Caddy straight to api:3081 with a prefix strip (checking the OAuth host-rewrite and cookie handling first), or at least add timeouts and stream bodies.

apps/dashboard/src/routes/+layout.server.ts returns the whole App.Locals (user, session, profile, organizations) as root layout data. It is re-serialised into the HTML and every __data.json on each rerun, and likely includes the session token field from better-auth's session object, exposing it to client JS and defeating the HttpOnly cookie. Return only the fields the client uses (user id/name, profile, orgs), and strip session.token.

apps/api/src/app.ts:111-153: resolveActor and getSession are not wrapped separately, so a DB hiccup in resolveActor fails every authenticated request with a 500. Combined with the missing statement_timeout and 10-connection pool, that makes DB slowness an all-user outage, not a degraded mode.

apps/api/src/middlewares/automation-key.ts:11-34: the try/catch wraps await next(), so a downstream throw is mislabelled as 401 UNAUTHORIZED for public-api/automation callers. This is a correctness and observability issue that grows with integration traffic.

apps/api/src/services/registration/decisions.ts:77-123 (approveRegistration): runInTransaction holds a pooled connection while it calls checkEmailExistsInOrg (bare db) and onboardLearner (creates the auth user, enrols, queues the invite email, all on bare db / better-auth, comment at :107 admits its writes are 'outside this tx'). Same nested-pool hold-and-wait deadlock as nested-pool-in-invite-tx plus external work inside a tx; fix by running only the claim in the tx, doing onboardLearner after commit, and reverting the claim to pending on failure (or passing tx through).

apps/api/src/services/cohort/cohort.ts:266: assertStudentCapacityOrThrow (bare db, cloud only) is called inside a per-member db.transaction under Promise.allSettled, so a large cohort add on a cloud build both fans out unbounded transactions and nests a second pool connection inside each. Self-hosted prod returns early at student-limit.ts:63.

apps/api/src/app.ts:140: resolveActor sits outside the getSession try/catch, so any DB error during identity lookup turns every authenticated request into an unhandled 500 (not a retryable 503) and customSession's swallow-and-default behaviour is inconsistent with it.

apps/api/src/services/course/compliance.ts:622 runComplianceExpiryCheck opens one transaction per record serially and loads all ready records into memory; fine today, but should be batched with a LIMIT/cursor before the compliance table grows.

packages/db/src/auth/email-verification.ts (sendChangeEmailConfirmation): `console.log('\nsendChangeEmailConfirmation', options)` also logs the live change-email token URL; the finding only names sendVerificationEmail.

apps/api/src/services/course/compliance.ts:~620-650 (runComplianceExpiryCheck): the `.catch` that swallows a duplicate-key error from createCourseCompletionRecord runs INSIDE db.transaction. Postgres marks the transaction aborted, so the expiredAt and certificate-expired updates are silently rolled back while the counters report success. The record is re-processed on every run.

apps/jobs/src/workers/{emails,notifications,media}.ts worker.on('failed') handlers: `await recordDeadLetterJob(...)` has no try/catch inside an async event handler. A DB error becomes an unhandled rejection, which is only logged by uncaughtException, so a DB blip during a provider outage loses the dead-letter row.

packages/db/src/queries/jobs/dead-letter-job.ts and the emails worker: dead-letter rows persist the full email payload (recipient address, branding HTML, ICS) with no retention job scheduled. This is PII accumulating indefinitely, in addition to the Redis removeOnFail age-only retention.

apps/jobs/src/workers/notifications.ts: the session-reminder-scan is a scheduler job on a concurrency-5 worker, and the manual POST /internal/compliance/send-session-reminders can also enqueue it. Overlapping scans are possible whenever a scan takes longer than 15 min; add a single-flight guard (the ledger insert covers correctness but not load).

apps/jobs/src/processors/emails/send.ts: ZodError from ZSendEmailPayload.parse and template-field validation is retried like a transient failure (5 attempts); bad payloads should be UnrecoverableError and dead-lettered immediately.

packages/db/src/queries/submission/submission.ts:76-90 - getSubmissionsByCourseIdWithDetails does questionAnswers.filter(qa => qa.submissionId === ...) inside submissions.map, which is O(submissions x answers) in memory for every exercise listing. Group by submissionId into a Map.

apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/services/api/index.ts:159-177 - the client timeout is cleared as soon as headers arrive and covers only time-to-headers. After any streaming change, large downloads run without an abort. It also means the retries:1 on 5xx re-issues expensive requests like download-all (a retry-amplification risk worth an opt-out).

apps/api/src/routes/hls/hls.ts:148-162 - GetObject ignores the Range header, and nothing propagates a client abort to the S3 stream, so seeks on large single-file renditions (.mp4/.m4s in HLS_CONTENT_TYPES) re-download the whole object through two Node hops. Verify whether renditions use byte-range playlists.

apps/api/src/app.ts:105-154 - the HLS cookie is minted for any org asset by orgMemberMiddleware without course-enrolment binding, so a de-enrolled or unauthorised org member keeps playback for 15 min per mint. A longer TTL (as the HLS finding proposes) widens this.

docker-compose.deploy.yaml:101 + apps/dashboard proxy - the dashboard Node process streams ALL video bytes (HLS) in addition to SSR. There is no separate pool or limit for media vs page rendering, so heavy playback degrades page loads. Consider routing /proxy/hls past the SvelteKit server at the Caddy level directly to the api.

apps/dashboard/src/routes/+layout.server.ts:32-47 + apps/api/src/services/org/og.ts:37-75 + apps/api/src/services/org/og-cache.ts: the per-navigation warm fetch triggers an API call that does getOrganizationBySiteName + getActiveOrganizationPlan + S3 HeadObject + GetObject on every dashboard navigation. This is a likely source of the 335k org/organization_plan queries and 166k storage.objects lookups. The auditor treated it only as 'outbound socket' cost; it should be the top-priority fix (per-siteName TTL guard in the dashboard plus an in-process etag cache in generateOrgSiteOgImage).

apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/services/auth/session.ts:34-48 (authServerClient.getSession) has no AbortSignal/timeout, unlike classroomio calls (30s). If the API stalls, every SSR request blocks indefinitely inside hooks.server.ts handle(); add a short timeout (3-5s) and fail to logged-out/error rather than hanging all pages.

apps/dashboard/src/hooks.server.ts:112 getSessionData runs before the isPublicRoute check, so public routes (login, landing, health probes, bots) also pay the session round trip; bots/crawlers hitting public pages without cookies are already skipped (getCioCookieString empty), but any request carrying stale cookies is not.

apps/dashboard/src/routes/+layout.svelte:33 console.log('Layout', data) runs in every browser and dumps the entire locals payload (including the session row) to the console; remove together with the locals trimming.

apps/dashboard/src/lib/features/ui/navigation/header-context.svelte:11-17 polls an admin-only endpoint (requireAdmin) every 45s from AppHeader, which is also mounted for non-admin roles in org/[slug]/+layout, producing repeated 403s; gate on admin actor.

docker-compose.deploy.yaml: no json-file log rotation on any service (api, dashboard, jobs, redis, caddy), so the per-request console.log volume can fill the 4 GB droplet disk over time; also no healthcheck or memory limit on the dashboard container.

apps/dashboard/src/routes/(auth)/register/+page.server.ts:45 plus docker-compose.deploy.yaml dashboard env: no ADDRESS_HEADER/XFF_DEPTH is set (repo-wide grep finds none), so SvelteKit adapter-node getClientAddress() returns the TCP peer, i.e. Caddy's docker IP. The registration form forwards that as x-forwarded-for, so hitRegistrationRateLimit (services/registration/rate-limit.ts, 5 per 60 s) is effectively ONE global bucket for all visitors. Legitimate applicants get 409/429 under moderate public traffic. This contradicts the finding's claim that registration is the less exposed limiter. Fix: set ADDRESS_HEADER=x-forwarded-for and XFF_DEPTH=1 on the dashboard container. hooks.server.ts reportToApi has the same wrong ip.

apps/api/src/app.ts:~110-150: the global rateLimiter runs AFTER getSession + resolveActor (organizationmember/profile lookups), so an authenticated flood spends DB queries before being rejected; the 100/min limit does not protect the pool from per-user request storms. Consider a cheap early limiter keyed on the session cookie/IP before resolveActor.

packages/core/src/utils/zip.ts:~18 and apps/api/src/services/caseload/download-all.ts:~40: two files with the same sanitized name in one learner folder collide and JSZip silently overwrites one, so a learner's multiple files can be lost from the archive without any 'skipped' report.
apps/api/src/services/caseload/caseload.ts:~123: `roster.find(...)` inside the per-submission loop is O(roster x awaiting) CPU on the single Node thread; build a Map once.

apps/api/src/services/comms/announcements.ts:~190: recipients are built without an `email` field, so emitNotification's email leg (and the announcement email preference) never runs; announcements are in-app only. Any batching refactor must decide whether to add emails, with attendant send volume (thousands of SMTP sends) and per-org opt-in handling.

apps/api/src/routes/course/presign.ts and other presign routes: unbounded keys arrays and per-key sequential awaits (isUnitUnlocked) can be used for request amplification by any enrolled learner; related to the jsonb finding but also affects the material-download path.

packages/db/src/queries/dash/dash.ts:22-72 + apps/api/src/services/dash.ts: getCourseStats ordering aside, getOrganisationAnalytics (org stats widget shown to all roles on load) is uncached and runs this cross-join query on every call; it is only half-covered by overview-cache-weak.

apps/api/src/services/dash/admin-overview.ts:236-246 and progression.ts:236-243: both call getCourseProgressReport per course in unbounded Promise.all; the same function is invoked once per course per admin page view from two separate pages (overview and learner progressions) with no shared memoisation.

apps/api/src/services/lms/tutor-feedback.ts:19-23 + routes/lms/lms.ts:42: the /lms layout calls the feedback-status endpoint on every learner layout mount and it runs full per-course progress (the N+1) before the cheap milestone check. A single learner count (or a short per-learner TTL cache) would remove the cost from the most frequent learner request; the auditor folded this into progress-n-plus-1 without prioritising it.

packages/db/src/queries/coursework/coursework.ts:252-298: getSubmissionsWithContextForLearners orders by submittedAt DESC with an inArray on all learner ids and has no (learner_id, submitted_at) index. The existing idx_coursework_submission_learner_lesson covers learner_id, but the sort is still done over the whole result.

apps/jobs/src/workers/maintenance.ts: only system_event purge and asset purge are scheduled; there is no scheduled purge of expired better-auth session rows (grep of apps/jobs found none). session grows without bound, and session scans (last-seen, online-now) get slower over time. Not verified whether better-auth cleans up lazily; worth checking row count of expired sessions in prod.

apps/api/src/services/dash/admin-overview.ts:127-155: the overview computes the org last-seen map once (line 168) AND again inside computePipelineForRoster; the same roster-wide lookup could be passed in. A cheap de-duplication that does not need any SQL rewrite.

apps/api/src/app.ts:154 - the rateLimiter middleware is registered AFTER the getSession and resolveActor middleware (app.ts:125-145). Every request, including ones about to be rejected as over-limit, already paid for the session lookup and the organizationmember/profile DB lookups. That matches the 90-110k resolveActor counts and makes the limiter useless against DB-load abuse. Move the IP-keyed limiter before the session and actor resolution, or add a cheap pre-auth limiter.

docker-compose.deploy.yaml:104-107 and docker/Caddyfile - Caddy has no trusted_proxies, no per-IP connection or rate limit and no request timeouts. The dashboard is the only public surface, so there is no edge protection (slowloris and large-body floods) before Node.

docker-compose.deploy.yaml - the dashboard, jobs and caddy services have no healthcheck, and the api healthcheck calls '/', which passes through the same session and rate-limit middleware. The dashboard also has depends_on api: service_healthy but only starts once, so an api restart gives 502s until the api is healthy again with no dashboard-side retry (covered only partially by no-zero-downtime-deploy).

packages/db/src/drizzle.ts:24 - the pool is `postgres()` with max 10 for the api AND 10 for jobs, both on the Supabase transaction pooler, plus six BullMQ workers sharing jobs' 10 connections. With media concurrency 2 and notification fan-out, jobs can starve the same 10-connection pool that its maintenance scheduler needs. No per-query statement timeout is set on the runtime client, so one slow query can hold a pool slot indefinitely.
